title: TIME CRITICAL: cancel the paying customer's Lemon Squeezy subscription before 2026-08-05
description:
ONE active Lemon Squeezy subscription belongs to a real paying customer:

  LS subscription 1676073, customer 7242020 (player b447fded-dff1-4911-8c9c-23535a8031ad)
  Pro Monthly, renews 2026-08-05

If it is not cancelled AT PERIOD END before that date, the customer is billed for another month on the provider we are leaving, while also being asked to subscribe on Polar. Double payment caused by our own migration.

Cancel at period end, NOT immediately — immediate cancellation would strip access already paid for.

The other two active subscriptions (2955982 monthly, 2829245 annual) are the owner's and their spouse's own accounts on 100% discount codes. No money is involved, so no urgency and no double-charge risk; handle them at leisure. Their membership_status stays 'pro' after cutover regardless, since nothing revokes it.

Owner action in the Lemon Squeezy dashboard; no code involved.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: subscription 1676073 is set to cancel at period end, confirmed in the Lemon Squeezy dashboard, before 2026-08-05.
notes:

For comparison, the owner's own annual (370720) reports status=cancelled, cancelled=true, ends_at=2027-05-17 after being cancelled at period end, so the API representation is unambiguous and this one has genuinely not been cancelled.

Owner believed this was complete; it is not. Renewal is 2026-08-05, so the window is roughly two days. If it lapses the customer is charged for another month on the provider we have already left, while being asked to subscribe on Polar.

Cancel AT PERIOD END, not immediately. Re-verify afterwards with:

Re-verified via GET /v1/subscriptions/1676073: status=cancelled, cancelled=true, ends_at=2026-08-05T10:00:00Z, matching the period-end shape of the owner's own annual (370720). title: Server actions in me/actions.ts perform privileged writes without authorization
description:
src/app/me/actions.ts starts with 'use server', so every export is a Next.js Server Action — a public HTTP endpoint. Confirmed against .next/server/server-reference-manifest.json: all 21 registered action ids carry the action-browser layer, and 12 are reachable from the webhook route's module graph.

processWebhookEvent and storeWebhookEvent are among them. They accept a caller-supplied event argument, use createAdminClient (service role, bypasses RLS), write player_customer.membership_status, and invoke handle_upgrade_team_invites — with no session or authorization check. Sibling actions in the same file (createTeam) do call getSession and throw Unauthorized, so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate.

Next.js guidance is explicit that Server Actions are public endpoints and must verify authorization themselves; reachability of an action id is not a security boundary.

Present in production today under the Lemon Squeezy integration — not introduced by the Polar migration.

FIX IN PROGRESS: wordle-teams-c6v moves both functions into src/lib/polar/webhook.ts, a module without the 'use server' directive, so they stop being actions at all. That closes this specific path.

STILL TO AUDIT after that: the remaining exports of me/actions.ts. getCheckoutUrl(user: User) takes a caller-supplied User rather than deriving it from the session, which is the same class of problem at lower severity.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: no export of a 'use server' module performs a privileged write without deriving identity from the session, and getCheckoutUrl derives the player from the session rather than a caller-supplied argument.
notes:
FULLY FIXED as of ymy. getCheckoutUrl now takes NO arguments and derives the player from the session via getUserFromSession, as does the new getBillingPortalUrl; both live in src/lib/polar/actions.ts. The previous getCheckoutUrl(user: User) accepted caller-supplied identity on what Next.js treats as a public HTTP endpoint.

Registered server actions across the three commits: 21 (12 reachable from the webhook route) -> 19 -> 16. The reduction comes from deleting the two webhook handlers and the duplicate getCheckoutUrl copies.

Verified: 14 assertions covering both actions rejecting unauthenticated callers WITHOUT calling Polar at all, using the session id and email rather than any argument, and — asserted directly — having an arity of zero, so no caller-supplied identity is even expressible.
close_reason: Both webhook handlers and both billing actions no longer accept caller-supplied identity; action count 21 -> 16

title: Polar P2e: DB migration - auth hook, drop columns, webhook idempotency
description:
One migration file. THE INTERNAL ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING:

  1. create or replace public.custom_access_token_hook FIRST, dropping the user_customer_id and user_member_variant claims
  2. THEN alter table public.player_customer drop column customer_id, drop column membership_variant
  3. create unique index webhook_events_webhook_id_key on public.webhook_events (webhook_id)

If the columns are dropped while the old hook still selects them, custom_access_token_hook throws and EVERY LOGIN BREAKS. This project already has a login-lockout incident (wordle-teams-jvt) in its history. Base the new hook on supabase/migrations/20240325200437_add_customerid_back_into_auth_hook.sql, keeping user_member_status / user_first_name / user_last_name and removing the other two.

Then regenerate src/lib/database.types.ts via npm run gen-types.

P0 because this is the single riskiest step in the migration.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: migration applies cleanly on dev, login still works on dev afterward, player_customer has only (id, player_id, membership_status), and a duplicate webhook_id insert is rejected by the unique index.
notes:
Done. supabase/migrations/20260731120000_polar_migration_drop_lemonsqueezy_columns.sql, verified against a real local Postgres (not just written).

FOUND DURING VERIFICATION — webhook_id was uuid, not text. The spec and this issue both claimed it was already text and needed no change. It was uuid, because Lemon Squeezy's meta.webhook_id happened to be one and database.types.ts renders uuid as string, which hid it. Standard Webhooks explicitly does NOT require a UUID — the spec's own example id is msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W, which a uuid cast rejects. Left alone, the first non-UUID id from Polar would throw on insert, return 500, and put Polar into an infinite retry loop against an event that could never be stored. The migration now converts the column to text. Spec corrected; c6v updated.

SCOPE MOVED: gen-types moved to ymy. Regenerating database.types.ts here would break typecheck in utils.ts:107-108, me/page.tsx:41, and app-bar-server.tsx:31-33, which is ymy's type-ripple scope. This migration touches no TypeScript, so the repo stays green.

OTHER DECISIONS: unique index is PARTIAL (where webhook_id is not null) so legacy null rows stay exempt. Dedupe before indexing orders by processed desc, id asc, so a retry set containing one processed and one failed row keeps the processed one. 'immutable' volatility on the hook was deliberately preserved to keep this migration to one concern — filed separately as wordle-teams-wau.

VERIFIED LOCALLY (supabase db reset, then psql): player_customer is exactly (id, player_id, membership_status); both columns gone; no remaining function or RLS policy references either; the hook INVOKES without throwing for both an unknown user and a real pro player, returning the three expected claims — this is the login-safety proof; webhook_id is text; the partial unique index exists; a non-UUID Standard Webhooks id inserts fine; a duplicate raises a unique violation; two null webhook_ids are both allowed; member_status enum unchanged.
close_reason: Migration written and verified against a local Postgres; caught and fixed a uuid/text column bug that would have broken the webhook pipeline

title: P0: /login is completely unusable for anyone blocking lemonsqueezy.com — infinite error loop locks the page
description:
REPRODUCED AGAINST PRODUCTION 2026-07-30. If app.lemonsqueezy.com fails to load, the login page enters an infinite error loop, pegs the main thread, never renders, and the tab eventually crashes. Affected users cannot sign in or sign up AT ALL.

MEASURED (headless Chromium, prod https://wordleteams.com/login, fresh profile):
 - normal load: renders fine, createLemonSqueezy defined, 0 errors
 - lemon.js request aborted: 998 'createLemonSqueezy is not a function' errors within the first 500ms;
 document.body.innerText() times out after 3s (main thread locked);
 page never renders the sign-in UI; tab crashes shortly after
 - lemon.js delayed 0.5/1.5/3s: 0 errors, renders fine

So the trigger is FAILURE TO LOAD, not slowness. beforeInteractive defers hydration until the script resolves, so a slow network is safe; an aborted/blocked request is not.

THE LOOP (all four links confirmed in code):
 1. src/components/app-bar/app-bar-base.tsx:34-35 — useEffect calls window.createLemonSqueezy() unguarded, as its FIRST statement.
 2. src/app/login/layout.tsx renders <Welcome />, and src/components/welcome.tsx:21 renders <AppBar />. So AppBar lives in the LAYOUT of the /login segment.
 3. Next.js error.tsx does not catch errors thrown by the layout of its own segment, so src/app/login/error.tsx cannot catch it. There is no src/app/error.tsx. It bubbles all the way to src/app/global-error.tsx.
 4. src/app/global-error.tsx:15 renders <AppBar /> — the same component that just threw. It throws again. Loop.

SENTRY: issue 6834987895, 3380 events / 11 users, first seen 2025-08-25, still firing 2026-07-26. Sampled transactions: /login 447, /home 63, / 3, /terms 1 — never /me. ~63 events per session is the loop signature.

WHO IS BLOCKED: app.lemonsqueezy.com is a payments/tracking domain blocked by uBlock Origin + EasyPrivacy, Brave Shields, Safari content blockers, Pi-hole/NextDNS, and corporate/school DNS filtering. Note the churn data in wordle-teams-456: a large share of never-activated accounts are on school and corporate domains (multiple k12/university and enterprise domains) — exactly the networks most likely to filter that domain.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the failure is 100% client-side, so Vercel/Axiom logs show nothing — which is why the earlier log-only pass found 163 visitors reaching /login with only ~12 completing auth and zero server errors. Sentry's 11-user count is an undercount: the /monitoring tunnel drops ~11% of events (306x 400, 87x 429), and an ad-blocker that blocks lemonsqueezy will usually block the Sentry tunnel too — the users most affected are the least able to report it.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Guard the call: if (typeof window.createLemonSqueezy === 'function') before invoking, and move the LemonSqueezy Setup into its own useEffect so a failure cannot block the PWA and time-zone logic that follow it in the same effect. 2) Move the <Script> out of the component into the root layout, or load it lazily only where checkout is actually used. 3) Remove <AppBar /> from src/app/global-error.tsx so the error fallback can never re-trigger the error it is displaying. 4) Add src/app/error.tsx so page-level errors stop escalating to global-error. 5) Re-run scripts/repro-login.mjs with lemon.js blocked and confirm the sign-in UI renders with 0 errors.
notes: SHIPPED TO PRODUCTION 2026-07-30. Merged dev (aeb3c00) then main (762cbda); Vercel production deploy Ready. Verified against live https://wordleteams.com/login with the regression script: lemon.js allowed PASS, lemon.js BLOCKED PASS (0 errors, page responsive, sign-in UI rendered). Was 998 errors in 500ms with an unresponsive page. Next: watch Sentry issue 6834987895 for new events — it should go quiet — then re-measure the login funnel in wordle-teams-390.
close_reason: Fixed in a5d91f1 on branch fix/login-lemonsqueezy-lockout. Verified on a local production build: with lemon.js blocked, 0 createLemonSqueezy errors and the sign-in UI renders (was 998 errors in 500ms with the page unresponsive). All 5 acceptance criteria met: guarded call driven by Script onReady, strategy corrected to afterInteractive, setup split out of the mount effect, AppBar removed from global-error.tsx, src/app/error.tsx added. Regression check at scripts/repro-login-lockout.mjs. Still needs a production deploy before the funnel can be re-measured.

title: Nothing in the Phase 5 plan sets the POLAR_* env vars on the Convex deployment - and there are five, not four
description:
Found while building Task 9 (wordle-teams-l1v).

The spec's operational note and every plan task name four variables: POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET, POLAR_PRO_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID, POLAR_PRO_ANNUAL_PRODUCT_ID. NO TASK IN THE PLAN ACTUALLY SETS THEM on any Convex deployment; Task 13's sandbox pass assumes they are already there.

There are now FIVE. v1's client.ts picked the Polar server with ENVIRONMENT === 'prod' ? 'production' : 'sandbox'. v2 HAS NO SUCH VARIABLE IN CONVEX - the only ENVIRONMENT in the tree is wrangler.jsonc's, set on the Cloudflare worker that serves the front end, invisible to a Convex function. So convex/polar.ts requires POLAR_SERVER, validated in the same set as the other four and checked to be exactly 'production' or 'sandbox' (v1's ternary silently defaulted anything unrecognised to sandbox, so a typo would send real subscribers to an instance holding none of their data).

Polar's sandbox is a wholly separate instance from production - separate accounts, organizations, products and tokens - so server and credentials must move together. Phase 5 verifies on sandbox against beta (decision C); the SAME deployment flips to production at cutover by changing POLAR_SERVER plus the token and both product ids together.

NO VALUES IN THIS REPO OR IN BEADS - this repo is public. Names only.

DONE WHEN: all five are set on the deployment beta runs on, before Task 13's sandbox pass, and the cutover checklist names all five as a set that moves together.
notes:
PARTIALLY VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-27, after the owner set the five vars on the PROD Convex deployment (which beta uses).

PROBED THE DEPLOYED ENDPOINT: https://fabulous-goldfish-949.convex.site/polar/webhook
(Convex serves httpActions on .convex.site, NOT .convex.cloud - that is the URL to register in Polar.)

  POST, no webhook-id header  -> 400
  POST, bogus signature       -> 403, body 'Invalid signature'

THE 400 IS THE PROOF. convex/http.ts checks POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET at :121, BEFORE the webhook-id header at :144. With the secret missing that request returned 500; it now returns 400. So POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set on the deployment AND is reaching the code. The 403 confirms the standardwebhooks verifier is live and rejects an unsigned request without leaking anything.

THE OTHER FOUR ARE NOT YET VERIFIED, and deliberately were not: POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_PRO_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID, POLAR_PRO_ANNUAL_PRODUCT_ID and POLAR_SERVER are read only by assertPolarEnv on the ACTION paths (checkout, portal, the checkout fallback), and every one of those requires either an authenticated session or a validly signed delivery. Listing them would mean extracting a production deploy key into a temp file; the marginal value did not justify it.

THAT IS SAFE BY DESIGN. assertPolarEnv validates ALL FIVE TOGETHER and throws naming every missing one, so the FIRST checkout or portal click in the sandbox pass is a complete test of the remaining four and fails loudly rather than silently. That was the point of validating them as a set rather than one per call site.

POLAR_SERVER must be exactly 'production' or 'sandbox' - it is NOT a ternary with a default, precisely so a typo cannot silently resolve to sandbox. For the sandbox pass it must be 'sandbox', and it must move to 'production' at cutover together with the credentials, since Polar's sandbox is a separate instance with its own accounts, products and tokens.

title: getCustomerPortalUrl resolves in one namespace; a migrated subscriber gets 'no-customer'
description:
Found while building Task 9 (wordle-teams-l1v). NOT a defect ported from v1 - v1 had only one namespace.

convex/polar.ts's getCustomerPortalUrl calls customerSessions.create({ externalCustomerId: <convex player id> }). Inbound identity resolves across BOTH namespaces (decision F, resolvePlayerIdFor: Convex id then by_legacyId), because after cutover a migrated subscriber's Polar customer carries their v1 uuid as external_id - v1's checkout.ts:22 set it to the v1 player id. The OUTBOUND direction does not.

CONSEQUENCE: between cutover and that subscriber's next subscription webhook, the portal answers { url: null, reason: 'no-customer' } to a PAYING subscriber - the exact 'say something untrue' failure the three-way result exists to prevent. repairCustomerExternalId closes it, but only on their next event, which for an annual plan can be months away.

OPTIONS: (a) on no-customer, retry once with player.legacyId when present, and schedule repairCustomerExternalId on success; (b) a pre-cutover backfill over the Polar API stamping Convex ids onto every migrated customer - which spec decision F rules out as a SOLE mechanism, but not as a supplement; (c) accept and make the UI copy honest.

NOT DONE IN TASK 9 deliberately: it is a second Polar call plus a change to which identities the portal accepts, which is a design question rather than a port. The gap is written into getCustomerPortalUrl's doc comment, which cites this issue id.

DONE WHEN: a migrated subscriber whose Polar customer still holds a v1 uuid can open the portal, or the phase records a decision not to and the UI copy says something true.
notes:
FIXED in the follow-up to Task 9. Option (a), as suggested by the coordinator.

WHY IT WAS NOT A NEW DECISION: decision F already establishes 'accept both namespaces'. Only the inbound direction had been written down; the portal resolving one was an inconsistency, not an open question.

WHAT SHIPPED, in convex/polar.ts:
- checkoutIdentity now also returns legacyId (null for a v2-native player).
- externalIdsFor({ playerId, legacyId }) -> the ordered names to try. Convex id first, v1 uuid second, empties and duplicates dropped. A player with NO legacyId gets a one-element list, so nobody who signed up after cutover pays for a second call, and the cost decays to zero as customers heal.
- lookupPortal(candidates, attempt) walks them. ONLY no-customer advances: a 500 or an auth failure stops the walk and stays an error, because retrying it as the next identity would report an outage as 'you have no subscription' - to everyone, not just migrated users. Exhausting every identity is still no-customer, which stays truthful for the genuinely new user.
- getCustomerPortalUrl wires the two and, when the winning identity was NOT the Convex id, schedules repairCustomerExternalId with the customer id the session returned (CustomerSession.customerId). Fire-and-forget via ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, ...), wrapped, so tidying up can never take away a session the player is entitled to. The portal is now the FIRST live caller of repairCustomerExternalId; the webhook's is still Task 10.

TESTABILITY: the attempt is an injected parameter, so the sequencing is real logic under test rather than a stub-and-assert-called test. 11 new tests (524 -> 535). Mutation-checked: dropping the legacy fallback and letting any failure advance the walk each turn tests red.

NOT TESTED: the SDK calls themselves and the scheduler wiring - network and ctx. Covered by Task 13's sandbox pass, whose checklist item 'a non-subscriber is told they have no billing account' should gain a sibling: a MIGRATED subscriber can open the portal.

Comments corrected that this made false: assertPolarEnv's list of what is unit tested (written in the previous commit), the portal's 'resolved by the Convex id' line, repairCustomerExternalId's 'nothing calls this yet', the module docblock's 'the single exception is checkoutIdentity', and polarIdentity.ts's customerId note.
close_reason: Closed

title: The db.delete site inventories are stale — 14 hits is now 21, and downgradeTeamRemovalFor is a new path in
description:
Filed by Task 7 (wordle-teams-stf), which was told to REPORT this rather than fix it. Parent is wt-ksh.6 (Phase 5) — link it with `bd dep`, since --parent could not mint a child id under that prefix.

Two documents enumerate v2's delete sites and both are now wrong.

1. wt-ksh.9's runbook, step 2, the 'players, playerMembership' bullet. It says: git grep -n "db\.delete(" convex/ printed FOURTEEN hits on 2026-08-25, and only three matter (winners.ts, scores.ts, teams.ts), the rest being testOtps.ts (three), migrate.ts and four *.test.ts files.

MEASURED 2026-08-26, same command, same directory: TWENTY-ONE hits. The breakdown is teams.ts 4, e2ePrune.ts 4, testOtps.ts 3, teams.test.ts 2, e2ePrune.test.ts 2, and one each in migrate.ts, scores.ts, winners.ts, access.test.ts, scores.test.ts, winners.test.ts.

The drift is NOT Task 7's. convex/billing.ts contains no db.delete call at all; it reaches deletion only through cascadeDeleteTeam. The seven extra hits are e2ePrune.ts and e2ePrune.test.ts, which landed with the e2e prune (wordle-teams-1cd) after the runbook line was written. So the runbook has been stale since before Phase 5 started, and an operator following it at cutover would find seven hits the text does not account for and no way to tell which are new.

2. Same runbook, the 'teams. STOP AND READ.' bullet. It names cascadeDeleteTeam's reachable callers as 'the creator deletes a team, or the last member leaves one'. There are now four: deleteTeamFor, leaveTeamFor's last-member case, e2ePrune.ts, and since Phase 5 billing.ts's downgradeTeamRemovalFor. It also still says 'creator', which the Phase 5 rename made a stale field name.

The downgrade one matters at cutover for a reason the others do not: a team it deletes carries a legacyId, so a later copy re-inserts it — exactly the resurrection wt-ksh.13.10 describes — and it is triggered by a Polar webhook rather than by a person, so it can fire during a dual-running window with nobody watching.

3. scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs:286 says 'Confirmed for teams (cascadeDeleteTeam, convex/teams.ts) and for boards (upsertBoardFor, convex/scores.ts)'. This one is arguably still TRUE as written — it names the deleting function, not its callers, and cascadeDeleteTeam is still the function. Check it rather than assuming it needs an edit.

DONE WHEN: the runbook's hit count is a measured number with a dated command beside it, its caller list for cascadeDeleteTeam names all four, the 'creator' wording is gone, and copy-tallies.mjs has been read and either updated or explicitly confirmed accurate.

title: Local Convex backend silently refused every push after the creator->owner rename
description:
FOUND 2026-08-26 while working wordle-teams-1cd. RESOLVED during that work, filed so the failure mode is recorded.

The local anonymous backend rejected EVERY 'convex dev' push from the moment the creator->owner rename landed until 2026-08-26 16:56. 47 consecutive failures in the watcher log, all identical:

  Schema validation failed. Document ... in table 'teams' does not match the schema:
  Object contains extra field 'creator' that is not in the validator.

1348 of 1680 local teams still carried the dropped 'creator' field, and none of them had 'owner' set. Convex validates the schema against every existing document on push and refuses a narrowing any row violates, so one stale field froze the whole deployment.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: the watcher process stayed alive and kept retrying, codegen kept succeeding (api.d.ts is only rewritten when the API SHAPE changes, and it did not), and the vite dev server kept serving current frontend code. So tsc, vitest and build were all green while the backend served pre-rename functions. Nothing in the quality gates looks at what is actually deployed locally - the same blind spot recorded for e2e.

The runbook step existed and was run on beta (see the Task 2b closure) but was never run against local, and migrate.clearTeamCreator refuses a team with creator and no owner, so it needed migrate.backfillTeamOwner first. Both were still deployed in the stale code; running backfillTeamOwner then clearTeamCreator (1348 rows each) unblocked the push immediately.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH CONSIDERING: a cheap check that the local deployment's function set matches the working tree, so 'the backend is running code from four days ago' cannot be invisible again.
notes:
TITLE CORRECTED: said '4 days', but the description is right - pushes failed from the moment the rename's schema drop landed (2247b25, 2026-08-26) until 16:56 the same day. The 4-day figure was the watcher's uptime, not the outage.

THIS IS THE EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION OF A DESIGN PREMISE THAT WAS UNVERIFIED WHEN THE PHASE 5 PLAN WAS WRITTEN. The five-step rename (add owner / backfill / switch readers / clear creator / drop creator) was designed around the belief that Convex rejects a schema push when existing documents carry a field the schema no longer declares. That could not be tested locally at design time - validation happens server-side, not in the installed package - so the safe ordering was adopted on the grounds that it is correct under either reading.

It is now MEASURED, and the belief was right:
  Schema validation failed. Document ... in table 'teams' does not match the schema:
  Object contains extra field 'creator' that is not in the validator.

Had the rename been done in fewer steps, the Task 2c deploy would have failed against BETA exactly as it failed locally. Beta survived only because steps 2 and 4 (backfill, then clear) were run against it. The local backend never had them run - that is the entire difference, and it is why local broke while beta did not.

THE REAL LESSON, and it is bigger than this bug: lint, typecheck, vitest and build were ALL GREEN throughout, because none of them talks to the backend. convex-test builds its own schema in memory. So a deployment can be frozen for an arbitrary period while every gate reports success. The only signal was e2e, which is not in the gates.

title: Task 3: widen playerMembership.legacyId and webhookEvents.legacyId to optional
description:
Phase 5. See Task 3 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-v2-phase5-polar.md.

BLOCKS EVERY NATIVE WRITE IN THIS PHASE. playerMembership.legacyId is v.string() and webhookEvents.legacyId is v.number(), both REQUIRED (schema.ts:228,236). They are the only two required legacyId fields left - players, teams, dailyScores and monthlyWinners were each made optional exactly when their phase began writing natively.

Phase 5 is the first phase to WRITE either table, so neither can be written today. None of the ten provisional children mentioned this.

Both are WIDENING changes, so no backfill and one push.

ALSO: players.ts:53-55 justifies omitting a 'new' membership row by saying playerMembership.legacyId is a required string. That reason expires here. Rewrite it to the real reason - isProFor already reads a MISSING row as not-pro, which is what 'new' meant.

DONE WHEN: a convex-test inserts both a playerMembership and a webhookEvents row with no legacyId; gates green.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-26. Commits 0759e39 (widening + test), 33c4a9d, c6bce6a, 8ff2e97 (comment accuracy).

MEASURED BY THE CONTROLLER INDEPENDENTLY, from v2/, by exit code: lint 0, typecheck 0, test:once 0 (419 passed / 27 files), build 0.

Both fields independently pinned: reverting either one alone reddens the test, verified by a reviewer in a scratch tree.

FOUR COMMENT DEFECTS FOUND ACROSS THREE REVIEW ROUNDS. Two were the PLAN's errors, not the implementer's:
- 'the rows that DO carry a legacyId are the copied Lemon Squeezy ones' came verbatim from the plan and is FALSE: v1 migrated to Polar in place on 2026-08-03, the copy filters by neither provider nor date, so copied rows include v1's own Polar events.
- The filter rationale was built on a parallel-run collision at the controller's prompting, omitting the reason provable today: copied rows with a null Postgres webhook_id all arrive as webhookId undefined, so the by_webhookId range returns ALL of them and .unique() would throw. The legacyId filter is what reduces it to one row.

CORRECTION TO THE CONTROLLER, VERIFIED: webhook_id was NOT added by the Polar migration. 20240323195151 added it 2024-03-23 as a nullable UUID; 20260731120000 only retyped it to text. So rows lacking one predate 2024-03-23 - a Lemon Squeezy row from after that date holds a uuid. There is a real 4-day window (table created 2024-03-19).

PROCESS FAILURE WORTH REMEMBERING: one gate round ran from the REPO ROOT, not v2/, and each gate was piped through 'tail -3' so the && chain read tail's exit status. All four printed OK while typecheck and test:once did not exist and the build failed. Self-caught and re-run. Always set -o pipefail and echo the real exit code.
close_reason: Closed

title: Task 2: switch every reader to teams.owner (rename 3/5)
description:
Phase 5, deploy step 3 of 5. See Task 2 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-v2-phase5-polar.md.

Switch all 311 refs to owner: isCreator->isOwner, requireTeamCreatorFor->requireTeamOwnerFor, NOT_TEAM_CREATOR->NOT_TEAM_OWNER, CREATOR_NOT_REMOVABLE->OWNER_NOT_REMOVABLE. migrate.ts line 323 is the ONLY write-side change there; the arg name creatorLegacyId STAYS because it names v1's column on the wire.

DO NOT TOUCH scripts/*.mjs. Its 3 refs name v1's Postgres column.

title: Task 10: the webhook endpoint - verify, store, process, retry on failure
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. Port src/lib/polar/webhook.ts into a Convex httpAction registered in convex/http.ts (which today only registers Better Auth routes).

THE ORDER MATTERS AND IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: verify the Standard Webhooks signature -> resolve the player (Task 4) -> STORE the event -> process it -> return. A failure AFTER storing must return non-2xx so Polar retries. Anything that auto-acknowledges before the handler resolves destroys this - see Task 0.

IDEMPOTENCY KEYS ON A STRING FROM THE HEADER. Polar follows Standard Webhooks; ids look like msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W. Read it from the webhook-id HEADER, not the body. v1 lost a day to a uuid column that rejected them, returned 500, and put Polar into an infinite retry loop against an event that could never be stored. The v2 schema comment on webhookEvents already says all of this.

CONVEX HAS NO UNIQUE CONSTRAINTS, so the replay guard is an explicit by_webhookId lookup at the top of the mutation, returning early if the row exists. v1 got this free from a partial unique index; v2 does not.

FOUR OUTCOMES, all distinct, following v1's WebhookOutcome:
  processed  - stored and applied
  duplicate  - already handled; return 2xx WITHOUT reprocessing
  ignored    - accepted but not actionable and retrying will never help (unknown player)
  failed     - return non-2xx so Polar retries

Recognised-but-inert events (canceled, past_due) still STORE the row for the audit trail and still return processed; they simply apply no transition.

Mark the row processed after the membership change succeeds or fails on its own terms - and do NOT make marking-processed fatal, or a 500 there makes Polar redeliver an event that was in fact applied.

DONE WHEN: a duplicate webhook-id returns success without reprocessing (parent acceptance criterion 3); an unknown player is ignored rather than retried forever; a mid-processing failure returns non-2xx; a bad signature is rejected before any write; and all of it is pinned by convex-test.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-27. Commits 5c949d0 + a35e035 + 968a3dd. 566 tests / 35 files; four gates exit 0. ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 3 PINNED, BOTH HALVES.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERED MOST IN THE PHASE: @polar-sh/sdk's validateEvent CANNOT RUN ON CONVEX'S DEFAULT RUNTIME. dist/esm/webhooks.js:126 calls Buffer.from(secret,'utf-8'); Buffer is a Node global the default runtime does not provide. EVERY DELIVERY WOULD HAVE FAILED VERIFICATION.

NO GATE IN THIS REPO COULD SEE IT. vitest's edge-runtime environment DOES define Buffer, and npx convex codegen analyses modules without serving a request. lint/typecheck/test/build were all green over code that could not process a single real delivery. Only issuing a live request found it.

Fixed by verifying through standardwebhooks@1.0.0 directly - the library the SDK itself verifies through - which never calls the Buffer global. BYTE-IDENTITY PROVEN, not assumed: the reviewer traced both key derivations to source (SDK: base64.decode(base64(utf8(secret))) == utf8(secret); shipped: TextEncoder().encode(secret) == utf8(secret)) and then signed a delivery under the SDK-DERIVED key and verified it under the SHIPPED key, across 8 secrets including non-ASCII, CJK and emoji. That cross-test is the operation real Polar bytes perform.

The latin-1 trap was avoided: passing the STRING with format:'raw' takes Uint8Array.from(s, c => c.charCodeAt(0)), which diverges on any non-ASCII secret.

CONSEQUENCE: a verified delivery is the RAW WIRE JSON, so polarIdentity.ts reads customer.external_id / customer_id / checkout_id. metadata.player_id is unchanged, being our own key. Decision F is untouched; only the field names in the spec were wrong, and the spec now carries the correction.

SECOND BUG, FOUND IN REVIEW: a transient failure of the checkout fallback became a permanent unretryable 202. fetchCheckoutExternalId caught EVERYTHING - Polar 5xx, 429, network, assertPolarEnv's throw - and returned null, which fell to the 202 path. 202 tells Polar never to redeliver AND stores no audit row, so the delivery vanished. It bit exactly the shape the fallback exists for, and a deployment with the webhook secret set but POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN missing would silently drop those upgrades. Now isMissingCheckout returns true only for 404/422 (the two client errors checkoutsGet declares, measured at dist/esm/funcs/checkoutsGet.js:87); everything else rethrows and answers 500.

MUTATION VERDICTS (exit codes): restore-the-swallow 1 | guard-on-row-existence 1 (exactly one test, the divergence-13 one; the duplicate test correctly stays green) | canceled-as-revoked 1 (4 tests) | sanity 0.

convex/http.test.ts now drives the whole protocol through t.fetch with REAL Standard Webhooks signatures - 500 no secret, 400 no webhook-id, 403 bad signature, 403 body swapped after signing, 202 nobody, 500 fallback unaskable, 200 across all three identity namespaces, redelivery changing nothing, canceled inert.

PROCESS FAILURE WORTH REMEMBERING: the first mutation run reported a FALSE PASS because git stash create captures only TRACKED files, so the new http.test.ts was absent from all four extractions (34 files/553 tests instead of 35/566). Saved as a memory: git add before extracting, and assert the extraction's test count matches the live tree's before trusting any verdict.

title: Task 5: identity - candidate extraction + dual-namespace resolution
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. Port src/lib/polar/identity.ts. THIS IS A CUTOVER PREREQUISITE, NOT HARDENING.

THE BUG IT EXISTS FOR: Polar does NOT reliably stamp external_customer_id onto a customer. When a checkout matches an EXISTING customer by email, the value stays on the checkout and the customer keeps its own null external id. The webhook is delivered, logged succeeded=true http=202, and NOBODY IS UPGRADED. Silent, because 202 is not an error. Observed on dev 2026-08-03 against a real subscription.

WORSE IN V2 THAN IN V1: at cutover every migrated user already exists as a Polar customer under their email - which is exactly the failing case. Every single upgrade would hit it.

RESOLVE IN THREE STEPS, cheapest first:
  1. customer.externalId                      - the happy path, no API call
  2. metadata.player_id from the checkout      - we set it ourselves, no API call
  3. checkouts.get(checkoutId).externalCustomerId - one API call, last resort
Then REPAIR: stamp the id onto the Polar customer so later events for the same person take path 1. Best-effort, never awaited by the caller, never fatal - failing to tidy up must not turn a successful webhook into a retry.

v1 validates the resolved value against a UUID regex before trusting it. In v2 the external id is the player's Convex id, which is NOT a uuid - decide what the validation becomes and state it. Do not simply drop the check.

Needs network, so this is a Convex ACTION, not a mutation.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 2 OF THE PARENT LANDS HERE, and the design requires it be pinned by a UNIT TEST before any sandbox run: customer.externalId null + metadata.player_id present -> resolution succeeds. The owner chose to build everything before verifying, so this test is what stops the identity bug surfacing late.

DONE WHEN: all three paths are pinned by test including the null-externalId case; the repair is pinned as best-effort - a repair failure does not fail the resolution; and a resolution that finds nothing returns null rather than throwing.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-27 for the RESOLUTION half. Commits 2c15986 + 4d7e9a9. 483 tests / 32 files; four gates exit 0, verified independently by the controller.

SPLIT: this issue's DONE-WHEN spanned all three resolution paths AND the customer repair. The repair and the checkouts.get fallback both need the Polar SDK and belong to Task 9 (wordle-teams-l1v), where they are now recorded. This issue covers convex/lib/polarIdentity.ts (pure candidate extraction) and resolvePlayerIdFor (dual-namespace DB resolution).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 2 IS NOW PINNED - both release-gate cases, before any sandbox run, as decision C requires.

MUTATION VERDICTS (exit codes, isolated extraction, re-run after the review amendments rather than assumed inert):
  by_legacyId fallback deleted     -> 1 (3 failed)
  existence check dropped          -> 1 (1 failed)
  metadata-ignoring extractor      -> 1 (3 failed)
  sanity rename                    -> 0

THE PLAN'S RELEASE-GATE TEST WAS VACUOUS AND THIS IS THE MOST SERIOUS PLAN DEFECT SO FAR. 'RELEASE GATE, case 1' was a BYTE-FOR-BYTE duplicate of the plain 'resolves a native Convex player id' test above it - same body, different name - so it asserted nothing about metadata.player_id. The owner had designated exactly this case a gate that must pass BEFORE the sandbox run, so a vacuous test there would have manufactured the false confidence the gate exists to prevent.

The check that replaces it is 'does this name a live player' - normalizeId for shape, then ctx.db.get for existence, then by_legacyId.

title: Task 7: downgradeTeamRemovalFor - SOFTENED, never deletes an occupied team
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. The Convex port of v1's handle_downgrade_team_removal - DELIBERATELY NOT FAITHFUL. See design decision A.

WHAT V1 DOES (20240501191728): keeps the first 2 teams the player belongs to, ordered creator-owned first then oldest; removes the player from the rest; then DELETES the teams they created that are not in the keep list - taking every other member's scores and monthly-winner history with them.

WHAT V2 DOES INSTEAD. Owner's decision 2026-08-25: a billing event on one account must not destroy a third party's data.
  1. Keep 2 teams. Same ordering rule as v1: teams the player created first, then oldest.
  2. Remove the player from every other team they belong to.
  3. For a team they CREATED and have now left: reassign creator to the earliest-joined remaining member.
  4. ONLY if no members remain: delete the team. Nobody loses anything, and copy-filters.mjs already establishes that a team with nobody on it is not a team.

RULED OUT - leaving the team creator-less. V2-ADDENDUM already records that a creator-less team cannot be edited by anyone; manufacturing that state deliberately is worse than reassigning.

THE ORDERING RULE IS SUBTLE AND V1'S SQL IS HARD TO READ. Establish what it actually does before porting - the keep query does 'group by creator, created_at ... order by case when creator = player then 0 else 1 end, created_at limit 2'. Verify the intended semantics rather than transliterating the SQL.

INTERACTION WORTH KNOWING: a team deleted here carries a legacyId, so a later copy re-inserts it - that is wt-ksh.13.10, already detected by the copy's insert report, not this task's problem. But step 4 above is a NEW delete site, so wt-ksh.13.10's runbook step 2 and the 'db.delete' inventory in scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs both name delete sites and may need updating. Check.

DONE WHEN: a downgrade with 5 teams keeps exactly 2; a team the player created and left survives with a reassigned creator; a team with no members left is deleted; no team containing another member is EVER deleted; and all four are pinned by convex-test.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-26. Commits e405d8b (implementation) + 5e8fd58 (pin the copy). DIVERGENCE 12.

MEASURED independently by the controller: lint/typecheck/build exit 0; 454 tests / 30 files; e2e 15 passed (38.6s).

  ordering SANITY  (rename a local)       -> exit 0
Both reproduced independently by the spec reviewer.

THE COPY FIX IS PINNED BY A PROPERTY TEST, not an exact string. src/lib/convex-error.test.ts is the FIRST test file for that module. It asserts no /creat/i and a present /\bowner\b/i over both codes, plus a length guard so an empty string cannot satisfy 'does not mention creation'. Two controls (one per code) both exit 1; a SANITY rewrite to DIFFERENT owner-based sentences still passes - so it pins the property, not the wording.

WHY THAT MATTERED: the review noticed the rewording was itself guarded by nothing, which is the exact blind spot that let the original strings go stale. Fixing the sentence without fixing the mechanism would have left the next drift equally invisible.

TWO PLAN SNIPPETS WERE WRONG AND WERE CAUGHT (both reproduced verbatim by the reviewer):
- The 5-team ordering test used all-solo teams, so the three dropped ones are correctly DELETED and the test's own (await ctx.db.get(id))!.playerIds then dereferences null. Real TypeError.
- The cascade test used a nonexistent monthlyWinners.score field and omitted the REQUIRED hasSeenCelebration.
Neither rewrite weakened the pin; the cascade test is now stronger, asserting the scoringSystems row is gone too.

BEHAVIOURAL TENSION WORTH KNOWING: teams.ts:382 refuses to let an owner leave their own team (OWNER_NOT_REMOVABLE), yet this helper removes an owner from theirs. The user-facing copy stays true only because the owner reassignment happens in the SAME ctx.db.patch. A future refactor that splits that patch has the copy downstream of it.

title: Task 6: upgradeTeamInvitesFor + the derived pending-invite count
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. The Convex port of v1's handle_upgrade_team_invites RPC.

v1 (20240426190809): for the upgrading player, on every team whose invited array holds their email - remove the email from invited, append their id to player_ids - then zero invites_pending_upgrade.

v2: the same, as a ...For helper. Move the player from team.invited to team.playerIds on every team that invited them, and reset their pending-upgrade count to 0.

KEYS OFF teams.invited, NOT OFF THE COUNTER. This is what makes design decision D safe: v1's counter lives in auth.users.raw_app_meta_data, which the copy script does not read and will not start reading. The actual parking is in teams.invited, which IS copied - so a migrated v1 user with parked invites is released correctly in v2 even though their counter arrives as 0.

Addresses in invited are lowercased on write since Phase 4; compare normalised.

title: Task 4: convex/lib/polarEvents.ts - the pure event map
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. Port src/lib/polar/events.ts. Pure - no I/O, no env, no Convex. It holds the only real logic in the billing integration.

THE MAP:
  subscription.active / subscription.uncanceled -> pro,     release parked invites
  subscription.revoked                          -> expired, apply the team limit
  subscription.canceled / subscription.past_due -> recognised, NO CHANGE
  anything else                                 -> null

WHY canceled MUST NOT DOWNGRADE: Polar splits Lemon Squeezy's single cancellation moment in two. canceled means the customer SCHEDULED a cancellation and keeps paid access to the end of the period they paid for; revoked means access actually ended. Downgrading on canceled strips a paying customer's teams weeks early.

USE A Map, NOT AN OBJECT LITERAL. The key is an arbitrary string arriving from a webhook. A Record lookup walks the prototype chain, so 'toString' returns a Function and '__proto__' returns an object - both truthy, both violating the contract that anything unrecognised yields null, and both capable of reaching the database as an undefined membership status. v1 documents this; do not undo it.

subscription.created is DELIBERATELY ABSENT: it fires when a subscription record is established, which is not the same as it being paid for. subscription.active is the grant signal.

DONE WHEN: every one of the five acknowledged events is pinned by a test; 'toString', '__proto__' and 'constructor' are pinned to return null; and the recognised-but-inert events are distinguishable from unrecognised ones (v1 does this with an ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENTS set, worth porting).
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-26. Commits 212814c (module) + 0777597 (api.d.ts codegen) + f79b1bf (review fixes).

MEASURED independently by the controller: lint/typecheck/build exit 0; 467 tests / 31 files.

MUTATION VERDICTS, exit codes, isolated git-archive extraction. Four, not two:
  CONTROL canceled->REVOKE                      -> exit 1
  SANITY  reorder two map entries               -> exit 0
  UNSHARE give uncanceled its own frozen object -> exit 1
  NAIVE   isAcknowledgedEvent delegating to mapEventToTransition (losing the inert distinction) -> exit 1
The reviewer independently ran five FURTHER mutations and found every assertion load-bearing - no dead weight in the suite.

HOSTILE-INPUT PROOF: the reviewer probed 30 hostile keys (all prototype members, all Map method names, '', ' ', '0', 'null', 'NaN', '[object Object]') plus 8 non-string values forced through the type hole. Every one returned null or a frozen transition. Nothing escapes the contract.

API CHANGE FROM THE PLAN: ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENTS was REPLACED by isAcknowledgedEvent(). ReadonlySet is compile-time only - a caller can .add() to the exported set at runtime, and Object.freeze does NOT prevent it (measured: a frozen Set still accepts .add, because entries live in internal slots). That made the acknowledged-vs-unrecognised classification corruptible, which is exactly what Task 10 branches on. TASK 10 MUST CALL isAcknowledgedEvent(), NOT ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENTS.has(). Recorded in the plan's Task 4 section.

THREE FALSE COMMENTS CAUGHT IN REVIEW, all verified by the controller:
- 'migrate.ts:695 is the only non-test writer of membershipStatus' - line 695 is inside parityProbe, an internalQuery. A READ. The real writers are the patch and insert in upsertMemberships. The implementer had added this line SPECIFICALLY to be accurate.
- 'the functions that carry the effects out live in convex/billing.ts' - billing.ts exports exactly one symbol; no release-invites implementation exists anywhere (Task 6).
- 'the five events the Polar webhook endpoint subscribes to' - present tense about an endpoint that does not exist; convex/http.ts registers only Better Auth routes.

The plan's own test named 'the two grant events do not share a mutable object' only asserted frozenness and never compared them - proven by running it under an unshare mutation, where it exits 0.

title: Task 0: Verify @polar-sh/better-auth does not auto-acknowledge webhooks
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. FIRST TASK: it decides the shape of every task after it.

The v2 design named @polar-sh/better-auth as the integration path. v1 DELIBERATELY REJECTED @polar-sh/nextjs because its Webhooks helper auto-acknowledges - it returns 2xx before the handler has stored and processed the event. That destroys the store-then-process-then-500-so-Polar-retries behaviour the entire idempotency design rests on. The Better Auth plugin may do the same thing.

DO NOT ADOPT IT UNTIL THIS IS ANSWERED. Read the plugin source (node_modules or GitHub) and establish, by reading actual code rather than docs: does its webhook handler send a response before, or after, the user handler resolves? Can the handler force a non-2xx that Polar will retry?

Raw @polar-sh/sdk is the KNOWN-GOOD fallback and is what v1 ships today.

DONE WHEN: the finding is written on this issue citing the file and lines that decide it; the chosen dependency is added to v2/package.json; and if the plugin was rejected, the reason is recorded where the next person will not re-litigate it.
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-08-26 by reading the plugin source, NOT the docs. The premise in this issue was WRONG, and the correction matters.

@polar-sh/better-auth@1.8.4 does NOT auto-acknowledge. dist/index.js:801-806 AWAITS handleWebhookPayload before `return ctx.json({ received: true })`. So the concern inherited from @polar-sh/nextjs's Webhooks helper does not apply to this plugin.

IT IS STILL REJECTED, for a different and equally disqualifying reason. On any handler error it throws APIError("BAD_REQUEST") (dist/index.js:812-816), and BAD_REQUEST maps to HTTP 400 (better-call@1.3.7, dist/error.mjs:56). The endpoint can therefore only ever produce 200 or 400. There is no path to a 5xx, so Polar is never asked to retry.

DECISION: raw @polar-sh/sdk only, with a plain Convex httpAction that owns its own status code. The status code IS the retry protocol here.

Recorded precisely so nobody re-litigates this against the wrong reason - "it auto-acknowledges" is false and would be easy to disprove, which could reopen a settled decision.

Superseded by Task 9 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-v2-phase5-polar.md.
close_reason: Closed

title: internal.migrate.counts does unbounded .collect() and will blow Convex's read limit at full scale
description:
Found while reviewing wt-ksh.13.10, 2026-08-24. Verified by direct read, not inferred.

convex/migrate.ts:691-698 - the counts query:

    players: (await ctx.db.query('players').collect()).length,
    teams: (await ctx.db.query('teams').collect()).length,
    dailyScores: (await ctx.db.query('dailyScores').collect()).length,
    monthlyWinners: (await ctx.db.query('monthlyWinners').collect()).length,
    playerMembership: (await ctx.db.query('playerMembership').collect()).length,
    webhookEvents: (await ctx.db.query('webhookEvents').collect()).length,

Six unbounded collects, one of them dailyScores.

THE LIMIT IS DOCUMENTED IN THIS SAME FILE, TWICE, AND counts IS THE ONE PLACE THAT IGNORES IT:
  - migrate.ts:574 (purgeCopiedData): 'Convex caps a single function execution at 4096 reads, and the copied scope alone is ~7000 daily scores. So this deletes a bounded slice per call and reports whether more remains; the caller loops until done.'
  - migrate.ts:616-618 (parityProbe): 'Deliberately excludes daily scores: there are ~7000 of them in the scoped copy alone, and Convex bounds reads per execution. Those go through playerScoreFingerprint, one player at a time.'
  - migrate.ts:658-660 (playerScoreFingerprint): 'One player at a time so a big copy cannot blow the per-execution read limit.'

So the author knew, and handled it in three places. counts is the outlier.

WHO CALLS IT, AND WHY THIS IS P1:
  1. scripts/verify-parity.mjs:59 - the FIRST query the parity verifier makes, in a Promise.all beside parityProbe. This is the one that matters. The verifier's whole purpose is the Phase 7 parity audit and the cutover window, and at --scope=all it would fail before comparing a single row. A verifier that cannot run at the one moment it is load-bearing is worse than no verifier.
  2. scripts/copy-from-supabase.mjs - the end-of-run 'Convex now holds:' block (pre-existing).
  3. scripts/copy-from-supabase.mjs - the new PRE-WRITE call added by wt-ksh.13.10's insert detector. That one is being wrapped in try/catch under 13.10 so a failure degrades rather than killing the copy, but the underlying query is still broken.

SCALE: production is 535 players / 535 memberships / ~173 teams and the daily-score count is the problem - the repo's own comments put the SCOPED set at ~7000, and cutover runs --scope=all. Either figure is well past 4096.

NOT YET MEASURED: whether it already fails on beta. Beta held 6950 daily scores as of the Phase 4 design's measurement, which is already over the cap, so it may be failing there today and nobody has run the verifier at that scale to notice. Someone should just run verify-parity.mjs against beta and see - that is a five-minute answer and it decides whether this is latent or already broken.

LIKELY FIX: counts does not need the rows, only the number. Options in rough order of preference:
  - keep a counter table maintained by the upserts (exact, O(1) read, but new write surface)
  - paginate internally and sum, the way purgeCopiedData already loops
  - drop dailyScores from counts and get that number from playerScoreFingerprint's per-player totals, which the verifier already walks - mirrors what parityProbe already does for the same reason
The third is the smallest change and matches the precedent in this file.

BLOCKS: the Phase 7 parity audit (wt-ksh.8) and cutover (wt-ksh.9) in practice, since both run these scripts at --scope=all.

title: A re-copy RESURRECTS rows v2 deleted, and no diff report can see it
description:
Found by the wt-ksh.13.4 review, 2026-08-24, and confirmed by probe.

THE CLOBBER REPORT BUILT IN 13.4 CANNOT COVER THIS, BY CONSTRUCTION. It diffs an incoming doc against an existing row. When v2 DELETED the row there is nothing to diff: byLegacyId finds no match, the copy takes the insert branch, and the row comes back reported as 'inserted=1' - indistinguishable from a genuinely new v1 row.

CONFIRMED FOR TEAMS. cascadeDeleteTeam (convex/teams.ts:250-266) hard-deletes the team doc plus its monthlyWinners and scoringSystems rows, and is reachable from deleteTeamFor (creator-only) and from leaveTeamFor's last-member branch. It does not care whether the team carries a legacyId. Probe against a team with legacyId 1: the deleted team was re-inserted, its winner row with it, and the summary read inserted=1.

CONFIRMED FOR DAILY SCORES, and this is the half of wordle-teams-r9d that r9d itself notes cannot be fixed by reporting. upsertBoardFor (convex/scores.ts:235) deletes a board when the player clears it; upsertDailyScores matches on legacyId, finds nothing, and re-inserts. A board the player deliberately deleted returns, changing monthly totals and the winner for that month.

WHY IT IS NOT COVERED BY THE 'v2-born rows are unreachable' ARGUMENT: that argument says a row born in v2 has no legacyId so the copy can never match it. True, and irrelevant here. These rows WERE copied - they have a legacyId - and were then removed by v2. Deletion is what puts them back in the insert path.

POSSIBLE CURES, none chosen:
 - a tombstone: record the legacyId of anything v2 deletes, and have the copy report an insert whose legacyId is in that set
 - accept it, and put it in the cutover runbook beside the discard decision - defensible for beta, per the owner's 2026-08-24 restatement that beta is permanently testing data, but NOT defensible once real users are on v2
 - refuse to re-insert a legacyId the deployment has seen before, which needs the tombstone anyway

BLAST RADIUS IS LARGER THAN THE CLOBBER'S. An overwritten name is cosmetic; a resurrected board or team changes scoring history, and monthlyWinners rows are recomputed from boards.
notes: Bumped to P1 by the owner on 2026-08-24. Rationale: a resurrected board or team rewrites SCORING HISTORY - monthlyWinners are recomputed from boards, so a returning board can change who won a month - where a clobbered team name is cosmetic. The beta case is covered by the owner's discard decision; this stops being defensible the moment real users are on v2, which makes it cutover-blocking rather than merely untidy.
close_reason:
Shipped in 4ff27f2..69cfd81 (three commits). The owner chose cure C+D-style: an INSERT-COUNT DETECTOR plus a runbook line. The tombstone was considered and explicitly NOT built - no Convex table, no schema change, no writes at delete sites. convex/ is untouched.

THE INSIGHT: a re-copy against unchanged v1 data should insert NOTHING, and all six upserts already return 'inserted' (migrate.ts:266/341/388/466/508/553). So a non-zero insert count on a re-run is either a genuinely new v1 row or a resurrection - a detector for what the clobber report structurally cannot see, with no schema change. It covers ALL SIX TABLES, including dailyScores, which the clobber report deliberately does not diff (wordle-teams-r9d).

IT DOES NOT ATTRIBUTE, and every comment and printed line says so. It narrows 'invisible' to 'visible and worth adjudicating'. wt-ksh.9 step 2 does the adjudicating.

THE TRIGGER IS MEASURED, NOT FLAGGED. formatInsertReport(talliesByTable, countsBefore) in scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs; copy-from-supabase.mjs reads internal.migrate.counts BEFORE the writes and uses 'the deployment was already non-empty' as the re-run signal. No --expect-no-inserts flag an operator can forget at the one moment it matters. Empty deployment stays SILENT (every row is legitimately an insert on a first copy); non-empty with zero inserts prints one quiet line; non-empty with inserts prints a second framed block after the clobber block.

TOTAL-EMPTINESS IS THE RIGHT TEST AND PER-TABLE WOULD BE WRONG - measured, not argued. Review built a per-table variant and ran both against this bead's own confirmed resurrection paths. Per-table goes SILENT on both, because v2 deleting a table's last row makes that table look like a first copy.

FOUR BLOCKING DEFECTS FOUND BY REVIEW, all fixed:
  1. THE FIX WAS ITSELF A CUTOVER REGRESSION. The new pre-write call sat on a bare top-level await, so a failure would kill the copy BEFORE any write - where today the same query runs only at the end, costing a summary rather than the run. And the risk is concrete: migrate.counts does unbounded .collect()s. Now wrapped: the copy proceeds, countsBefore becomes null, and an explicit 'Insert check DID NOT RUN' line prints - because silence is the FIRST-COPY answer and would be read as an all-clear. Only null degrades; malformed shapes still throw, and a mutant confirms the tests enforce the split.
  2. THE BLOCK PRINTED A FALSE DICHOTOMY - 'either new in v1, or one v2 deleted' - in the one place the operator actually reads. At least three innocent explanations exist. Now non-exhaustive, with the enumeration moved to step 2.
  3. THE GREP THE RUNBOOK TELLS THE OPERATOR TO RUN did not match the list it gave them: 14 hits, not the three named. Now states the full breakdown.
  4. THE ADJUDICATION CONDEMNED A RESUMED PARTIAL COPY. A copy that died after players+teams and was re-run fires the block with ~22,000 rows, all of which fail the created_at question - so the remedy said hand-delete 22,058 legitimately-copied rows. Now GATED: gate A (is this the same copy run again - partial resume, widened or CHANGED scope, first copy into a deployment holding v2-born rows, or an unlooped purgeCopiedData leaving ~800 dailyScores to come back), gate B (did the skip filters' inputs move - a nameless player since named), gate C (the created_at question, only with A and B ruled out). The remedy ends: 'DELETING ON GATE C ALONE IS THE DANGEROUS MISTAKE HERE.'

The implementer also found two more instances of defect 2 inside step 2 that neither the reviewer nor the controller had flagged.

VERIFICATION. 415 tests (from 392 at task start), four gates green, re-run by the controller. Review executed the spliced pre-write region against a throwing stub to prove the copy still writes; ran 21 input shapes through the degrade path; killed 14 mutants in the first round including 'held === 0' -> 'held < 0' and the per-table swap; re-ran the grep hit for hit; verified step 1 untouched by independent hashing; and confirmed the frame holds at 16 lines with the longest at 76 columns. Counts-only holds including err.message - the catch does not widen disclosure, since an unhandled rejection printed the same string.

ACCEPTED, NOT SOLVED, and on the record:
  - The block will fire on nearly every dual-running re-run, because v1 gains daily scores continuously. Inherent to the chosen cure. If it proves too noisy the answer is the tombstone, not a threshold.
  - One silent path: an empty deployment. Reaching it needs either never having copied or an explicit purge. No v2 path can empty it, since nothing deletes players - verified recursively.
  - totalHeld's guard is slipped by NaN (prints the block) and by Map/Date/Object.create(null) (returns SILENT, worse in kind). Both unreachable through migrate.counts, which returns .length. Not guarded; speculative.
  - wt-ksh.9 step 2 is now 1249 words, larger than step 1's 851. The gates earn it, but the next person to add to that runbook should move the mechanics into the epic instead.

FOUND WHILE REVIEWING THIS, AND MORE CONSEQUENTIAL THAN THE TASK: wordle-teams-b31 (P1). internal.migrate.counts does six unbounded .collect()s including dailyScores, and it is the FIRST query verify-parity.mjs makes. At --scope=all the parity verifier would fail before comparing a row. migrate.ts documents the 4096-read cap in three other places and works around it in all three; counts is the outlier. Flagged on wt-ksh.8.

title: Task 4: verify-parity.mjs applies the copy's own exclusion rules (wordle-teams-9lt)
description:
Acceptance criterion 4 of the parent. Closes wordle-teams-9lt.

verify-parity.mjs compares every scoped Supabase row against Convex, but the copy deliberately skips nameless players and memberless teams - 151 of 533 and 29 of 173 measured against production. Apply selectCopyable from scripts/lib/copy-filters.mjs to the source rows.

NOT JUST THE TWO COUNT LINES at :66-67. src.teams is iterated again at :77 for the invited-set comparison, and src.players at :124 and :127 for the timezone and per-player score probes. Narrow ONCE at the top and have everything downstream read the narrowed set, or the counts agree while the field comparisons still walk rows that were never copied.

DO NOT fix by relaxing the comparison - 9lt says this explicitly. The point of the verifier is exactness; it must account for the exclusions, not tolerate a delta.

copy-filters.mjs's header currently says it is deliberately NOT shared with the verifier, so that this stays addressable rather than silently divergent. That sentence becomes false with this task - update it.

DONE WHEN: a clean copy reports parity on players and teams rather than a shortfall, and scripts/lib/copy-filters.test.mjs still passes unchanged.
notes:
SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-24 by wt-ksh.13.8's answer, which is now closed. The verifier must narrow MEMBERSHIPS as well as players and teams.

MEASURED IN PRODUCTION: all 151 nameless players carry a player_customer row, and memberships_total == players_total == 535, so player_customer is exactly 1:1 with players. The membership shortfall is therefore exactly 151 - the same number as the player shortfall, by construction rather than by coincidence, because each skipped player takes precisely one membership row with it. No orphans (memberships_orphaned = 0).

WHAT CHANGES IN THE TASK: selectCopyable returns players and teams only. The verifier additionally needs its memberships narrowed to those whose player_id is in the copyable player set. Do NOT widen selectCopyable's return to do this - the copier does not need it (upsertMemberships already drops orphans and counts them into its own skipped tally, which is deliberate per copy-from-supabase.mjs:103-108). This is a verifier-side narrowing over the copyable ids selectCopyable already yields.

SANITY CHECK AVAILABLE TO WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS THIS: after the fix, a full-copy verification should report parity on players, teams AND playerMembership. If players and memberships do not move by the SAME 151, the narrowing predicate has diverged from isNamed and that is the bug, not a data problem.

WIDENED ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: a clean copy reports parity on players, teams and playerMembership rather than a shortfall on any of them.

Scores, winners and webhooks are still out of scope and still correctly left to each upsert's own orphan tally - the Phase 4 design measured that nameless players own 0 boards and 0 monthly-winner rows, and webhook_events is scoped by player_id the same way but was never claimed to be affected. If a full-copy verification shows a shortfall on any of those three, that is a NEW finding, not this task.
FULL CLOSE ACCOUNT (the close reason got the short text intended for wordle-teams-9lt; this is the real one).

Shipped in df63225..e22d2ea (three commits). Closes wordle-teams-9lt.

verify-parity.mjs now narrows ONCE, immediately after readScoped: 'scoped' holds the raw result and survives only as the 'of N in scope' denominators; 'src = narrowToCopied(scoped)' is what every comparison below reads. No per-site .filter() exists, so no site can be forgotten.

NEW MODULE scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs (+ verify-filters.test.mjs, 15 tests) rather than widening copy-filters.mjs:
  - narrowToCopied(src) IMPORTS selectCopyable rather than reimplementing the rules, so the verifier cannot drift from the copier, and additionally narrows MEMBERSHIPS to those whose player_id is in the copyable set. selectCopyable's return is unwidened, per the bead. It also returns copiedPlayerIds, which the roster comparison reads rather than recomputing.
  - copy-filters.test.mjs is byte-identical to its pre-task state - the done-when satisfied literally rather than loosely.
  - expectedMemberCount(team, copiedPlayerIds) lives here too. It started inline in the script, which review caught: pure logic in an un-importable file, with the test re-implementing the same expression, is the exact drift this task exists to remove, one level down.

SITES NARROWED: the players/teams/playerMembership count checks; the teams loop (name, member count, invited set); the membership status map - narrowing the count line alone would have left 'statuses agreeing' comparing 535 rows against 384, the bead's stated failure mode; tzByPlayerId and the per-player score probe; and the PARITY OK summary, so the success line agrees with the checks above it.

DELIBERATELY NOT NARROWED, now commented on both sides: the COPIER's identically-named tzByPlayerId must stay built from all scoped players, because it is read once per scoped score including scores owned by skipped players. supabase-scope.mjs:115 falls back to HOME_TZ, so narrowing it there would silently compute a wrong puzzleDay. dailyScores/monthlyWinners/webhookEvents count checks stay full-scoped, per the bead.

THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL, raised by the implementer and adjudicated by review. The team member-count check compared t.player_ids.length against Convex. upsertTeams drops members whose uuid does not resolve, and the Phase 4 design measures 3 live teams holding a nameless member, so a --scope=all run would have produced 3 false FAILs. The expectation is now the roster filtered through copiedPlayerIds. Review simulated upsertTeams' real resolution across five cases: this is NOT the relaxation wordle-teams-9lt forbids. A named member genuinely lost still FAILS, and a nameless player WRONGLY PRESENT in Convex now FAILS where the old check PASSED. The accepted set moved rather than widened - strictly more precise in both directions. The --scope=mine worry does not arise: supabase-scope.mjs:64 flat-maps every scoped team's roster into scopedPlayerIds, so every member of a scoped team is itself in scope.

THE VERIFIER NOW SAYS THE NARROWING RAN - an unconditional three-line block, zeroes included, following copy-from-supabase.mjs's precedent that a zero states the filters ran rather than leaving silence that could equally mean they never did. Counts only; review audited the whole output path and confirmed no name, email or invited address can reach stdout.

STALE COMMENTS FIXED: copy-filters.mjs's header ('NOT shared with verify-parity.mjs'), named by the bead; and copy-from-supabase.mjs's header consequence paragraph ('Teach it before the Phase 7 parity audit'), which the bead did not name and grep found.

VERIFICATION. 392 tests (from 377 at task start), four gates green, re-run by the controller. Review reproduced the implementer's mutation tests exactly and added a third; re-ran the five-case matrix against the extracted expectedMemberCount and confirmed it identical to the inline version, so the extraction is behaviour-preserving. narrowToCopied was attacked with null/undefined player_ids, orphan and null player_id memberships, duplicates, empty inputs and input-mutation checks. It does NOT assume 1:1 - a duplicate gives skippedPlayers=1/skippedMemberships=2, now pinned.

ONE CORRECTION WORTH RECORDING. The bead's own sanity check ('if players and memberships do not move by the SAME 151, the narrowing predicate has diverged from isNamed') is no longer the right diagnosis, and the first draft of verify-filters.mjs repeated it. Because copiedPlayerIds is derived FROM selectCopyable's output, the predicate cannot drift from isNamed. A divergence can now only mean player_customer stopped being 1:1 with players - a DATA finding. The header now says so, names both directions (a SKIPPED player with two rows, or with none), notes that a NAMED player's rows are all copied however many there are, and tells whoever sees 152 against 151 to query the skipped players' rows rather than read the file.
close_reason: Fixed by wt-ksh.13.7 (Task 4), shipped in df63225..e22d2ea. The verifier now applies selectCopyable to its source rows via scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs, narrowing players, teams AND memberships once at the top, with every downstream comparison reading the narrowed set. Not fixed by relaxing any comparison, as this issue required: the team member-count expectation was narrowed rather than loosened, and review confirmed it now fails on cases the old raw-length comparison passed. See wt-ksh.13.7's close reason for the full account.

title: Task 3: write the discard decision where a cutover reader will find it
description:
Acceptance criterion 1 of the parent. This is the C half, and it is what turns the bug into intent.

Record that BETA TEAM AND PLAYER STATE IS DISCARDED AT CUTOVER, deliberately, because the final copy is meant to overwrite beta test data.

WHERE: the parent design's Data Model & Migration section, which is where the re-runnable property is asserted today - the claim and its consequence belong together. Add a pointer from docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md if the divergence table is the more likely reading path.

ALSO: put an explicit step on wt-ksh.9 (Phase 8 - Cutover), since the runbook does not exist yet and this decision is worthless if it is not in front of whoever writes it. The step is: expect the copy's overwrite report to be non-zero for beta state, and confirm it is non-zero for NOTHING ELSE.

notes:

Say that beta is permanently testing data INCLUDING rows created by other testers - it removes the obvious future objection, 'but someone else made that team'.

close_reason:
