title: Task 2: the copy script prints the clobber report loudly
description:
Acceptance criterion 2 of the parent.

copy-from-supabase.mjs already prints a 'Skipped (not copied)' section from selectCopyable's counts. Add the overwrite report beside it, fed by Task 1's return values.

IT MUST BE HARD TO MISS WHEN NON-ZERO and quiet when zero. A copy that overwrote nothing should say so in one line; a copy that reverted v2 state should be visually distinct from the routine output around it, because the person running it at cutover is watching for exactly one thing.

COUNTS ONLY, NEVER VALUES. This repository is public and the fields include team names and invited email addresses. The existing skip report already establishes this rule - follow it.

DONE WHEN: a copy against a deployment with v2 edits prints which fields on how many rows it overwrote, per table; a copy against a pristine deployment prints zero; and no field value appears in the output.
close_reason:
Shipped in 7a895e3..32a7e20 (five commits).

formatClobberReport() in scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs, wired into copy-from-supabase.mjs between the write lines and the final 'Convex now holds:' counts. It partitions the six tables three ways - overwrote something / reported clean / not diffed - and a table whose tally is {} (never written) appears in none of them.

NON-ZERO: a framed 80-column block, all-caps headline, '##' gutter, impossible to scroll past. Detail lines wrap and indent under their label with the comma riding the item before the break, so the frame holds at the worst case (nine diffable player fields, which ran to 229 columns unwrapped).

ZERO: one quiet line - 'Overwrote nothing: players, teams, monthlyWinners. Not diffed: dailyScores, playerMembership, webhookEvents.'

COUNTS ONLY, NEVER VALUES: verified by grepping the whole output path. Only field names (clobbered's keys), row counts (its values) and the writeAll label literals are interpolated. Reviewer confirmed nothing else can reach stdout.

THE ZERO LINE DOES NOT OVERCLAIM, which was not in the original bead and matters: three of the six tables never report clobbered at all, so a bare 'overwrote nothing' would have silently asserted something about dailyScores, which does not diff (wordle-teams-r9d). Both branches now build from one scopeClauses() helper, with a test that renders the same tallies through both and fails if the wording diverges.

TWO REAL DEFECTS CAUGHT BY REVIEW, both fixed:
  1. The headline first read 'OVERWROTE v2 EDITS', which asserts a cause the diff cannot know - a clobber only proves incoming != stored, which is equally a v1-side edit landing during dual-running. For the scoring group it was outright false: migrate.ts documents that v2 never writes those eight fields after createTeam. That would have fired the loudest line on screen on a run that lost nothing, which migrate.ts itself names as the failure mode that trains people to ignore the report. Now 'OVERWROTE STORED VALUES', with the cause stated in the body as the either/or it is.
  2. writeAll had been changed to store into module state keyed by its display label instead of returning. Correct only by a string literal six lines away; a reorder would have thrown a TypeError at the END of a live cutover run, after all six writes landed. Replaced with a TABLES list driving a sequential loop, writeAll returning its tally again.

Also: formatTally now throws and names the key for any nested record other than clobbered, closing a silent-drop path this change introduced - the old formatter printed any nested record inline.

VERIFICATION. 377 tests (up from 360), lint/typecheck/build green, all four gates re-run by the controller. TDD confirmed by extracting the parent commit and running the new tests against the old implementation. The wrapper was checked with a differential harness over 4,608 inputs (zero divergence on the refactor), a field-length x field-count sweep confirming max line is exactly 80 and never 81, and a mutation test on the <= FRAME boundary. Column figures in the comments were independently binary-searched against real rendered output. e2e not implicated - scripts only, no app code.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: wordle-teams-ct3 (P3) - the headline and footer are themselves unwrapped and unasserted; a fourth reporting table pushes the headline to 90 columns, outside its own frame. Unreachable today, trigger is wordle-teams-r9d, linked from there.

title: Task 1: upsertTeams and upsertPlayers report what they overwrite
description:
Acceptance criteria 2, 3 and 5 of the parent.

Both mutations already load the existing row via byLegacyId before patching. Diff the incoming doc against it and return per-field counts alongside the existing inserted/updated tallies.

SHAPE: add a 'clobbered' record to each mutation's return - e.g. { name: 3, invited: 2, playerIds: 1 } - counting rows where the incoming value DIFFERS from what is stored. Only fields that actually differ; an identical re-copy must report zero, or the report becomes noise nobody reads.

COMPARISON IS NOT ===. playerIds is an array of Ids and invited an array of strings; both need order-insensitive set comparison, because upsertTeams rebuilds playerIds by resolving uuids in source order and that order need not match what v2 left. Getting this wrong reports a clobber on every run and trains everyone to ignore it.

DO NOT defend v2-born rows. They have no legacyId, byLegacyId cannot match them, and they never reach the patch branch. Adding a guard would be dead code - see the parent's scoping section.

DONE WHEN: convex/migrate.test.ts pins that a differing field is counted, an identical field is not, and array fields compare order-insensitively; mutation-tested with a CONTROL and a SANITY mutant, verdicts by exit code.
close_reason:
Shipped in f0f51c5. upsertPlayers, upsertTeams and upsertMonthlyWinners diff the incoming doc against the stored row and return per-field overwrite counts; writeAll's merge and formatting moved to scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs with a test. 360 unit tests, lint, typecheck, build all exit 0; beta deploy 32759040913 green.

MONTHLY WINNERS ADDED BEYOND THE ORIGINAL SCOPE, owner-approved. The review found upsertMonthlyWinners matches on by_team_year_month, the exact key recomputeTeamMonth patches and deletes on; a probe showed a re-copy reverting a v2-computed winner and clearing hasSeenCelebration while reporting clobbered={}. It is also the ONE upsert that can ADOPT a v2-born row, so its report shows legacyId moving from undefined to a Supabase id - teams and players structurally cannot report that.

VERIFICATION WORTH KEEPING: the load-bearing claim is that the report iterates exactly the keys the patch writes. That was tested against an oracle derived from the stored document BEFORE and AFTER the patch rather than from the implementation - 800 random row-and-edit pairs, matched in every case - plus 13 targeted probes establishing the report never fires on a no-op, which is the property that decides whether anyone still reads it on run two.

MUTATION TESTING, all with CONTROL and SANITY, verdicts by exit code: 12 mutants in the review pass, 13 in the fix pass. One SURVIVED and is worth recording - the Array.isArray guard in the tally merge was not pinned by the first test written for it, because an array of STRINGS is refused either way; only an array of NUMBERS distinguishes the guarded from the unguarded code. The implementer found this itself, added the right test, and the mutant then died.

DECISIONS MADE ON THE AMBIGUOUS FIELDS: arrays compare as multisets (order-insensitive, since the copy rebuilds them in source order; duplicate-sensitive, since Phase 4 established invited can hold an address twice); an absent creator is not a clobber, because the conditional spread means the patch never touches it; the eight scoring fields report as one count, since v1 writes all eight in a single update.

PROCESS NOTE: the subagent's git commit --amend rewrote the CONTROLLER's beads commit, which was HEAD at the time - the exact hazard the no-commits-while-subagents-run memory describes. No content was lost (bd's export is cumulative and all markers survived) and history was rebuilt cleanly before pushing, but the pattern is now confirmed rather than theoretical.

title: Enforce the non-pro 2-team cap on invitees (deferred from Phase 4)
description:
Phase 4 deferred v1's server-side 2-team cap on non-pro INVITEES to Phase 5, with the rest of pro enforcement. v2 is currently MORE PERMISSIVE than prod.

THE RETROFIT HAZARD IS THE POINT: enforcing this later means removing people from teams they have already joined. The longer it waits, the more of them there are.

v1 implements it in handle_invited_signup and in handle_add_player_to_team. CORRECTED 2026-08-22: an earlier version of this note - and the Phase 4 epic, design spec and divergence table - claimed handle_add_player_to_team was BROKEN in production because it referenced an undeclared invited_id, and that a faithful port would port a fault. THAT IS FALSE. The bug was real but was fixed on 2024-04-29 (migration 20240429204119_handle_add_player_add_to_invited.sql changed WHERE id = invited_id to WHERE id = player_id_input). The current definition, 20240501180309_add_player_to_invited_if_not_signedup.sql, caps correctly: it increments invites_pending_upgrade and parks the address in teams.invited. Both cap branches work. Port the real behaviour.

v1 stores the overflow count in auth.users.raw_app_meta_data.invites_pending_upgrade and releases it in handle_upgrade_team_invites on upgrade. v2 has no auth metadata store; the count belongs on the players doc.

Recorded as divergence 8 in docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md 7a.
close_reason: Folded into Phase 5 as wordle-teams-qyd (Task 6), 2026-08-25, at the owner's direction. The cap is genuinely coupled to Phase 5's upgrade path - v1 parks over-cap invitees in teams.invited and releases them on upgrade, and Phase 5 has to build the release half regardless. The 2026-08-22 correction (both v1 cap branches work; the invited_id bug was fixed on 2024-04-29) is carried onto qyd verbatim so it cannot be re-litigated.

title: invitePlayer sends real invite email to e2e addresses - no isE2eEmail guard
description:
Found during Phase 4 Task 8, 2026-08-22.

auth.ts:199 short-circuits OTP mail when E2E_TEST_MODE === 'true' && isE2eEmail(email). invitePlayer has NO equivalent guard: teams.ts:591 calls resend.sendEmail unconditionally, and RESEND_API_KEY is set on the dev deployment.

CONSEQUENCE: every e2e run that exercises the invite path sends real invite emails to e2e+*@wordleteams.com. That domain has ImprovMX MX records, so they FORWARD TO A REAL INBOX rather than bouncing. Task 8's spec sends ~2 per run, and the suite was run dozens of times during implementation and verification - so this has already delivered on the order of tens of messages to the owner's inbox.

FIX: mirror auth.ts's guard at the send site in invitePlayerFor - skip resend.sendEmail when E2E_TEST_MODE === 'true' && isE2eEmail(email). Note the ground rule that every rule belongs in the ...For helper, and that the send is deliberately the one part that cannot live in the helper (see teams.ts:456), so the guard has to sit at the enqueue point rather than in a pure function.

RELATED: wordle-teams-7az already tracks that E2E_TEST_MODE must not survive onto prod. This issue is the inverse - the flag exists on dev but is not consulted where it should be.

Also worth checking whether any OTHER Resend send path (Phase 6 reminders) will need the same guard before it ships.
notes: Follow-up id correction: the Phase 6 choke-point issue is wordle-teams-sga (the close reason names 'wordle-teams-e6t', which was a placeholder written before the issue was filed and does not exist).
close_reason:
Fixed in 08cb6f4 + 9954cc3. invitePlayer now skips resend.sendEmail for e2e traffic, matching the guard auth.ts already had for sign-in codes. Only the SEND is suppressed - the address is still parked in invited and the outcome is unchanged, so the e2e specs still drive the real invite path.

The rule is a pure predicate, isE2eTraffic(email, e2eTestMode), in convex/lib/e2e.ts rather than an inline check at the send site: the send lives in the mutation wrapper, invitePlayer is authed, and nothing in this repo can drive an authed wrapper (wordle-teams-obw), so a rule stated there would be untestable - and this one SUPPRESSES, where a silent inversion stops real invitations going out on production. All five e2e-traffic checks in convex/ (auth.ts, e2eSeed.ts x2, testOtps.ts, teams.ts) now call it, so the flag comparison appears exactly once; it had been written four times in two polarities.

PROOF IT WORKED, read directly from the local backend store: the newest queued delivery from invites@wordleteams.com is 2026-08-22 11:25:30. The fix landed 13:34:24. Six full e2e suite runs since - each of which previously queued two - produced ZERO new rows, while the store was provably live (newest row of any kind 44 seconds old). Before the fix, 198 of the last 200 mail rows were invites to e2e+inv-joiner-* addresses.

Also verified: 8 mutants on the predicate killed with CONTROL and SANITY by exit code and byte-identical restore, including two that survived the first attempt (unconstrained leading ^, which would have let a real address like ada.e2e+news@wordleteams.com be reclassified and its invitation dropped with a green suite; and the unpinned escaped dot). 311 unit tests, tsc, build clean; e2e 15/15 across three runs after touching the sign-in and seed guards.

CAVEAT CARRIED TO wordle-teams-7az: the production half of this predicate is a REQUIREMENT, not a fact. Beta carries its environment into production at cutover, so if E2E_TEST_MODE survives, invitations to any e2e+*@wordleteams.com address are now dropped silently here. 7az is the step that clears it.

FOLLOW-UP: no choke point stops Phase 6 reintroducing this - see wordle-teams-e6t.

title: bd auto-populates a personal email into every issue's owner field, in a public repo
description:
Found by the Phase 4 Task 0c/0d joint review, 2026-08-21.

.beads/issues.jsonl is git-tracked and this repository is PUBLIC. bd writes the
configured owner into every issue's `owner` field, so a personal address now
appears in that file once per issue — 202 occurrences as of today, growing by one
per issue created.

It is NOT the git author identity, so it is not otherwise present in the repo:
commit metadata carries a different, work address. This one is exposed only via
beads.

Pre-existing and auto-populated rather than typed, so no single commit introduced
it. But it is exactly what the "never put user emails in beads" rule exists to
prevent, arriving through a path that rule did not anticipate — the tool, not the
author.

Two parts to fix:
 1. Stop new issues carrying it — bd config (owner/assignee identity), so future
    issues use a handle rather than an address.
 2. Decide what to do about the 202 existing rows. Rewriting them changes every
    line of a tracked file and its Dolt history; leaving them means the address
    stays in the public repo and in git history regardless. Owner's call, and
    worth taking before the repo gets more attention at cutover.

Do not paste the address into this issue or any other.
acceptance_criteria: issues.jsonl carries no personal email address, and new issues do not reintroduce one.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-08-21: fine with their own address in beads. Not a concern.

title: verify-parity.mjs will report a false shortfall once the copy skips nameless players
description:
Found while implementing Phase 4 Task 0c (wt-ksh.5.11), 2026-08-21.

v2/scripts/verify-parity.mjs compares src.players.length and src.teams.length —
every scoped Supabase row — against Convex's counts. Since Task 0c, the copy
deliberately SKIPS players with no first/last name, and teams left with no
members after that filter.

So the moment either skip count is non-zero, the verifier reports a players/teams
shortfall that is not a shortfall. Measured against production: 151 of 533
players and 29 of 173 teams would be skipped, so at the full copy this is not a
rare edge case — the verifier will be wrong by 151 and 29 respectively.

This matters at the PHASE 7 PARITY AUDIT, which is the one moment the verifier's
answer is load-bearing. A verifier that cries wolf at the audit is worse than no
verifier, because the real discrepancies it exists to find will be sitting inside
a known-bad number.

The exclusion rules are already extracted and testable at
v2/scripts/lib/copy-filters.mjs (isNamed, selectCopyable). The fix is to have the
verifier apply the same selection to its source rows before comparing, rather
than reimplementing the rule — copy-filters.mjs's own header notes it is
deliberately NOT shared with the verifier yet, precisely so this is addressable
rather than silently divergent.

Do NOT fix by relaxing the comparison; the point of the verifier is exactness.
acceptance_criteria: The parity verifier accounts for rows the copy deliberately skips, so a clean copy reports parity rather than a players/teams shortfall.
notes: FOLDED INTO wt-ksh.13's plan on 2026-08-24 at the owner's direction. The fix is wt-ksh.13.7 (Task 4); the unanswered playerMembership question this issue does not cover is wt-ksh.13.8 (Task 5), which blocks it. Close this issue when 13.7 closes.
close_reason: Fixed by wt-ksh.13.7 (Task 4), shipped in df63225..e22d2ea. The verifier now applies selectCopyable to its source rows via scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs, narrowing players, teams AND memberships once at the top, with every downstream comparison reading the narrowed set. Not fixed by relaxing any comparison, as this issue required: the team member-count expectation was narrowed rather than loosened, and review confirmed it now fails on cases the old raw-length comparison passed. See wt-ksh.13.7's close reason for the full account.

title: Task 2: completeProfile + needsProfile
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 2

Creates convex/players.ts - the only place a player is born other than the
Supabase copy and e2eSeed.

Deliberately NOT requirePlayer: there is no player yet, which is the entire
point. Authenticates against the Better Auth user directly.

ORDER MATTERS inside completeProfileFor: the player must exist before invites are
claimed, and the claim must happen before the recompute, because the recompute's
answer depends on the roster the claim just changed.

THE RECOMPUTE IS wt-ksh.5.2. The joiner becomes eligible for every month their
new teams already have a winner row for; without it each of those months stays
wrong forever. monthsWithWinners does not help on its own - it returns months
that already HAVE a winner row, and the joiner was excluded from every
computation that produced them. winners.ts already exposes the entry point; this
is the third caller its extraction (wordle-teams-4gj) was for.

Also adds INVALID_EMAIL and INVALID_NAME to AccessCode, which breaks the
exhaustive switch in src/lib/convex-error.ts until each has copy - that check is
deliberate and is doing its job. And splits NO_PLAYER's message away from
UNAUTHENTICATED: "Your session expired" is actively wrong for someone whose
session is fine and who simply has no profile yet, and signing in again does not
help.

MUTATION-TEST STEP: comment out the recompute loop and confirm the winner-row
test fails.

Blocks Tasks 6 and 7.
acceptance_criteria: A player row is created with no legacyId and v1's column defaults; a second call patches rather than duplicating; a MIXED-CASE invite is claimed from the lowercase account; and every claimed team's existing winner rows are recomputed.

title: Task 1: convex/lib/invite.ts - address normalisation and name completeness
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 1

Dependency-free, like everything in convex/lib/.

normaliseInviteEmail is A2's fix at the write boundary. v1 stored teams.invited
as typed and matched it case-sensitively while auth lowercases addresses, so
anyone invited at a mixed-case address silently never joined their team. That is
a data-model bug, not a platform one, and a faithful port reproduces it.
Normalise on WRITE and compare case-insensitively on READ, so copied rows that
predate v1's own fix cannot slip through either.

isCompleteName is ONE function used by BOTH completeProfile's validation and the
needsProfile route guard. If they ever disagree, a name that saves does not clear
the guard and the user is redirected to the profile form forever. v1 has exactly
that latent bug: it accepts any non-empty name but guards on length > 1, so a
one-character name loops. Do NOT tighten this to length > 1 - there is a test
pinning the one-character case for this reason.
acceptance_criteria: normaliseInviteEmail trims, lowercases and rejects malformed input; isCompleteName accepts a ONE-CHARACTER name and rejects whitespace-only parts.
close_reason: Approved by spec and code-quality review; 16-mutant battery green

title: Task 0d: Delete hasCompleteProfile and its three call sites
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 0d

The payoff of Task 0c. hasCompleteProfile's own doc comment warns that its three
call sites - the scoreboard (scores.ts), the winner computation (winners.ts) and
the team card (teams.ts) - MUST agree or the three views of "who is on this team"
disagree with each other, and that keeping them in sync by cross-referencing
comments is one edit away from drifting. They cannot drift if the state cannot
exist.

CRITICAL: the missing-document guards STAY. Checking that ctx.db.get returned
null is a DIFFERENT check from the name filter - a member id with no document is
something a scoped copy legitimately produces - and deleting the name check must
not take it with it.

Also updates e2eSeed.ts's comment, which justifies its synthetic e2e- prefixed
legacyId by players.legacyId being required. That stops being true; the synthetic
value itself stays as a test-data marker.
acceptance_criteria: convex/lib/player.ts is gone, tsc is clean, and the scores, winners and teams suites are green. The missing-document guards survive.
close_reason: hasCompleteProfile deleted, cleanup retired; 3/3 null-guard mutants killed, schema deployed clean to beta

title: Task 0c: players.legacyId optional, firstName/lastName required, copy-script filter
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 0c

Closes the wt-ksh.5.1 blocker. legacyId becomes optional for the reason the
schema already records for teams, dailyScores and monthlyWinners: absence means
"born in v2, not copied", which is Phase 7's reconciliation marker. NO
synthesised uuid - the copy matches on by_legacyId, so a fake value would
silently never match and would lie to every future reader.

as a second gate so a filter regression fails loudly at the boundary.

copy-from-supabase.mjs gains a permanent filter - it runs again at the Phase 7
audit and inside the cutover window, which is what makes it the load-bearing fix

title: The copy script overwrites v2's own team writes
description:
Found by the whole-phase review of Phase 3 (wt-ksh.4), 2026-08-19. NEW AS OF THIS PHASE.

convex/migrate.ts's upsertTeams patches an existing team with a doc carrying name, playerIds, playWeekends, showLetters and all eight scoring fields, resolved from Supabase.

Phase 2 only ever wrote dailyScores. PHASE 3 IS THE FIRST PHASE WHERE v2 MUTATES teams — createTeam, updateTeam, deleteTeam, removeMember, setScoringSystem — and the copy script has no idea any of that exists.

Re-running the copy against a deployment that has been used therefore:
 - reverts team renames and settings changes
 - RESTORES REMOVED MEMBERS, with no winner recompute, so the stale-winner rows that divergence 5 exists to fix come straight back
 - RESURRECTS DELETED TEAMS, because a deleted team no longer matches by_legacyId and is treated as a fresh insert
 - imports a v1-side scoring edit made during the dual-running window as the BASE system, retroactively rewriting every month before v2's first version row — which is exactly the bug wordle-teams-1j3 was filed against

The copy is designed to be re-runnable and the cutover runbook runs it again inside the cutover window (parent design, Data Model & Migration). That is fine while v2 is read-only against teams. It stopped being fine this phase.

Options to weigh, not yet decided:
 - make upsertTeams insert-only for teams that already exist, or patch only fields v2 never writes
 - track which teams were born in v2 (legacyId === undefined already distinguishes them) and skip them entirely
 - accept it, and make the cutover runbook explicit that beta team state is discarded at cutover — which is defensible, since the final copy is meant to overwrite beta test data, but must be a decision rather than a surprise

Belongs to Phase 7 (parity audit) or Phase 8 (cutover). Must be settled before anyone treats beta team data as real, and before Phase 4 adds invites to the same table.
design:
DECIDED 2026-08-24 by the owner: option C + D, extended to players.

=== WHAT WE ARE BUILDING, AND WHY ===

The copy script is designed to be re-runnable, and the cutover runbook runs it
again inside the cutover window. That was safe while v2 was read-only against
teams. Phase 3 made v2 write teams; Phase 4 made it write teams.invited and
teams.playerIds through invites, joins, cancels and leaves. upsertTeams patches
an existing row with a doc rebuilt from Supabase, so a re-run reverts every one
of those.

We are NOT going to make the copy preserve v2 state. We are going to make the
overwrite an explicit, documented property of the cutover, and make any instance
of it LOUD instead of silent.

=== KEY DECISIONS, AND WHAT WAS RULED OUT ===

C. BETA TEAM AND PLAYER STATE IS DISCARDED AT CUTOVER, deliberately. The final
   copy is meant to overwrite beta test data; that is its job. This stops being
   a bug the moment it is written down as intent, and it is written down.

D. THE COPY REPORTS WHAT IT CLOBBERS. upsertTeams and upsertPlayers already load
   the existing row before patching. They diff the incoming doc against it and
   return per-field counts, which the script prints. An invisible failure becomes
   a visible one, and a copy run at the wrong moment announces itself.

RULED OUT - insert-only for existing rows. It would also block legitimate v1-side
edits from landing during dual-running, which is the copy's actual job at cutover.

RULED OUT - patch only fields v2 never writes. Principled, but after Phase 4 that
set is nearly empty for teams: name, playWeekends, showLetters, playerIds,
invited and the eight base scoring fields are all v2-written. It degenerates into
insert-only.

=== A SCOPING FACT THAT SHRINKS THE PROBLEM ===

convex/teams.ts contains no legacyId at all, and completeProfileFor inserts v2
players without one. byLegacyId is the entire upsert key, so a row born in v2 can
never be matched and is STRUCTURALLY SAFE. Only COPIED rows that v2 later edited
are at risk. Do not add defences for v2-born rows; there is no path to them.

=== WHY PLAYERS ARE IN SCOPE, THOUGH THE ORIGINAL ISSUE SAID TEAMS ===

upsertPlayers patches the whole row: firstName, lastName, hasPwa, timeZone,
reminderDeliveryMethods, reminderDeliveryTime, lastBoardEntryReminder, createdAt.

It is LATENT TODAY. needsProfile is a row-existence check, so a copied player
never reaches /complete-profile, and v2 has no rename surface - completeProfileFor's
existing-row patch is idempotency defence for a double-submit, not a feature.

PHASE 6 ARMS IT. wt-ksh.7 is Reminders & PWA, and four of those fields - timeZone,
reminderDeliveryMethods, reminderDeliveryTime, hasPwa - are exactly what it will
make user-editable. Deciding players now, while the teams decision is being made,
costs one extra task. Deciding it after Phase 6 means rediscovering this.

=== SCOPE BOUNDARIES - EXPLICITLY OUT ===

  - Preserving v2 state across a copy. That is the option we ruled out.
  - A --allow-clobber confirmation flag. Report only, per D. If the owner wants
    the copy to REFUSE without explicit opt-in, that is a deliberate escalation
    beyond D and should be filed separately rather than smuggled in here.
  - The scoringSystems table. upsertTeams overwrites the eight BASE fields on the
    team doc, which is wordle-teams-1j3's retroactive-rewrite problem; the
    scoringSystems rows themselves are not copied and are not touched here.
  - Phase 8's runbook itself, which does not exist yet. This records the decision
    where a cutover reader will find it and puts the step on wt-ksh.9.

=== FOLDED IN: wordle-teams-9lt ===

verify-parity.mjs compares every scoped Supabase row against Convex, but the copy
now deliberately skips nameless players and memberless teams - 151 of 533 and 29
of 173 measured against production. The fix is to apply copy-filters.mjs's
selectCopyable to the verifier's source rows.

NOT JUST THE TWO COUNT LINES. src.teams is also iterated for the invited-set
comparison, and src.players for the timezone and per-player score probes, so the
narrowing belongs once at the top with everything downstream reading it.

OPEN, AND NOT GUESSABLE: the copy narrows only players and teams. Scores, winners,
memberships and webhooks are left to each upsert to drop as orphans. The design
measured that nameless players own 0 boards and 0 winner rows, but says nothing
about playerMembership. If those 151 players carry membership rows, the
playerMembership count is a false shortfall too and 9lt is incomplete without it.
Needs one query against production.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

  1. Re-running the copy against a deployment carrying v2 edits has a defined,
     intended effect that is written down where a cutover reader will find it.
  2. That run REPORTS, per table and per field, how many existing rows it
     overwrote - and reports zero when it overwrote nothing.
  3. The same holds for players as for teams.
  4. A clean copy reports parity rather than a players/teams shortfall.
  5. Nothing in the change defends v2-born rows, which cannot be reached.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running the copy against a used deployment has a defined, intended effect on teams created or edited in v2.
notes:
OWNER RESTATEMENT, 2026-08-24, broader than the original C: 'I approve overwriting any v2 born data as beta even if I get help testing, will always be used for testing.'

So the discard decision is not narrowly about the owner's own beta rows - it covers data created by ANY tester the owner invites. Beta is testing data, permanently. Task 3's write-up should say that, because it removes the obvious future objection ('but someone else made that team').

ONE PRECISION FOR THE WRITE-UP, and it cuts the opposite way from the phrasing. A row BORN in v2 has no legacyId, byLegacyId cannot match it, and the copy can never touch it - v2-born rows are the SAFE ones. What the copy actually overwrites is COPIED rows that v2 later edited. The owner's intent covers both cases and nothing about the decision changes; the documentation must simply not repeat the phrase 'v2-born data' as though those were the rows at risk, or a future reader will look for a bug in the wrong place.

CONSEQUENCE FOR D: since no beta data needs protecting, the overwrite report's purpose is not to guard rows. It is to make a copy run at the WRONG moment - after cutover, with real users on v2 - announce itself. That rationale applies to every table the copy can clobber, not just the two originally scoped, which is why monthlyWinners is being wired in.
close_reason:
ALL SEVEN CHILDREN CLOSED. Shipped across f0f51c5..69cfd81 on feat/v2-replatform.

The five acceptance criteria, each against what shipped:

1. 'Re-running the copy against a deployment carrying v2 edits has a defined, intended effect, written down where a cutover reader will find it.' - MET by 13.6. The discard decision sits in the epic's Data Model & Migration section directly after the re-runnable claim it follows from, with a pointer from V2-ADDENDUM 7a and two required steps on wt-ksh.9, plus a pointer on wt-ksh.8 because that is the issue actually scoped to WRITE the runbook.

2. 'That run REPORTS, per table and per field, how many existing rows it overwrote - and reports zero when it overwrote nothing.' - MET by 13.4 and 13.5. upsertPlayers, upsertTeams and upsertMonthlyWinners diff the incoming doc against the stored row and return per-field counts; the copy prints a framed 80-column block when non-zero and one quiet line when zero. Counts only, never values.

3. 'The same holds for players as for teams.' - MET. Players were in scope from 13.4 on, and Phase 6 arms five player fields before cutover.

4. 'A clean copy reports parity rather than a players/teams shortfall.' - MET by 13.7, widened by 13.8's production answer to cover memberships. verify-parity.mjs narrows once at the top through scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs, which imports selectCopyable rather than reimplementing it.

5. 'Nothing in the change defends v2-born rows, which cannot be reached.' - MET. No defence was added, and the documentation states the precision the owner's phrasing cut against: a row born in v2 has no legacyId, byLegacyId is the whole match key for players and teams, so v2-born rows are the SAFE ones. What the copy overwrites is a COPIED row v2 later edited. monthlyWinners is the exception, matching on (teamId, year, month).

WHAT THE EPIC GREW BEYOND ITS ORIGINAL SCOPE, and why:
  - 13.8 answered a question the design flagged as 'OPEN, AND NOT GUESSABLE' with a production query: player_customer is 1:1 with players (535/535, 151 nameless, 0 orphans), so each skipped player takes exactly one membership row. That widened 13.7.
  - 13.10 was found by 13.4's review: the clobber report cannot see a row v2 DELETED, by construction. The owner chose an insert-count detector plus a runbook line over a tombstone. It covers all six tables, including the one the clobber report does not diff.
  - 13.11 corrected two stale production measurements the epic's own work depended on.

VERIFICATION ACROSS THE EPIC. 360 tests at the start, 415 at the end. Four gates green on every task, re-run by the controller each time, never taken on report. Every task went implementer -> spec review -> fixes -> re-review, and THE REVIEW LOOP FOUND SOMETHING REAL ON EVERY SINGLE TASK - including two cases where the fix to a real defect introduced a narrower one in the same sentence, and one where the fix was itself a cutover regression.

THE RECURRING DEFECT CLASS, recorded because it cost more time than any bug: correct structural work paired with an unmeasured or overstated claim in the prose about it. A test 'pinning' a shape the test disproved; 'verified against every db.patch' from a non-recursive glob; 'by construction' for a property with no constraint behind it; two wrong test counts. Every measured claim held. See bd memories 'numeric-claims-in-code-comments-on-this-repo'.

LEFT OPEN, DELIBERATELY:
  - wordle-teams-b31 (P1) - internal.migrate.counts does unbounded .collect()s and is the first query verify-parity.mjs makes. Found while reviewing 13.10 and MORE CONSEQUENTIAL THAN ANYTHING IN THIS EPIC: at --scope=all the parity verifier fails before comparing a row. Flagged on wt-ksh.8. Cheapest first step is running verify-parity.mjs against beta, which already holds ~6950 daily scores.
  - wordle-teams-r9d (P2) - upsertDailyScores still has the clobber shape and is unwired. Now also carries notes that wiring it trips wordle-teams-ct3 and makes the blind-spot list wrong in four places.
  - wordle-teams-ct3 (P3) - the clobber banner's headline and footer are unwrapped; a fourth reporting table pushes the headline outside its own frame.
  - wordle-teams-9vq (P3) - three sites still carrying a stale 533 or the false 'no membership row' claim, including wt-ksh.5's epic body.

title: players.legacyId is required, so v2 cannot create a person at all — cold signup dead-ends
description:
Found while driving Task 13's zero-teams empty state (wt-ksh.4.30), 2026-08-19.

A brand-new email that signs up on v2 gets a Better Auth user but NO players row. Nothing in the login flow creates one — access.ts's requirePlayer resolves by lowercased email against the players table, and the only writers are the Supabase copy (migrate.ts) and e2eSeed.

Consequence, observed end to end: such an account CAN see the dashboard and the new zero-teams empty state, because getMyTeams uses currentPlayer and returns [] rather than throwing. But pressing Create a Team throws NO_PLAYER, which convex-error.ts maps to "Your session expired. Please sign in again." Signing in again does not help, because the account is not broken — it simply has no player.

So a cold signup reaches a working-looking screen with one call to action, and that call to action cannot succeed, with an error message that misdescribes the cause.

=== AMENDED 2026-08-20: THE REAL BLOCKER IS ONE LAYER DOWN ===

This was originally filed as "a cold signup cannot create a team". That understates it. Trying to add a real user to a real team by hand on the beta/prod deployment surfaced the actual constraint:

  players.legacyId is a REQUIRED v.string() — the Supabase auth user uuid.

So v2 has no way to bring a person into existence at all except by copying them out of Supabase. This is not a missing mutation that Phase 4 can simply add; the schema forbids the row. Any onboarding path — cold signup OR the invite flow this phase is named for — has to get past it first.

It is the same problem Task 0 fixed for teams.legacyId (wt-ksh.4.17), and Phase 2 fixed for dailyScores and monthlyWinners, and it is still unfixed for players. The fix has an established shape and rationale in this codebase:

  make it v.optional(v.string()), so absence honestly means "born in v2, not copied"

That is the marker Phase 7's row-count reconciliation against Supabase already relies on for the other three tables, and widening a required field to optional is permissive — no data migration. Do NOT synthesise a fake Supabase uuid instead: the schema's own header comment argues against exactly that, the copy matches on by_legacyId so a fake value would silently never match, and it would lie to every future reader about where the row came from.

Consequences to work through in Phase 4, now that the ordering is clear:
 - players.legacyId must be widened BEFORE any onboarding mutation can be written. It blocks the invite flow, not just cold signup.
 - hasCompleteProfile (convex/lib/player.ts) excludes a player with no firstName/lastName from the scoreboard, the team card AND the winner computation — so creating the row is necessary but not sufficient; onboarding must set a name or the person is invisible (see wt-ksh.5.3) .
 - whatever mutation sets that name must also recompute winners, or every month that player could have won stays wrong forever (wt-ksh.5.2).
 - decide whether a players row is created on first authenticated visit, or only through the invite path.
 - NO_PLAYER's copy is actively misleading here — "Your session expired" for someone whose session is fine and whose profile does not exist yet.

Why it matters more than the row count suggests: amendment A7 made login and onboarding a sanctioned exception to strict parity precisely because that surface is the product's largest measured leak (wordle-teams-456: 87% of prod signups never enter a board; wordle-teams-390: ~93% abandon at login). Shipping a cutover where a new signup hits a dead end would make that worse, not better.

Reproduce: sign in on a never-before-seen e2e address with E2E_TEST_MODE on, land on the empty state, press Create a Team.
acceptance_criteria: players.legacyId is optional, and a brand-new signup can create a team — or is told accurately why it cannot yet.
close_reason: Closed by Phase 4. players.legacyId became optional in Task 0c (wt-ksh.5.11), and Task 6 (wt-ksh.5.18) added /complete-profile plus the dashboard guard, so a brand-new signup now lands on the profile form, creates its player row on submit, and reaches the dashboard where Create a Team works. Verified three ways: driven in a browser end to end, pinned by e2e/complete-profile.spec.ts, and pinned again by e2e/invites.spec.ts's full invite -> sign-in -> profile -> land-on-team path. The dead end this issue describes - reaching the dashboard anyway because getMyTeams returns [] rather than throwing, then getting NO_PLAYER rendered as 'Your session expired' - is gone: the guard redirects before the dashboard renders, and NO_PLAYER's copy was corrected to 'Finish setting up your profile'.

title: Task 12 — month-scoped Scoring System card and editor
description:
Plan task 12.

The card shows the system that governed the month currently in the URL - the same resolved system the scores table computes with, so the two can never disagree. A badge reads "In effect from Mon YYYY" when the month resolved to a version rather than the team's original values.

Customize is hidden when viewing a past month (a past month's rules are settled), when the viewer is not pro, and when they did not create the team. The first is a correctness rule; the other two are v1's gates, and like v1's they are UI-only.

Editor is Dialog on desktop, Sheet on mobile, as v1's CustomizeButton. Values are held as strings so a half-typed minus sign does not become 0.

The missed-day row is labelled "Missed day", NOT v1's "0". The schema field nA is a misnomer - v1's own card files it under "0 attempts" and it has nothing to do with the N/A shown for weekends. The schema field name is unchanged.

Files: v2/src/components/scoring-system-card.tsx (new), scoring-system-editor.tsx (new), v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

Step 5 of the plan is the acceptance walk and is the actual proof of wordle-teams-1j3.
acceptance_criteria: Editing the system in the current month leaves the previous month's displayed totals, row order and card values unchanged; the badge appears only on a historical month; Customize is absent on a past month, for non-pro and for non-creators; both themes screenshotted.
close_reason:
Done in 6af1865 (card + editor) and bdbf442 (review fixes). wordle-teams-1j3 is now visible to a user.

ACCEPTANCE WALK PASSED: July 2026 read Casey 5 / Robin 3. The system was then changed drastically in August — nA from 0 to -50, fail to -100 — and August recomputed to -900 each. July re-read UNCHANGED at Casey 5 / Robin 3, same order, no badge, no Customize button. Had versioning regressed, July's 28 unplayed days would each have shifted by -50.

CRITICAL BUG CAUGHT IN REVIEW: the plan specified inputMode='numeric' on the eight point inputs, which renders a digits-only keypad with no minus sign on iOS. Negative values are the entire feature — the DEFAULT system contains sixGuesses -1 and failed -3 — and the mobile Sheet exists specifically for phone users. v1 uses plain type='text' with no inputMode. Removed, with a comment so it is not re-added as an obvious mobile improvement. Not directly observable in headless chromium; verified that '-' and '-50' are accepted, round-trip through the server range check, and that out-of-range sets aria-invalid.

Also: the two eight-row label lists are now one exhaustiveness-checked Record<keyof ScoringSystem,string>, the [-100,100] bound is shared with requireValues, Save explains itself via aria-invalid plus a role=alert message, and the as-unknown-as cast is gone.

209 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: Task 10 — CurrentTeam card, member removal, team settings dialog
description:
Plan task 10.

The settings dialog ships in the SAME task as the Settings button that opens it. tsconfig has noUnusedLocals, so splitting them would leave this task with an unused settingsOpen local and a failing tsc.

Ports v1's current-team-client.tsx minus the Invite button (Phase 4). Settings and per-member remove are creator-only in the UI, and now also in the mutation. The creator's own row is filtered at the CALL SITE, so the card needs no knowledge of who the creator is.

The fix removes the race regardless.

title: Task 9 — team dropdown with create-team, and the upgrade swap
description:
Plan task 9.

title: Task 8 — resolve the scoring version per month, and setScoringSystem
description:
Plan task 8. The load-bearing task for wordle-teams-1j3.

TWO HALVES, AND HALF OF IT IS WORSE THAN NONE.

The read half: getTeamMonthFor returns systemFor(team, versions, month) plus systemEffectiveFrom for the badge, instead of the team's live values - without it the scores table computes a past month's totals under today's rules.

The write half: winners.ts resolves the version for each month it recomputes, and setScoringSystem upserts the row for the current month then recomputes that month and every later month with a winner row.

The submitter's local today is client-supplied and bounded to +/-1 day of the server's date, reusing upsertBoard's guard - it decides which month a version governs for the WHOLE TEAM, so an unbounded value is shared-state corruption, not a personal view quirk. See wordle-teams-04r: that Convex's clock is UTC is currently an inference, not an observation.

No pro check in the mutation, matching v1's save action.

Files: v2/convex/winners.ts, scores.ts, scores.test.ts, teams.ts, teams.test.ts.

Blocked by Tasks 1, 3, 4. THIS IS THE TASK MOST LIKELY TO GO WRONG - it looks correct until someone views a past month.
acceptance_criteria: Inverting the scoring system in the current month leaves the previous month's winner, its hasSeenCelebration and its resolved system unchanged, while the current month recomputes — proven by test, not by inspection.
close_reason:
Done in feca88a (both halves + 4 added tests) and 654e986 (review fixes: OCC overclaim corrected to match upsertBoardFor, SYSTEM_FIELDS derived from DEFAULT_SYSTEM so a new field cannot skip validation, accepted-bounds test, vacuous-assertion comment corrected, bandwidth-guard enumeration updated, loadTeamMonthSystem rename). 209 tests, tsc + build clean.

TWO FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING:
1. The plan's flagship test did NOT pin the write half. Reverting to 'system: team' left all 204 tests green — the test targets a current-month edit, so the previous month was protected by the month filter, not by version resolution. Reproduced by the controller. Only the implementer's added tests catch it; a second reviewer confirmed they also catch a hoisted-resolution failure mode.
2. The plan told the implementer to return the resolved system directly. systemFor returns the TEAM DOC on fallback, so that would have put invited (real emails, public repo) and creator on the wire for every team with no version rows. The implementer refused the instruction and kept the explicit eight-field pick.

title: Task 7 — removeMember recomputes every affected month
description:
Plan task 7. Divergence 5.

Removing a member recomputes EVERY month the team has a winner row for. v1's update_monthly_winners is a trigger on daily_scores and removing a player touches teams, so it never fires - a removed player stays named as the winner of months they are no longer in, and production is carrying stale rows today.

The creator cannot be removed, matching v1's UI which hides the button on your own row. Since only the creator can reach the mutation at all, that makes "remove yourself" unreachable rather than merely hidden - v1 has no leave-team affordance and neither does this.

The removed player's boards are untouched.

Files: v2/convex/teams.ts, teams.test.ts.

Blocked by Tasks 1, 4.
acceptance_criteria: The member is gone, the creator cannot be removed, every affected month's winner row is recomputed, and the removed player's boards survive — all by test.
close_reason: Done in 71b56d7 (mutation + tests) and e78d4fc (review fixes: silent no-op for a non-member, winnerOf docstring + test). Spec review constructed the partial-recompute failure case independently and confirmed the rewritten test goes red for the right reason. 197 tests, tsc + build clean. Note: the plan's original test premise was wrong — winnerOf returns null only for an empty candidate list, not an all-zero one.

title: Task 6 — createTeam, updateTeam, deleteTeam with a hand-written cascade
description:
Plan task 6.

createTeam writes DEFAULT_SYSTEM's eight values, creator, playerIds of just the caller, empty invited, createdAt, and NO legacyId. No server-side team cap - v1's is UI-only.

updateTeam recomputes every month with a winner row WHEN playWeekends FLIPS, and nothing otherwise. playWeekends is an input to monthTotal, so flipping it re-scores every month; a rename changes no total.

deleteTeam CASCADES BY HAND. Postgres has ON DELETE CASCADE on monthly_winners.team_id; Convex has nothing, so the monthlyWinners and scoringSystems rows go explicitly. dailyScores are NOT deleted - a board belongs to a player and is shared across every team they are on.

Files: v2/convex/teams.ts, teams.test.ts.

Blocked by Tasks 0, 3, 4.
acceptance_criteria: Create, update and delete proven; delete removes the team's winner and scoring-version rows and leaves its boards; a playWeekends flip recomputes; a non-creator member is refused on all three.
close_reason:
Done in 2d0eb51 (three mutations + cascade) and f023c77 (review fixes: no-recompute branch pinned by a stale-winner test, today bound extracted to isPlausibleToday in lib/puzzleDay.ts, empty-cascade test). Spec review confirmed the stale-team-doc test would genuinely catch a regression, the cascade's prefix index queries match every row, and cross-team isolation holds. 190 tests, tsc + build clean.

Side effect worth recording: sharing the today bound exposed that upsertBoard threw INVALID_BOARD for clock skew, rendering 'That board is not complete. Check the answer and your guesses.' to a user whose board was fine and whose clock was wrong. Shipped Phase 2 code; now throws INVALID_DATE.

title: Task 5 — convex/teams.ts, one widened getMyTeams
description:
Plan task 5.

getMyTeams moves out of scores.ts and grows members, creator flag and settings, so ONE subscription drives the picker, the CurrentTeam card and the MyTeams card. Plus amIPro for the two UI gates.

Splitting into a thin picker query and a scoped detail query would NOT be cheaper: the read set is the whole teams table either way, because Convex cannot index array membership.

Members exclude profile-incomplete players, matching getTeamMonthFor and the winner recomputation. Fields are picked explicitly so the wire payload cannot carry the invite list, which holds real email addresses.

Files: v2/convex/teams.ts (new), teams.test.ts (new), v2/convex/scores.ts, v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

Changes the dashboard loader, so pnpm e2e is mandatory.
acceptance_criteria: One query returns members, creator flag and settings for the caller's teams only; a non-member's team is absent; the invite list does not reach the wire; pnpm e2e green.
close_reason: Done in 206c32f (widened query) and e30d038 (review fixes: undefined-creator and zero-teams tests, hasCompleteProfile extracted to convex/lib/player.ts as a type predicate, three stale comments repointed). Spec review verified the invited-array never reaches the wire, the profile filter agrees across all three sites, and no api.scores.getMyTeams reference survives. 176 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: Task 4 — requireTeamCreator, isPro, and three typed error codes
description:
Plan task 4.

requireTeamCreatorFor throws NOT_A_MEMBER for a non-member (so a probe cannot distinguish "no such team" from "not yours" from "yours but not yours to edit") and NOT_TEAM_CREATOR for a member who is not the creator. isProFor reads playerMembership and is never enforced.

AccessCode gains NOT_TEAM_CREATOR, INVALID_TEAM and INVALID_SYSTEM, which BREAKS the exhaustive switch in src/lib/convex-error.ts until each has copy. That failure is the check doing its job - do not route around it.

Includes the edge case worth asserting rather than discovering: teams.creator is optional because a scoped copy may not include it, so a team whose creator was not copied has NOBODY who can edit it.

Files: v2/convex/access.ts, access.test.ts, v2/src/lib/convex-error.ts.

BLOCKS Tasks 6, 7, 8.
acceptance_criteria: A non-creator member is refused, a non-member is refused with a different code, and an uncopied-creator team is refused to everyone — all by test; tsc clean again.
close_reason: Done in 11a11b6 (helpers + codes) and 74a5b1c (review fixes: INVALID_TEAM split into INVALID_TEAM/INVALID_DATE/CREATOR_NOT_REMOVABLE, fixtures consolidated onto convex/fixtures.ts, typed-code assertions). Spec review verified all four authorization semantics: NOT_A_MEMBER for non-members with no information leak, undefined creator refused to everyone, accessError still throwing internally, isProFor true only for 'pro'. Guard and exhaustive switch both cover 9 codes. 168 tests, tsc + build clean.

title: Task 3 — scoringSystems table and lib/scoringSystem.ts
description:
Plan task 3. Part of wordle-teams-1j3.

New table keyed on (teamId, effectiveFrom). New dependency-free module exporting systemFor, effectiveFromOf and DEFAULT_SYSTEM.

Resolution is "the version with the greatest effectiveFrom <= month, else the base". The base is the team doc's own eight fields, which is what makes this need no backfill and no change to the copy script.

NO legacyId on the table, and that is not an oversight: it has no Supabase counterpart, so nothing is ever copied into it.

pointsFor, monthTotal and winnerOf are UNTOUCHED - they already take the system as a parameter.

Files: v2/convex/schema.ts, v2/convex/lib/scoringSystem.ts (new), scoringSystem.test.ts (new).

close_reason: Done in b05f173 (module + table) and c51069e (review fixes: total comparator, tie-break test, as-const DEFAULT_SYSTEM). Spec review verified resolution semantics, boundary inclusivity, year rollover, non-mutation of the caller's array, and systemFor/effectiveFromOf agreement. 162 tests, tsc + build clean. Note: the mid-task convex dev push was dropped from the plan — CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT is a local sqlite backend and convex-test is the real schema gate.

title: Task 2 — extract the dashboard search-param sync into a tested hook
description:
Plan task 2. Closes wordle-teams-lb9.

The effect in index.tsx navigates to fill in URL state while racing hydration - the classic infinite-redirect shape, and the highest-risk code in the Phase 2 UI. Phase 3 adds three cards to the same file.

The decomposition is the point: the DECISION comes out as a pure resolveDashboardSearch that needs no router, and the hook becomes a thin effect around it. The termination property then becomes a test rather than a comment - feed the function its own output and it must return null.

Files: v2/src/lib/dashboard-search.ts (new), dashboard-search.test.ts (new), use-dashboard-search-sync.ts (new), v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

Touches a route, so pnpm e2e is mandatory.

close_reason: Done in d67e29b (extraction) and 44a20ab (review fixes: stale cross-file comment, STORAGE_KEY consolidation, null-return doc, idempotency assertion). Spec review verified behaviour equivalence field by field and could not construct a looping input. 151 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: Task 1 — extract recomputeWinners into convex/winners.ts
description:
Plan task 1. Closes wordle-teams-4gj.

recomputeWinners is an unexported function inside scores.ts, reachable only by constructing a valid board submission and passing it through the whole validity and upsert machinery. Phase 3 calls it from three more mutations, so it moves out FIRST.

Four entry points: recomputeTeamMonth (the unit of work), recomputeTeamMonths, recomputePlayerMonth (what upsertBoard calls, behaviour unchanged), monthsWithWinners (what bounds the blast radius of a membership or scoring change).

THIS IS A PURE REFACTOR. The proof is that scores.test.ts passes untouched - if an assertion there needed editing, behaviour changed and the extraction is wrong.

Files: v2/convex/winners.ts (new), v2/convex/winners.test.ts (new), v2/convex/scores.ts.

close_reason: Done in 273196b (extraction) and 4816483 (review fixes: shared fixtures module, restored cost comment, WriterCtx export rationale, two test gaps). Spec review confirmed the extraction is behaviour-identical statement-by-statement and scores.test.ts assertions are untouched. 144 tests, tsc + build clean.

description:
Plan task 0. teams.legacyId is a required v.number(), and a team created natively in v2 has no Supabase primary key to carry, so createTeam cannot insert as the schema stands.

Same fix and same rationale as Phase 2's widening of dailyScores and monthlyWinners: the copy is unaffected because idempotency runs through by_legacyId and native rows correctly never match, and legacyId === undefined becomes the marker Phase 7's row-count reconciliation against Supabase needs.

Files: v2/convex/schema.ts, v2/convex/schema.test.ts.

BLOCKS Task 6.

close_reason: Done in dea05fb (schema + tests) and 2c1649e (fixture reuse after code review). NOTE: dea05fb's trailer says wt-ksh.4.2, an id invented in the plan before beads minted the real ones — not amended, since it is a shared branch and the trailer is cosmetic. Plan corrected in cee7727.

title: Verify live cross-player scoreboard update on beta (deferred from Phase 2)
description:
DEFERRED FROM PHASE 2 by owner decision, 2026-08-19. The only acceptance criterion of wt-ksh.3 not verified on beta.

Criterion 5 of the Phase 2 design: "A board entered in one browser updates another viewer's table WITHOUT a refresh." This is one of only two sanctioned departures from strict 1:1 parity with v1 (Convex reactivity making scoreboards live), so it is a headline feature rather than a nicety.

What IS verified on beta, by the owner:
 - a board entered on a copied account lands in the right cell with no refresh (single browser)
 - monthlyWinners rows are present and correct per team
 - month totals and row ordering match expectations

What is NOT verified: propagation to a DIFFERENT signed-in player's browser. The single-browser check proves the local mutation-to-query path; it does not prove the subscription pushes to other connected clients.

Deferred because it needs a second team with a second player to log in as, which Phase 2 cannot create — team creation is Phase 3 (wt-ksh.4) and invites are Phase 4 (wt-ksh.5). Attempting it in Phase 2 would have meant hand-seeding data on the deployment that becomes production.

DO THIS AT THE END OF PHASE 3, or Phase 4 if adding a second player to a team turns out to need the invite flow. Two browsers, two different signed-in players on one team: enter a board as A, confirm B's table updates with no refresh and no interaction.

Nothing in the repo covers this and nothing can — it needs two authenticated sessions against a real deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Two browsers, two different players, one team: a board entered by one appears in the other's table with no refresh.
close_reason:
AUTOMATED rather than observed once. v2/e2e/teams.spec.ts drives two independent Playwright browser contexts — separate storage state, two different signed-in players, one shared team seeded profile-complete via ensureSharedTeamFor. Player A enters a board; the assertion watches PLAYER A's cell as rendered on PLAYER B's page, with no page.reload() anywhere in B's path and no interaction with B between sign-in and the assertion.

Proven load-bearing rather than assumed: the implementer's first draft watched B's OWN row, which stays empty because B never plays — caught because the assertion timed out. Then, with the fixed version passing, they temporarily set B's context offline before A submits and confirmed the test fails identically. So it fails when reactivity is broken, not merely when something else changes.

Runs on every pnpm e2e. 8/8 green locally and in the deploy workflow.

Remaining for the owner: the same check against beta with two real browsers, as part of wt-ksh.4's side-by-side done-when.

title: Pinned columns drift while scrolling and row borders double — sticky vs border-collapse
description:
Two symptoms reported on beta, almost certainly ONE root cause.

SYMPTOM A: the pinned Player and Score columns move while scrolling horizontally and only settle into their sticky position after the gesture ends. They should never move at all.

SYMPTOM B: each player row appears to have both a top and a bottom border, so the line between rows is visibly thicker than the table's outer border.

HYPOTHESIS — position: sticky on table cells combined with border-collapse: collapse. Tailwind's preflight sets border-collapse: collapse on every table, and nothing here overrides it. That combination is long-broken across browsers: collapsed borders belong to the table's grid rather than to individual cells, so a sticky cell is repainted outside the normal flow and its borders escape the collapsed model. That produces exactly these two symptoms — late/jittery repositioning of the sticky cell, and a border rendered by the sticky cell IN ADDITION to the collapsed grid line, reading as a doubled row separator.

Compounding it: the pinned cells carry no z-index. scores-table.tsx sets `sticky left-0 bg-background` and `sticky right-0 bg-background` with no stacking context, so nothing guarantees they paint above the scrolling day cells.

PROPOSED FIX, to be verified rather than assumed:
 - border-separate + border-spacing-0 on the scores table
 - move the row border off <tr> and onto the cells, because a border on <tr> is ignored under border-collapse: separate — Tailwind's TableRow puts it on the row, so it will silently vanish otherwise
 - give the pinned cells an explicit z-index above the scrolling cells

Note this interacts with the earlier finding that the doubling was "entirely the currentColor border" (wt-ksh.3.12). That measurement was taken on DESKTOP chromium against a reproduction; the owner is reporting from a real device. Both can be true — the currentColor border made it far more visible, and a real doubling remains underneath.

VERIFY ON A REAL TOUCH VIEWPORT, and confirm both symptoms are gone, not just one.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned columns are stationary throughout a horizontal scroll, and the line between rows matches the table's outer border.
close_reason: Closed

title: Scores table still captures vertical touch scroll on mobile
description:
Reported on beta after the wt-ksh.3.13 fix: on mobile, dragging vertically with a finger inside the scores table scrolls the TABLE, not the page. No part of the table should scroll vertically.

wt-ksh.3.13 changed the Table primitive's wrapper from overflow-auto to overflow-x-auto, which was necessary but NOT sufficient, and the reason was already written down at the time. CSS refuses to pair a non-visible overflow-x with a visible overflow-y: setting overflow-x: auto silently coerces the COMPUTED overflow-y from visible to auto. That caveat is in the comment on ui/table.tsx. It was reasoned to be inert because nothing constrains the wrapper's height — which is true for LAYOUT, but not for TOUCH. A touch-capable element whose computed overflow-y is auto is still a scroll container as far as gesture handling is concerned, so it swallows the vertical drag instead of chaining it to the page.

FIX: set overflow-y explicitly to hidden rather than leaving it coerced. overflow-x: auto with overflow-y: hidden is a legal pair and stops the element being a vertical scroll target. Nothing gets clipped: the wrapper's height is auto and exactly matches the table's, so there is no vertical overflow to hide.

Consider overscroll-behavior-y: contain as belt-and-braces only if hidden proves insufficient — do not reach for it first, it treats the symptom.

Verify by actually dragging vertically at a mobile viewport with a touch-emulating context, not by reading computed styles: the computed value is the thing that misled the previous fix.
acceptance_criteria: A vertical drag starting inside the scores table scrolls the page, at a touch-emulating mobile viewport.
close_reason: Closed

title: E2E_TEST_MODE must be unset on the deployment that becomes production
description:
CUTOVER RISK. Same class as the wrangler.jsonc ENVIRONMENT issue.

Two public Convex mutations exist solely for e2e: testOtps.takeFor (pre-existing, Phase 0/1) and e2eSeed.ensureTeamFor (added Phase 2 task 9). Both are double-gated: process.env.E2E_TEST_MODE === 'true' AND the address matching /^e2e\+[^@]+@wordleteams\.com$/i. Neither can do anything without both.

The gating is sound. The risk is the deployment lifecycle around it.

E2E_TEST_MODE has to be set on whatever deployment the e2e suite runs against. The v2 design says the BETA Convex deployment BECOMES production at cutover — same project, same environment variables, DNS just flips. So if the variable is set on beta and nobody clears it, it is set on production the moment the domain moves.

With it set, anyone who can reach the deployment can mint an OTP for any e2e+*@wordleteams.com address and create a player and team. Bounded by the address pattern, so it cannot touch a real user's data — but it is a live unauthenticated write path in production.

Cutover checklist needs an explicit step: confirm E2E_TEST_MODE is UNSET on the production Convex deployment, and re-confirm after the final data copy. Consider also whether these two functions should be stripped at cutover rather than merely disabled.
acceptance_criteria: The Phase 8 cutover runbook has a step confirming E2E_TEST_MODE is unset on the production Convex deployment.
notes:
SHARPENED 2026-08-22 by the wordle-teams-96l fix. E2E_TEST_MODE surviving onto production now has a NEW and silent failure mode beyond the ones already recorded here.

convex/lib/e2e.ts's isE2eTraffic suppresses real mail for e2e+*@wordleteams.com addresses whenever the flag is 'true'. It guards BOTH senders: sign-in codes (auth.ts) and team invites (teams.ts). So if the flag survives cutover, then on production any address matching e2e+*@wordleteams.com:
  - never receives a sign-in code, and
  - never receives a team invitation,
with NO error raised anywhere - the invite is still parked in teams.invited and invitePlayer still reports success. The person simply never hears anything.

That domain is the product's own, so the population is small, but the failure is silent and indistinguishable from 'they ignored the email'.

The code comment in convex/lib/e2e.ts deliberately does NOT claim the flag is unset on production - an earlier draft did, citing this issue, which says the opposite. It now states the dependency and points here. Closing 7az is what makes that comment's production half true.

title: Phase 2: e2e smoke, beta verification and phase close
description:
One Playwright smoke test, not a suite, per the parent design. Extract the existing sign-in helper out of login.spec.ts into e2e/sign-in.ts so there is one definition, then login, enter a board, and assert the score lands. The dialog closing only on success means its disappearance is itself the assertion that the write landed. title: Phase 2: board entry with the keyboard-aware mobile sheet
description:
Ports v1's board entry AS IT STANDS ON dev, per amendment A3, not the version the 2026-07-16 design was written against. The three a335ae8 behaviours: handleSubmit wrapped in try/catch, setSubmitting(false) in finally so the form can never be left stuck, and the sheet closing ONLY on success (it used to close unconditionally and discard everything typed). The fourth, a warning toast when the winner update failed, is designed out rather than dropped, because the winner write now shares the mutation's transaction. Desktop Dialog and mobile top Sheet bound to the visual viewport, per the 2026-07-15 keyboard-aware sheet design: iOS Safari does not reflow a fixed panel when the keyboard opens and Radix locks body scroll, so without it the lower rows and Submit are unreachable. Adds shadcn popover and calendar for the date picker, which the design system does not cover; run the CLI from inside v2/.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop.md Task 8
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: Six guess rows reachable by finger-scroll at an iOS viewport with Submit pinned above the keyboard, and a failed submit leaves the sheet open with the typed board intact and the form not stuck submitting. Screenshotted.

Screenshot-verified (real Better Auth OTP login + temporary Convex seed, both cleaned up): desktop Dialog and mobile top Sheet, light+dark, board typed and colored correctly, forced-failure path confirmed sheet stays open / board intact / Submit re-enabled. Found and fixed two real bugs the toolchain missed: (1) form.tsx's scrollActiveRowIntoView used querySelector('#1-1') which throws (CSS ID selectors can't start with a digit) — crashed on every keystroke; (2) ui/sonner.tsx's <Toaster> was built but never mounted anywhere, so all toast calls app-wide were silent no-ops — mounted in __root.tsx. tsc/tests(118)/build all clean.

title: Phase 2: the month scores table
description:
The month grid. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 8 'Leaderboard table': horizontally scrolling grid in a rounded-md border, Player column pinned left and Score pinned right, both painted bg-background so rows slide underneath, rows sorted by month total descending, score bold and right-aligned. Hand-rolled on the shadcn table primitive rather than @tanstack/react-table, which v1 uses: this table never sorts, filters or paginates, and the pinning is plain sticky CSS that react-table plays no part in. Cell rules come from the existing scoreCell helper, already unit tested. Ports v1's player-name disambiguation: first name alone, 'First L' when two players share one, initials on mobile. Rendering only the days the month has means v1's getDayVisibility has no equivalent to port. No component test: the spec rules out a component-test suite for a 1:1 port.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop.md Task 7
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: Pinned columns paint over the scrolling days, and the X / 0 / N/A / blank rules all render correctly. Screenshotted in light and dark before being called done.

title: Phase 2: dashboard shell, day formatting, error mapping, team and month pickers
description:
Team and month live in the URL as search params, validated by the route. v1 kept them in a React context backed by localStorage and needed three separate hydration guards to stop the server and client disagreeing, and still shipped wordle-teams-uc5; search params cannot mismatch because both sides read the same URL. The current month is resolved from the browser clock in an effect after hydration, never during render, which is the 45e3cd6 lesson. localStorage still supplies the default team, applied post-mount via a replace navigation. Also: format-day.ts (Intl plus an ordinal helper, matching v1's 'EE do' and 'MMM yyyy' without adding date-fns), convex-error.ts mapping the typed ConvexError codes to user-facing copy, the read-only team picker, and the three-month picker. The pro expansion of the month window ships with the rest of the pro gate, not here.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: The URL drives team and month, a reload keeps the selection, and no hydration warning appears in the console. Ordinal and month-label formatting unit tested.

title: Phase 2: recompute monthly winners inside the score mutation
description:
The relocation of the update_monthly_winners Postgres trigger into the score mutation, in the same transaction as the board write. Recomputes for every team the submitting player belongs to, for that puzzleDay's month only. Two deliberate differences from the SQL: it derives the winner server-side rather than trusting a client-computed array, and hasSeenCelebration survives an unchanged winner instead of being wiped by the SQL's delete-and-reinsert, which would re-fire the confetti at someone who already dismissed it. No winner means any existing row is deleted, matching the SQL. Profile-incomplete players cannot win, matching their exclusion from the table. Blocked on the legacyId schema change.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop.md Task 5
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: convex-test proves a winner row per team, the highest total winning, ties broken as v1 breaks them, hasSeenCelebration preserved on an unchanged winner and reset on a changed one, and other months left alone.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2: upsertBoard keyed on (player, puzzleDay) so duplicates cannot recur
description:
upsertBoard keyed on (playerId, puzzleDay), which is what makes a duplicate row impossible. v1 keyed on a client-held score id and inserted whenever the client had none, so a double submit created a second row for the same day; it has already done so 5 times in production (wordle-teams-rac). The 5 copied pairs are left untouched and read first-wins, as v1 renders them. Empty answer and guesses with an existing row deletes. The mutation re-validates with the shared boardIsValid and throws INVALID_BOARD: unreachable through the UI, which disables submit on the same predicate, but v1 had no server-side validation at all. Blocked on the legacyId schema change.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop.md Task 4
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: Create, update and delete all proven, and a double submit yields exactly one row. An incomplete board and an empty board with no existing score are both refused.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2: team-and-month scoped read queries
description:
getTeamMonth scoped to one team and one month via a by_player_and_puzzleDay range query per member. v1 loaded every team, player and score ever into a client context; Convex re-pushes a query's whole result to every subscriber on every write, and wordle-teams-dcu flags database bandwidth, not function calls, as the binding free-tier limit. Also getMyTeams for the selector and getMyPlayerId so board entry can find the caller's own row without joining on name. Players without a completed profile are excluded, matching v1's getTeams, because a just-accepted invitee has no name and v1's fromDbPlayer throws on one.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop.md Task 3
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: A scoped month returns only that month's rows and only for team members, proven by convex-test. Team settings and the scoring system ride along for the table.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2: access-check helpers replacing the RLS policies
description:
convex/access.ts replaces the Supabase RLS policies, per the parent design's logic-relocation table. requirePlayer resolves the signed-in user's copied player by lowercased email, the same join me.ts uses. requireTeamMemberFor takes an explicit playerId and is what the tests exercise, so the negative cases can be proven against real documents without standing up a Better Auth session in convex-test; requireTeamMember is the thin wrapper the functions call. A missing team throws NOT_A_MEMBER too, so a probe cannot tell 'no such team' from 'not yours'.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop.md Task 2
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: convex-test proves a non-member is refused, an unauthenticated caller throws, and a deleted team is indistinguishable from a forbidden one.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2: pure day-string, board and scoring core shared by client and server
description:
Three dependency-free modules under v2/convex/lib/, imported by BOTH the browser and the Convex mutation so the scores table and the stored winner cannot disagree. puzzleDay.ts is arithmetic on YYYY-MM-DD strings. board.ts holds toRows, normalizeGuesses, attemptsFor and boardIsValid, ported from v1 utils.ts and the DailyScore class. scoring.ts holds pointsFor, monthTotal and winnerOf, ported from aggregateScoreByMonth and thisMonthsCurrentWinner. Two rules are load-bearing: attemptsFor must filter empty guesses because copied rows can carry v1's trailing sentinel, and winnerOf must compare with a strict > so the first player at the maximum wins a tie, as v1 does. pointsFor must be total and never throw, because it runs inside the board-entry transaction. src/lib/wordle.ts re-exports toRows rather than keeping its own copy.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop.md Task 1
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: vitest covers attempts including the trailing-sentinel case, points, month totals with missed days before today, weekends excluded when playWeekends is off, future days ignored, and tie-breaking. Suite green, tsc clean.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2: allow natively-created scores and winners to omit legacyId
description:
Schema prerequisite. dailyScores.legacyId and monthlyWinners.legacyId are required v.number(), because the schema was written for the Supabase copy where every row carries a primary key. Phase 2 is the first phase that creates rows natively and a board entered on beta has no Supabase identity, so upsertBoard cannot insert at all as things stand.

Widen both to v.optional(v.number()). Absence becomes meaningful: no legacyId means "born in v2, not copied", which is what Phase 7 row-count reconciliation needs. Leave the other four tables required.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: convex deploy accepts the schema and an insert without legacyId succeeds. Blocks the upsert and winner tasks.
