title: Polar P2d: rewrite webhook route for Polar
description:
Rewrite src/app/api/webhook/route.ts. Path stays /api/webhook (one provider, still accurate).

FLOW: (1) validateEvent(rawBody, headers, secret) from @polar-sh/sdk/webhooks; on WebhookVerificationError return 403. (2) playerId = event.data.customer.external_id. (3) If missing or not a UUID, log and return 202 NOT 500 - webhook_events.player_id is NOT NULL with an FK to players, so a foreign event would fail the insert and make Polar retry forever on something that can never succeed. (4) webhookId from the 'webhook-id' HEADER - Polar follows Standard Webhooks, so unlike LS's meta.webhook_id it is not in the body. Column is already text, no type change. (5) Store event; on unique-index conflict it is an already-handled retry, return 200. (6) Apply transition from P2b, run the RPC, mark processed.

Also delete src/lib/typeguards.ts outright - validateEvent returns discriminated typed events, so webhookHasMeta/webhookHasData have nothing left to guard. Update processWebhookEvent/storeWebhookEvent in src/app/me/actions.ts:292-397 accordingly, including deleting the per-webhook getFreeVariantId() API call.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a valid sandbox event updates player_customer and runs the right RPC; an invalid signature returns 403; a replayed webhook-id returns 200 without reprocessing; an event with an unknown external_id returns 202.
notes:
CORRECTION from j8c: the issue description says webhook_id is 'already text, no type change'. That was WRONG — the column was uuid (Lemon Squeezy's meta.webhook_id happened to be one, and database.types.ts renders uuid as string, which hid it). Migration 20260731120000 now converts it to text, verified locally. Standard Webhooks does not require UUIDs; the spec's own example id is msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W. Do NOT assume the header value parses as a UUID.

ALSO FROM j8c: gen-types moved OUT of j8c and into ymy. Regenerating database.types.ts breaks typecheck in utils.ts:107-108, me/page.tsx:41, and app-bar-server.tsx:31-33, and fixing those is ymy's type-ripple scope. j8c therefore shipped SQL only, keeping the repo green.

The unique index is PARTIAL (where webhook_id is not null), so legacy rows with a null webhook_id are exempt. A duplicate non-null webhook_id raises a unique violation on insert — catch that specifically and return 200, since it means an already-handled retry.
close_reason: Webhook route rewritten for Polar; also closed the server-action escalation path, proven via the build manifest

title: Polar P2c: checkout and portal modules
description:
Create src/lib/polar/checkout.ts with createProCheckout(playerId, email, name) -> checkout URL, and src/lib/polar/portal.ts with getCustomerPortalUrl(playerId).

Checkout uses POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID directly (replacing the current listProducts + .find(p => p.attributes.name === 'Pro') name lookup, deleting an API round-trip per checkout and a fragile string match). Sets external_customer_id = playerId, prefills customer email/name, and sets success_url to /me?checkout=success on the environment-appropriate origin (the existing url ternary in src/lib/lemonsqueezy/index.ts:14-20 has the right shape).

Portal creates a customer session via external_customer_id rather than a stored Polar customer UUID - this is what lets player_customer.customer_id be dropped entirely. Portal URLs are short-lived, so always generate fresh at click time, never store.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: both functions return usable URLs against Polar sandbox, and the portal path never reads a customer id from the database.
notes:
Done. src/lib/polar/checkout.ts (createProCheckout) and src/lib/polar/portal.ts (getCustomerPortalUrl). client.ts gained proProductIds() returning [annual, monthly] and appOrigin(); POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID replaced by the monthly/annual pair.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: portal.ts first matched a missing customer with 'error instanceof ResourceNotFound'. That check can NEVER match. The SDK only raises its typed error classes for responses declared in the OpenAPI spec, and customerSessions.create does not declare a 404 — it throws the generic SDKError. Probing the SDK with a stubbed 404 confirmed: 'THREW SDKError', not ResourceNotFound. Shipped as written, every player who had never checked out would have been told to try again later, forever, for a condition retrying can never fix. Now matched on 'error instanceof PolarError && error.statusCode === 404'. PolarError is the base of both classes and carries statusCode, so it holds whichever a future SDK version throws.

getCustomerPortalUrl returns a discriminated PortalResult ({url} | {url:null,reason:'no-customer'} | {url:null,reason:'error'}) so ymy's UI can say something true instead of a generic retry message. no-customer logs at info, not error — it is an expected state, not a fault.

appOrigin() follows the VERCEL_URL convention from src/lib/auth-urls.ts rather than the hardcoded ENVIRONMENT ternary the Lemon Squeezy module used. Noted in a comment as worth consolidating with auth-urls.ts if a third caller appears.

Verified: tsc clean, pnpm build exits 0, pnpm lint adds no warnings, and 22 assertions pass by intercepting fetch — asserting the exact request body Polar receives (both products, annual first, external_customer_id, no customer UUID, success_url, return_url), every failure branch, the log levels, and that neither module imports supabase. Live URL round-trip deferred to P3 (8sg), which has been updated.
close_reason: Checkout and portal modules landed; caught an unreachable error branch that would have broken the billing portal for all non-subscribers

title: Polar P2a: add @polar-sh/sdk and client module
description: Add @polar-sh/sdk dependency. Create src/lib/polar/client.ts exporting a configured SDK client whose server is derived from ENVIRONMENT: 'prod' -> production, everything else -> sandbox (mirroring the existing testMode pattern in src/lib/lemonsqueezy/index.ts). Validate POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET, POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID are present, following the existing configureLemonSqueezy() missing-vars pattern. Do NOT add @polar-sh/nextjs - its Webhooks helper auto-acknowledges, which would lose the store-then-process-then-500-so-Polar-retries behavior the webhook route depends on.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: client module builds, typechecks, and throws a clear error naming any missing POLAR_* env var.
notes: FOLLOW-UP applied in 19s: POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID was replaced by POLAR_PRO_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID and POLAR_PRO_ANNUAL_PRODUCT_ID, and proProductId() became proProductIds(). Polar has no variants, so Pro monthly and Pro annual are two separate products and checkout offers both in one session. The lazy-memoized client and the env validation pattern this issue established are unchanged.
close_reason: Client module landed and verified; build, typecheck, lint, and 13 runtime assertions pass

title: Polar P2b: pure event-mapping module
description:
Create src/lib/polar/events.ts with mapEventToTransition(eventType) -> { status, rpc } | null. Pure function, no I/O, no Supabase, no network - it holds the only real logic in the integration and is the unit most worth verifying independently.

MAPPING (see epic for why cancel != revoke):
  subscription.active     -> pro,     rpc: upgrade
  subscription.uncanceled -> pro,     rpc: upgrade (no-op if already pro)
  subscription.canceled   -> null     (NO CHANGE - access paid through period end)
  subscription.past_due   -> null     (NO CHANGE - recoverable)
  subscription.revoked    -> expired, rpc: downgrade

revoked maps to 'expired' unconditionally; distinguishing 'cancelled' would cost a payload branch and nothing reads the difference - only 'pro' gates anything.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: every one of the five subscribed event names returns the mapping above, and an unknown event name returns null rather than throwing.
notes:
Done. src/lib/polar/events.ts exports mapEventToTransition(eventType), ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENTS, and the MembershipTransition / MembershipRpc types. rpc values are the literal Postgres function names (handle_upgrade_team_invites / handle_downgrade_team_removal) so P2d has no indirection to resolve.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: the first implementation used Record<string, ...>, whose lookup walks the prototype chain. mapEventToTransition('toString') returned Object.prototype.toString (a Function) and '__proto__' returned {} — both truthy, both violating the documented 'unknown yields null' contract, and both would have reached P2d as a truthy transition with an undefined status, producing a database write of undefined membership_status. Not exploitable, since event types arrive inside signature-validated Polar payloads, but the contract was wrong. Switched to a Map, which has no prototype chain. Also froze the shared GRANT/REVOKE objects: both grant events return the same object, so an unfrozen result let a caller mutating one silently corrupt the other.

CROSS-CHECK WORTH REPEATING IN P2D: the verification reads the 37 event-type string literals straight out of @polar-sh/sdk's payload .d.ts files and asserts every acknowledged name exists among them. This specifically guards the British 'subscription.cancelled' typo, which is easy to write here because the app's own member_status enum uses 'cancelled' while Polar's event is 'subscription.canceled'.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, pnpm build exits 0, pnpm lint adds no warnings, and 26 assertions pass covering the five mapped events, seven unknown names, four prototype keys, the SDK cross-check, ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENTS contents, and the freeze behavior.
close_reason: Event mapping landed and verified; 26 assertions pass, prototype-chain bug found and fixed during verification

title: Polar P1: dashboard + Vercel env setup (owner task)
description:
Owner-executed. Full runbook: docs/plans/2026-07-31-polar-phase1-setup.md. Create sandbox org at sandbox.polar.sh and production org at polar.sh (separate instances, separate tokens). Pro product in each matching current LS Pro price. Org access tokens with checkout/customer-session/customer/product permissions. Webhook endpoints in Raw format subscribed to subscription.active, .uncanceled, .canceled, .revoked, .past_due. Six Vercel env vars (POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET, POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID across Production and Preview scopes).

LEAD TIME RISK: Polar reviews orgs before enabling live payments. Submit the production org for review FIRST since it gates prod verification.

DEV WEBHOOK GOTCHA: dev.wordleteams.com is behind Vercel Deployment Protection and would silently block Polar webhooks. Sandbox webhook URL must carry the automation bypass secret as a query param: https://dev.wordleteams.com/api/webhook?x-vercel-protection-bypass=SECRET. That URL contains a secret and this repo is PUBLIC - dashboard and Vercel env only, never committed.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: both Pro products exist at matching prices, all six Vercel env vars set, both webhook endpoints registered with the five events in Raw format, and production org review submitted.
notes:
COMPLETE. Verified independently: all four POLAR_* variables present in Vercel under both Production and Preview scopes with the corrected monthly/annual names, and the sandbox webhook endpoint is registered at https://dev.wordleteams.com/api/webhook with the bypass query param, format=raw, and the five subscribed events. Sandbox products resolve with the right recurring intervals (Pro Monthly = month, Pro Annual = year). A real sandbox checkout completed and its webhook was delivered. Note the variables were created as SENSITIVE, so 'vercel env pull' returns [SENSITIVE] placeholders. That is fine for the deployed app but means local dev cannot obtain them that way; the values were already present in .env.local. Consider un-marking the two PRODUCT_ID vars, which are not secrets and appear in checkout URLs anyway. One cosmetic follow-up split out as its own issue: both product descriptions contain literal HTML that renders as visible

tags on the checkout page.
close_reason: Dashboard and env setup verified working end to end via a real sandbox checkout

title: EPIC: Migrate billing from Lemon Squeezy to Polar.sh
description:
Full spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-polar-migration-design.md. Owner runbook for dashboard setup: docs/plans/2026-07-31-polar-phase1-setup.md. Branch: feat/polar-migration.

WHY NOW: Polar cannot import active subscriptions from Lemon Squeezy (polar-migrate moves products/customers/discounts only). Every paying customer must re-subscribe by hand, so the cost scales with subscriber count and is at its minimum at one paying customer.

KEY DECISIONS: (1) Hard cutover, LS removed entirely in one release. (2) No Polar Free product; 'free' is a DB default, never webhook-driven. (3) external_customer_id = player_id, so Polar customer UUID is never stored, which lets player_customer.customer_id AND membership_variant both be DROPPED rather than retyped int->uuid. (4) Downgrade on subscription.revoked ONLY, never on subscription.canceled, because Polar splits cancel-scheduled from access-ended and a literal port would strip a paying customer's teams weeks early. (5) Hosted redirect checkout, no third-party script, which also removes the DNS-filter failure mode lemon.js has. (6) Customer email held until dev is verified so cutover is a deploy, not a project.

OUT OF SCOPE: polar-migrate tooling; the three Postgres RPCs (handle_upgrade_team_invites, handle_downgrade_team_removal, handle_free_team_limit) which branch on membership_status='pro' and stay untouched by design; the two untracked scripts/*-dev.mjs files in the working tree.

HIGHEST RISK: the migration must 'create or replace' custom_access_token_hook BEFORE dropping player_customer.customer_id and membership_variant, in the same file. Dropping first makes the hook throw and breaks EVERY login. This project already has a login-lockout incident in its history.
acceptance_criteria: 1. New user completes Polar checkout and lands on /me as pro without manual refresh. 2. subscription.revoked downgrades player and removes teams beyond free limit. 3. subscription.canceled alone does NOT change membership_status or remove teams. 4. Existing pro user can open Polar customer portal from user dropdown. 5. Login works after auth hook migration, verified on dev before prod. 6. No Lemon Squeezy reference remains in codebase or Vercel env vars. 7. Duplicate webhook deliveries are idempotent (repeated webhook-id returns 200 without reprocessing).
notes:
POST-CUTOVER BEHAVIOUR CONFIRMED 2026-08-03. Nothing revokes membership_status any more.

Lemon Squeezy webhooks can no longer be processed: /api/webhook validates Polar Standard Webhooks signatures, and an LS payload carries X-Signature instead, so every delivery is rejected 403 before touching the database. Demonstrated in production — 18 rejected deliveries in 33 seconds after an at-period-end cancellation, with webhook_events unchanged at 136 rows.

This is intended for the grace period and means no subscriber loses access during the switch. The corollary is that the grace period has no automatic end, so the paying customer must be downgraded by hand if they never convert; tracked in wordle-teams-g3k, deferred to 2026-09-05. Once a subscriber is on Polar, their lifecycle is automatic again.

Also note the two owner-controlled accounts now sit at 'pro' permanently and free. Deliberate, but it means 'pro' in the database no longer implies a paying subscriber — read it with care.
close_reason: All 11 child tasks complete and Polar is live in production. Acceptance criteria 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 verified (event mapping, auth hook rewrite 14/14 against prod Supabase, no Lemon Squeezy in code or Vercel env, webhook idempotency). Criteria 1 and 4 verified against the Polar sandbox API but not yet with a real production payment, because there are no Polar subscribers — tracked in wordle-teams-7xl rather than left implicit. Remaining Lemon Squeezy store closure is deferred in wordle-teams-0sl; manual downgrade of the unconverted customer is deferred in wordle-teams-g3k.

title: Hydration error + streaming-reveal crash on /me in production (muted in Sentry, 9 users)
description:
Two Sentry issues on the board page that are almost certainly one root cause. Both are PRODUCTION (vercel-production, https://wordleteams.com/me), not dev:

  6804715751  'Hydration Error'                            449 events,  9 users, status IGNORED, last 2026-07-27
  7103187406  TypeError: null is not an object (b.parentNode)  312 events, 2 users, last 2026-07-12

9 users is the second-highest user count in the whole project, behind only the login lockout (wordle-teams-jvt). The sampled events are Mobile Safari / iPhone (iOS 18.7).

The b.parentNode stack is 'app:///me:2 in $RS'. $RS is React's inline streaming-reveal helper (completeBoundary), which moves content out of a hidden template div into a resolved Suspense slot. A null parentNode means the target node was already detached when the boundary resolved — the classic downstream symptom of a hydration mismatch causing React to discard and re-render server HTML. Same page, same environment, same platform as the hydration error, so treat them as one bug until proven otherwise.

WHY THIS WAS MISSED: issue 6804715751 is set to IGNORED in Sentry, so it does not appear in any 'is:unresolved' query — which is how the 2026-07-30 triage pass enumerated issues. It only surfaced when the issues endpoint was queried with an empty status filter. Muted issues need a periodic explicit sweep.

Note the sibling issue 6809975309 ('Cannot read properties of null (parentNode)', 1070 events) is NOT this bug — its events are vercel-preview / dev.wordleteams.com, i.e. dev noise. Do not spend time on it.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce on iOS Safari against production /me and identify the hydration mismatch (likely a date/locale/timezone-dependent render, a Math.random or Date.now in render, or a client-only value used during SSR — the board is date-driven, so suspect date formatting first). Fix the mismatch, then un-ignore 6804715751 in Sentry and confirm the event rate drops to zero.
notes:
FILTER APPLIED 2026-08-17 (2c088d4 on fix/signup-activation), NOT yet deployed.

Chose to drop the event rather than change behaviour, because nothing user-visible is broken and the cost was purely a buried signal. src/lib/sentry-filters.ts holds the predicate — extracted from sentry.client.config.ts so it can be exercised without initialising Sentry and without a DSN, which also means no test traffic reaches the real project.

The predicate requires BOTH a React bootstrap frame (function $RS/$RC/$RX/$RB, or a document-only frame matching ^app:///[^/]*:\d+$) AND a message containing 'parentNode'. Matching on the substring rather than a full string is deliberate: V8 says "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'parentNode')", JavaScriptCore "null is not an object (evaluating 'b.parentNode')", Firefox "b.parentNode is null".

Verified with 10 cases against real event shapes, all passing. The negative cases are the ones that matter:
  KEPT: a genuine parentNode TypeError from a bundle frame (app:///_next/static/chunks/...)
  KEPT: the Hydration Error, which is not a TypeError — wt-dyp depends on it still reporting
  KEPT: an unrelated TypeError even from an $RS-named frame
  KEPT: events with no exception, and message-only events
Also confirmed the filter is actually in the shipped client bundle (its DOCUMENT_FRAME regex appears in main-app), since resolving '@/lib/...' from a root-level config file was the one real risk.
pnpm lint clean, pnpm build passes.

KNOWN TRADE-OFF: replaysOnErrorSampleRate is 1.0, so these errors were reliably pulling in a session replay for /me — which is exactly how this was diagnosed. Dropping the event removes that trigger. replaysSessionSampleRate stays at 0.1, so /me replays keep arriving, just fewer. If wt-dyp needs more of them, raise the session rate temporarily rather than reverting this.

HOW TO VERIFY AFTER DEPLOY: do NOT use issue lastSeen or event counts — error events are being dropped upstream of us (replays report count_errors 0 and the referenced events 404), which is what made this look dormant since 2026-07-27. Instead confirm both halves:
  1. No new events on 6809975309 with a release at or after this deploy.
  2. Production /me replays with op 'navigation.back_forward' STILL appear, proving the trigger still occurs and we suppressed reporting rather than accidentally suppressing traffic.
Read replays with: SENTRY_READ_TOKEN=$SENTRY_WRITE_TOKEN node scripts/sentry-query.mjs raw "projects/christian-white/wordle-teams/replays/<id>/recording-segments/?download=true"

REMAINS OPEN under this issue: nothing. The hydration mismatch and the double document load moved to wt-dyp. Close uc5 once the two checks above hold.

title: PII: real user emails are committed to the PUBLIC repo in .beads/issues.jsonl
description:
github.com/cdub615/wordle-teams is PUBLIC (confirmed via gh repo view). .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked, so every issue body is published. Real user email addresses and first names were reaching that file, including a school-domain address and a corporate one.

DECISION 2026-07-30 (owner): scrub forward only. Existing git history is left as-is — no rewrite, no force-push. The owner's own address in the beads 'owner' field is intentionally retained; only third-party user data is removed.

DONE: all third-party emails and names in the beads DB replaced with stable pseudonyms (invitee-1..invitee-7, owner-alt-account) at redacted.invalid, so distinct people stay distinguishable without being identifiable. One-off prod remediation scripts that hardcode addresses are gitignored via scripts/*-prod.mjs.

STILL TRUE: the pre-scrub addresses remain reachable in published git history and may be indexed or mirrored. Anyone who needs them for debugging should read them from the prod DB, never from the repo.
acceptance_criteria: Adopt the convention that issue bodies reference users by player id, team id, or pseudonym — never by email or real name. Add a pre-commit hook that fails when an email pattern other than the owner's appears in .beads/issues.jsonl or docs/, so this cannot regress.
notes: Scrub script kept at scratchpad/scrub-pii.mjs (dry-run by default). A full pre-scrub backup bundle of all refs is at scratchpad/backup/wordle-teams-pre-scrub.bundle in case any redaction needs reversing. Remaining follow-up: the pre-commit hook is not yet written.
close_reason: Closed

title: Login conversion: 163 human visitors reached /login in 30d, ~7% completed auth
description:
Axiom prod funnel, 2026-06-30..2026-07-30 (30d, the full retention window):

 /login GET 163 unique non-bot IPs, 317 hits
 /login POST 4 unique IPs, 9 requests <- login/signup server action submissions
 /api/auth/callback 8 unique IPs, 14 requests (12 OAuth 'code', 1 invite token_hash, 1 provider error)

So ~163 real people reached the sign-in screen and roughly 12 completed an auth round-trip. Crucially there are ZERO server-side auth failures in the window: no 'Failed to verify OTP', no 'Failed to exchange code for session', no 'Failed to sign in', no 5xx anywhere. The auth backend works. All 6 OAuth providers were verified live against prod Supabase (google, twitter, azure, github, slack, discord) — every one 302s correctly to its provider. People are abandoning at the login screen, not hitting errors.

The email path is nearly unused: only 4 IPs ever submitted the email form in 30 days, and 12 of 14 callbacks were OAuth codes. src/app/login/page.tsx:32 shows OAuthSignin first — a 3x2 grid of six icon-only buttons whose labels exist only as sr-only text plus a hover Tooltip (src/app/login/oauth/oauth-provider.tsx:50-67). Tooltips do not appear on tap, and the heaviest login-page traffic is iPhone (105 hits / 22 IPs). Unlabeled icons on mobile is the leading hypothesis for the abandonment, but the logs cannot prove intent — this needs instrumentation, not more log reading.
acceptance_criteria: Add client-side funnel events for login-page view, provider-button click, and callback arrival so abandonment can be attributed. Then test labeled provider buttons (visible text, not tooltip-only) against the current icon grid and measure completion rate.
notes:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-17. Axiom, production, last 30d (2026-07-18..08-17), bots filtered on user agent:
  /login GET             981 hits, 203 unique IPs
  /login POST             34 hits,   6 unique IPs
  /api/auth/callback      56 hits,  16 unique IPs
Against the original window (2026-06-30..07-30): GET 317 hits/163 IPs, POST 9/4, callback 14/8.

Traffic is up — 163 to 203 people reaching the sign-in screen — and conversion is not: roughly 16 of 203 complete an auth round-trip, about 8% against the original ~7%. The leak is unchanged.

THIS IS STILL A PRE-FIX BASELINE. origin/main is f476605, the 2026-08-03 release, so production has NONE of the 2026-08-14..17 work. wt-odh (OTP form could submit with no code), wt-3io (a first-time visitor on the default Log In tab was told they had failed) and wt-4ov are merged into dev only. Re-measure after a dev -> main release before drawing conclusions about whether they moved anything.

CAVEATS on the numbers, so they are not over-read: unique IP is a rough proxy for people — mobile networks rotate addresses and households share one — so 203 is not 203 individuals. The bot filter is a user-agent heuristic and differs from whatever the original measurement used, so the two windows are not perfectly comparable. Callback hits mix OAuth code exchanges with invite token_hash links.

The original finding still stands and is the important one: there are no server-side auth failures in the window. People are leaving the sign-in screen without hitting an error, which makes this friction and trust rather than a bug — and it is a bigger leak than activation (93% here versus 87% at 456).

title: Middleware never ran in production — root-level middleware.ts is ignored when using src/
description:
CORRECTED 2026-07-30. This issue was originally filed as 'middleware runs on every request incl. static assets, causing 2.4s cold starts'. That premise was WRONG. Middleware was not running at all.

ROOT CAUSE: this project uses a src/ directory, so Next resolves middleware at src/middleware.ts. A root-level middleware.ts is silently ignored — no warning, no build error. Proof:
  - the production build emitted "middleware": {} in .next/server/middleware-manifest.json, with no middleware bundle on disk and sortedMiddleware: []
  - against live prod, a signed-out GET https://wordleteams.com/me returned 200 with no redirect (it should 307 to /login)
  - moving the file to src/middleware.ts immediately produced 'ƒ Middleware 132 kB' in the build and the correct matcher list

WHAT WAS SILENTLY BROKEN THE WHOLE TIME:
  1. Maintenance mode. Flipping maintenance_prod in Edge Config did nothing; the rewrite never executed. Never tested, because it never worked.
  2. The welcome-path redirect (signed-in user on / or /login -> /me). The comment in src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts:5-7 says this is specifically what keeps an installed PWA from opening on the welcome screen — so that bug is live for PWA users.
  3. Auth cookie refresh on every request. Plausible contributor to the forced logouts in wordle-teams-io0: without middleware refreshing the session, tokens age out and users get 'Invalid Refresh Token'.

NOT a security hole: every protected page does its own server-side check (src/app/me/page.tsx:31 redirects when !hasSession), so the middleware redirect was belt-and-braces, not the only gate.

THE ORIGINAL PERFORMANCE CLAIM IS UNEXPLAINED. /home 2421ms, /privacy 2258ms, /terms 2159ms, robots.txt 911ms are real measurements, but middleware cannot be the cause. The lambda invocations on robots.txt / sitemap.xml / manifest.json are their own route handlers (src/app/robots.ts, sitemap.ts, manifest.ts). For /privacy and /terms the likely explanation is a cold Next server handling a CDN miss on a prerendered page. That needs a separate investigation — see the follow-up issue.
acceptance_criteria: Middleware executes in production: a signed-out request to /me returns 307 to /login, and toggling maintenance_prod in Edge Config actually serves the maintenance page. Marketing and legal pages and static assets produce no middleware invocation. Neither an Edge Config outage nor a Supabase outage can 500 a matched route.
notes: Fixed on branch fix/middleware-cold-starts. The move is paired with two deliberate changes: (a) the matcher is now an allowlist of /, /login, /me, /branding, /complete-profile rather than a near-catch-all, so enabling middleware does not add invocations to marketing pages; (b) both halves fail open in try/catch, because this is middleware's production debut and every page behind it self-protects. Verified locally: matched routes 307 correctly, unmatched routes untouched, zero errors.
close_reason: Shipped to production 2026-07-30 (main c36d4b1, via dev da0c11d). Verified live: signed-out GET /me, /branding, /complete-profile now 307 to /login — previously 200 with no redirect because middleware never ran. Unmatched routes (/, /login, /home, /privacy, /terms, /about, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, manifest.json) all 200 and untouched. Login page re-verified in a real browser with lemon.js both allowed and blocked: still PASS, so no regression to wordle-teams-jvt. Maintenance mode and the PWA welcome redirect are now functional for the first time — neither has ever been exercised in prod, so watch for surprises. The original 2.2s cold-start claim was misdiagnosed and is split out to its own issue.

title: Activation funnel: 87% of prod signups never enter a single board
description:
Prod data (2026-07-30, scripts/prod-activity-report.mjs): 526 players and 171 teams exist, but only 68 players have ever written a daily_scores row with non-empty guesses. 458 accounts (87%) signed up and never entered one board.

Of the 68 who did enter, 50 are outside Christian's teams and 40 of those 50 entered only 1-2 boards ever, then stopped. Only one independent team ever showed sustained multi-user usage: team 55 (5 players, 39-92 entries each, churned 2025-05-02). Current daily volume is 3-7 entries/day, essentially all from Christian's 6 teams.

This is the same population affected by the invite->join bug (epic wordle-teams-c0v): invitees who could not join the inviter's team would appear as a player row with zero scores, which is exactly this signature. Need to determine what share of the 458 zero-score accounts are invite-flow casualties vs. ordinary signup churn before concluding the invite fix addresses it.
acceptance_criteria: Bucket the 458 zero-score players by origin (invited vs. self-signup) and by whether they ever landed in a team's player_ids. Report what share is attributable to the invite bug fixed in 15d1edb vs. other causes.
notes:
2026-08-24 — two fresh signups traced end-to-end (DB + Axiom + Sentry). Both reproduce the zero-score signature, and neither is an invite-flow casualty or an error:

Signup A (10:04:15Z, Google OAuth, Android/Chrome Mobile, UK IP):
  auth row, players row, and team created within 97s. Team has 1 member (self), invited=[]. Zero daily_scores. Session ran 10:04-10:12 across /login /me /home /about, every request 200, plus a brief return at 12:22Z. Only Sentry event in the window is the next-axiom vitals crash (wordle-teams-zkw), which did not block anything.

Signup B (13:56:01Z, Google OAuth, UK IP):
  /login -> /api/auth/callback 307 -> /me -> /complete-profile -> POST /complete-profile 200 -> /me -> /home. Filled in the profile form (first/last name are user-supplied in user_metadata, not Google's). Then stopped: last request 13:56:21Z, ~20s after landing. NO team created, NO team joined, invited=[] nowhere, zero daily_scores, and no return visit in the 3h since. Zero 4xx/5xx anywhere in the session; zero Sentry events.

So B's whole lifetime in the product was 39 seconds and ended on a team-less screen. This is consistent with the 2026-08-17 correction above — the screen does have a 'Create a Team' CTA, so the loss is not a missing call to action — but it narrows the question: the account survives auth and profile completion and then dies at the create-or-join-a-team step, before any board UI is ever reachable.

Corroborating pattern in the teams table — 6 of the 8 most recently created teams have exactly 1 member and invited=[]:
  211 2026-08-24 (signup A), 210 2026-08-19, 209 2026-08-14, 207 2026-07-28, 205 2026-07-07, 204 2026-06-29, 203 2026-06-23. Only 208 (2026-08-05, 3 members) is not solo.

That is the sharper framing for the bucketing work in the acceptance criteria: the dominant zero-score shape is not 'invited and could not join' but 'signed up, made a team of one, invited nobody, never entered a board' — a solo team has no leaderboard and nothing to come back for. Worth bucketing the 458 against this third category explicitly, not just invited-vs-self-signup.

title: Nameless just-joined invitee crashes team render (fromDbPlayer throws) + broken complete-profile gate
description:
Exposed by the now-working invite flow (wordle-teams-c0v). When an invitee accepts, handle_invited_signup adds them to teams.player_ids immediately, but first_name is null until they complete their profile.

Bug 1 (gate no-op): src/app/me/utils.ts:18 'if (!hasName(supabase))' is not awaited -> always false -> getTeams returns hasName:true always -> page.tsx:32 never redirects nameless users to /complete-profile.
Bug 2 (crash): src/lib/types.ts:138-139 fromDbPlayer throws on null first/last name; getTeams includes all player_ids members incl. the profile-incomplete invitee -> client TeamsProvider crash rendering the team. Hits invitee AND teammates viewing during the window.

Evidence (dev sgrx): team 43 'Test' player_ids includes 25eeb807 (owner-alt-account@redacted.invalid) with first_name=null; invited[] empty (invite join succeeded).

Fix: (1) await/derive hasName in getTeams so incomplete-profile users route to /complete-profile; (2) filter profile-incomplete players out of each team's rendered players in getTeams (reappear after they complete profile), so teammates don't crash.
acceptance_criteria: Invitee clicking invite link is routed to complete-profile, sets name, then sees the team; a teammate viewing a team with a not-yet-completed invitee does not crash.
close_reason: Fixed: getTeams filters profile-incomplete players + awaits name gate; app/page.tsx awaits hasName. Validated against dev team 43.

title: Invited teammates land on empty state and can only create a team, not join inviter's team
description:
Reported by user invitee-6@redacted.invalid: created team team 206, invited people; when invitees click the email link they can only create a new team instead of seeing team 206 and entering their Wordle board.

Invite/join path (v1 app, dev branch):
- invitePlayer (src/app/me/actions.ts): for new email -> supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail(email,{data:{invited:true}}) + appends email to teams.invited[].
- Invitee clicks link -> /api/auth/callback -> finishSignIn (src/lib/utils.ts) -> handleInvite gates on user.user_metadata.invited===true -> rpc handle_invited_signup(invited_email,invited_id).
- handle_invited_signup (migration 20240517174331) appends invited_id to player_ids for teams WHERE invited_email = ANY(invited), removes from invited, sets user_metadata.invited=false.

Leading hypotheses (need DB/Sentry evidence to confirm):
- B: invitee authenticated via OAuth (Google) instead of clicking the emailed invite link, so the account they use lacks invited:true metadata -> handleInvite never runs.
- E: email case/whitespace mismatch between teams.invited[] entry and auth user email -> WHERE invited_email = ANY(invited) matches nothing.
- A: invitee already had an account -> inviteUserByEmail path differs.

Next: read-only prod query of teams.invited/player_ids for team 206 + auth.users metadata/providers for invitees; check Sentry for handle_invited_signup errors.
design:
Proposed fix (route invite through the callback via token_hash path the app already supports):
1. Pass redirectTo to both inviteUserByEmail calls: `/api/auth/callback?next=/me`.
2. Update Supabase INVITE email template (prod dashboard) to: {{ .SiteURL }}/api/auth/callback?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=invite&next=/me (uses handleEmailSignin/verifyOtp token_hash path; no PKCE code_verifier needed).
3. Ensure prod Site URL + additional_redirect_urls include app domain and /api/auth/callback.
Regression test: e2e - invitePlayer -> GET callback token_hash&type=invite -> assert redirect /me, player_ids contains invitee, invited[] cleared, user_metadata.invited=false; unit - assert inviteUserByEmail called with redirectTo.
Data remediation (after fix): resend invite to invitee-1 (unconfirmed user) or manually attach; ask invitee-6 which other emails they invited (only 1 recorded).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed with prod evidence; invitees who click invite link land on inviter's team and can enter their board; regression test added.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED via prod (dcfqzbdusxhrfgvnpwqc) read-only diagnostics 2026-07-28.

Evidence:
- Team 206 team 206: player_ids=[invitee-6 only]; invited=['invitee-1@redacted.invalid'] (still pending). Only 1 invite ever recorded despite 'people'.
- auth.users invitee-1@redacted.invalid: user_metadata.invited=true, provider=email, last_sign_in_at=NULL, email_confirmed_at=NULL -> they have NEVER completed authentication. So join RPC (handle_invited_signup) is NOT the problem; it never runs.
- invitee-6 authenticated via Google (works). Only confirmed-working auth path in prod is Google OAuth (browser PKCE w/ code_verifier cookie).

Mechanism: invitePlayer calls supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail(email,{data:{invited:true}}) with NO redirectTo (actions.ts:120,145). Invite link therefore redirects to project Site URL, not /api/auth/callback. Clients use @supabase/ssr default PKCE (no flowType). Invitee lands unauthenticated (default template code-exchange needs a code_verifier cookie that admin-initiated invites don't have) -> never routed through handleInvite -> no team join. Login OTP works only because it uses code-entry/verifyOtp, not the email link; invite has only the email link.
close_reason: Released to prod and verified (deploy + test ran smoothly). Invite links route through callback via token_hash template; Site URL + redirect allowlist set on prod.

  TXT   @                v=spf1 include:spf.improvmx.com ~all
  TXT   @                google-site-verification=EDPUna6t...
  TXT   bounces          v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all         <- Resend
  TXT   _dmarc           v=DMARC1; p=none;
  TXT   resend._domainkey  p=MIGf...                               <- Resend DKIM
  TXT   _vercel          vc-domain-verify=feedback.wordl...
  CAA   @                sectigo / pki.goog / letsencrypt (+ comodoca, digicert, ssl.com per dig)
  Everything DNS only (grey cloud). Nothing proxied.

WHY THE WILDCARD MATTERS: 216.198.79.65 and 64.29.17.1 are Vercel's anycast addresses — the same pair the apex uses — so *.wordleteams.com sends EVERY subdomain to Vercel. That is why beta.wordleteams.com already answers today, with a 404 from 'server: Vercel'. See wt-ksh.1.9 for what it means for the Worker custom domain.

NOTE THE RESEND RECORDS. Three of these records (bounces MX, bounces SPF, resend._domainkey DKIM) are Resend email authentication, and v2 keeps Resend for OTP and invite mail. Do not let a future DNS tidy-up remove them.
close_reason: Already satisfied and now verified. wordleteams.com runs on Cloudflare nameservers with the zone reporting status=active via the API; Vercel records are DNS-only, the apex serves 200, www 307s to it, and improvmx MX plus Resend SPF/DKIM are intact. Step 5 closed out by recording the account id and an API token in .env.local.

title: Phase 8 — Cutover
description:
Cutover to the production domain. See epic wt-ksh and amendment A1.

Pre-cutover week: prod OAuth callbacks for all four providers, maintenance banner on prod, one runbook dry-run (copy + verify, no DNS flip).
Cutover day (<1hr): maintenance mode, final copy run, DNS flip, smoke test, OAuth + Polar webhook URL switch to the prod domain.

THE PAYING-CUSTOMER STEPS ARE OBSOLETE (amended 2026-08-03). The original runbook carried 'create real Polar product + webhook config', 'email the paying customer with a comp offer' and 'send the Polar checkout link'. v1 already migrated to Polar in production, so the products and webhooks exist. There is also no active Polar subscriber at all right now: the one paying customer is riding an unbounded 'pro' grace period with nothing behind it, to be resolved by hand on 2026-09-05 (wordle-teams-g3k). Drop those three steps.

What replaces them: whatever Polar subscription state exists at cutover must SURVIVE it, which means the v2 user has to resolve to the same Polar customer. That is an identity-mapping check, not a re-subscribe — and it runs straight into the identity bug described on wt-ksh.6, because every migrated user already exists as a Polar customer under their email.
acceptance_criteria: New app serves wordleteams.com; smoke test passes (OTP + social login, board entry, scoreboard, PWA); rollback path documented and live; and any Polar subscription live at cutover still resolves to the correct v2 user afterwards.
notes:
CUTOVER STEP ADDED 2026-08-24 (wt-ksh.13.6): the final copy run discards beta state on purpose, and two things about it have to be checked by hand.

Beta team and player state IS DISCARDED at cutover — the final copy is meant to overwrite beta test data. The owner's decision (2026-08-24) is that everything in the beta deployment is testing data permanently, including rows created by anyone brought in to help test. The full write-up is in epic wt-ksh under 'Data Model & Migration', beside the re-runnable claim it is the consequence of.

Note which rows that means, because it is easy to get backwards: a row BORN in v2 is the SAFE one — no legacyId, and byLegacyId is the whole upsert key for players and teams, so the copy never matches it. What a re-run reverts is a COPIED row v2 later edited. monthlyWinners is the exception: it matches on (teamId, year, month), so a winner row v2 computed itself IS adopted and overwritten.

1. THE OVERWRITE REPORT. copy-from-supabase.mjs prints what the run clobbered — per table, per field, row counts only; framed when non-zero, one quiet line when zero. EXPECT IT TO BE NON-ZERO FOR BETA STATE, and CONFIRM IT IS NON-ZERO FOR NOTHING ELSE.

READ THAT AT FIELD LEVEL, NOT TABLE LEVEL, or it is a check that cannot fail. Only players, teams and monthlyWinners ever appear in the overwritten list at all — partition() in scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs routes any table whose tally has no `clobbered` key straight to 'Not diffed', so dailyScores, playerMembership and webhookEvents are structurally incapable of showing up. 'Nothing else' therefore means no unexpected FIELD on those three tables, not no fourth table.

The report does not claim to cover everything and names what it is not speaking for in its own clean line: dailyScores is left undiffed (wordle-teams-r9d), and nothing in v2 writes playerMembership or webhookEvents yet. Array fields compare as multisets, so a re-copy can reorder playerIds and invited — the orders getMyTeamsFor and getTeamInvitesFor hand to the UI — with no line in the report. Deliberate; order-sensitive comparison would fire on every run.

AND THE REPORT CANNOT TELL YOU WHO WROTE THE VALUE IT REPLACED. A clobbered entry means only that the incoming v1 value differs from the stored one, which is produced by a lost v2 edit OR by v1 drifting since the last copy — the ordinary dual-running case this script exists to serve. So the judgement is per field, against this list.

EXPECTED — beta state being discarded as intended. DO NOT STOP FOR THESE:
  - teams: name, playWeekends, showLetters, playerIds, invited. ANY SUBSET IS ORDINARY — a field counts only when its VALUE differs (recordClobbers, convex/migrate.ts:164-167). updateTeamFor patches the first three in one write (convex/teams.ts:202-206), which is why they cluster, but a name-only save reports name alone.
  - players: timeZone, reminderDeliveryMethods, reminderDeliveryTime, hasPwa, lastBoardEntryReminder — but only once Phase 6 (wt-ksh.7) has landed, which is what makes the first four user-editable and what starts the cron writing the fifth. Phase 6 ships BEFORE cutover, so by the time this runbook runs, expect them. See the note at convex/migrate.ts:244-249.
  - monthlyWinners on an ADOPTED row — the exception described in the which-rows paragraph above. legacyId ALWAYS moves, undefined becoming a Supabase id; migrate.test.ts's adoption case asserts that field ALONE. The other two are conditional: playerId only if v1's winner differs from the one v2 computed, hasSeenCelebration only if the seen-lists differ as multisets — a pure reorder counts nothing. teamId, year and month are the match key and cannot differ.

STOP AND READ BEFORE THE DNS FLIP:
  - teams.creator. Insert-only in v2 — createTeamFor sets it (convex/teams.ts:161) and nothing ever patches it — so a count here is never a lost v2 edit. It means the copy is changing which player owns a team, or filling in one an earlier scoped copy left absent.
  - teams.scoring (the eight base fields, reported as one). Always v1-side: v2 never writes them after createTeam, since setScoringSystem writes a scoringSystems row rather than the team doc. That is NOT a reason to wave it through — it may be the most consequential count in the report. An imported v1 scoring edit lands as the team's BASE system, and any month with no scoringSystems version preceding it falls back to exactly those fields, so the import retroactively re-scores every month before v2's first version row and can change who won one (wordle-teams-1j3).
  - anything not on the expected list.

2. THE INSERT REPORT (wt-ksh.13.10). SHIPPED — this is no longer a hand-check. copy-from-supabase.mjs reads the deployment's row counts BEFORE it writes anything, and prints a SECOND framed block, below step 1's, whenever a deployment that already held rows gains any.

WHY A SECOND BLOCK AND NOT A COLUMN IN THE FIRST. A row v2 DELETED leaves the overwrite report nothing to diff against: byLegacyId finds no match, the copy takes the INSERT branch, and the row returns counted as 'inserted'. No diff-based report can see that. cascadeDeleteTeam (teams.ts), recomputeTeamMonth (winners.ts) and upsertBoardFor (scores.ts) all hard-delete without regard to legacyId, so a deleted team, a cleared board and a month that stopped having a winner all come back. This block does not diff. It rests on a different property: a re-copy against UNCHANGED v1 data inserts NOTHING.

IT COVERS ALL SIX TABLES, where step 1 covers three — every migrate.ts upsert returns an insert count, only three return clobbers. dailyScores is therefore in it: the table wordle-teams-r9d deliberately leaves undiffed, and the one a cleared board comes back through.

IT MAKES A RESURRECTION VISIBLE. IT DOES NOT ATTRIBUTE ONE. Resurrection is ONE of the reasons a re-run inserts, and the list of innocent ones is not short: a row new in v1 since the previous copy, a widened --scope, a previous copy that died partway, a first copy into a deployment already holding v2-born rows, a row that used to fail the skip filters. The counts cannot tell any of them apart. A tombstone could; it was considered and not built. Working the list is this step, and the block itself deliberately refuses to state it as an either/or.

FOUR STATES, so you know which one you are in:
  - NOTHING PRINTED. The deployment was EMPTY before the run, so every row was legitimately an insert and the block would be pure noise. Only two things empty it: never having been copied into, or a deliberate purgeCopiedData. If neither applies and no block appeared at all, stop and read the script's own output above the write summary — a failed pre-write read announces itself there and again below, so a true blank means neither branch fired.
  - ONE QUIET LINE, 'Inserted nothing on a re-run — the deployment already held N rows'. The check ran and no table gained a row, so nothing v2 deleted came back. Nothing to adjudicate.
  - THE FRAMED BLOCK, listing each table that inserted and how many. Adjudicate it.
  - 'Insert check DID NOT RUN'. The pre-write row counts could not be read, so there is no trigger and the check is simply absent for this run. The copy itself is unaffected and its writes stand — the read is wrapped precisely so that a report about the copy cannot kill the copy (internal.migrate.counts collects every row of every table, and Convex caps one execution at 4096 reads). TREAT THIS RUN AS UNCHECKED FOR RESURRECTION. Re-read the counts by hand before the DNS flip if the run mattered.

HOW TO ADJUDICATE, IN THIS ORDER. Do not start at the per-table list. Two WHOLE-RUN explanations come first, both of them innocent and both of them capable of producing tens of thousands of inserts, and the per-table question below gives the WRONG ANSWER for either — it would read every one of those rows as a resurrection and send you deleting rows the copy had legitimately just written.

  GATE A — IS THIS ACTUALLY THE SAME COPY, RUN AGAIN? It is not, if any of these hold, and each of them makes the inserts BACKLOG rather than resurrection:
    - the previous copy DIED PARTWAY. A run that failed after players and teams leaves the other four tables inserting everything on the next run. The give-away is scale and shape: whole tables at full size, not a handful of rows.
    - the SCOPE CHANGED. --scope=all after a --scope=mine run legitimately inserts old v1 rows, and so does the same --scope=mine run under a different ME_EMAIL — a scope change rather than a widening, with the same effect.
    - this is the FIRST copy into a deployment that already held v2-BORN rows. The deployment is non-empty, so the block fires, but nothing has ever been copied into it and every row is a first-time insert.
    - purgeCopiedData WAS RUN BUT NOT LOOPED. It deletes a bounded slice per call (batch=800), breaks, and returns remaining:true for the caller to loop on (migrate.ts:579-601). Stop after one call and the deployment is PARTIALLY purged: the next copy re-inserts that slice — around 800 dailyScores, since children go first — and those are OLD rows, so they clear gates A and B and fail gate C. Recoverable, and nothing was lost: the copy put back what the half-finished purge removed. Finish the purge and re-copy, or simply re-copy.
  In every one of these the block firing is correct and there is NOTHING TO DELETE. Note what happened and re-read the block on the next run, when the backlog is gone.

  GATE B — DID THE SKIP FILTERS' INPUTS MOVE? A nameless v1 player and a memberless v1 team are skipped by scripts/lib/copy-filters.mjs, and the run prints both counts under 'Skipped (not copied)'. A player since given a name, or a team that gained a member, is a legitimate first-time insert of an OLD v1 row and will fail the created_at question below. Compare the two skip counts against the previous run's before concluding anything.

  GATE C — only with A and B ruled out, ask per row: DOES V1 HOLD IT WITH A created_at AFTER THE PREVIOUS COPY RUN? If yes it is new and expected. If v1's newest rows in that table all predate the previous run, the copy re-inserted an OLD v1 row, which means v2 had deleted it — a resurrection.

  - dailyScores. EXPECT INSERTS on every re-run; v1 gains boards daily. Judge the MAGNITUDE, against the 'In scope' dailyScores line and against the previous run's count. A day or two of play is ordinary; a jump is not, because a re-inserted cleared board is indistinguishable from a new one and only the size gives it away.
  - monthlyWinners. Expect inserts for months v2 held no winner row for. recomputeTeamMonth DELETES a winner row when a month stops having one, so a month v2 correctly emptied comes back here.
  - webhookEvents. Expect inserts if v1 processed a Polar webhook since the last copy. Nothing in v2 deletes them.
  - players, playerMembership. Nothing in v2 deletes from either table, so an insert is a new v1 signup — or, for players, someone who used to fail the nameless-player filter and now passes (gate B). Re-check the delete claim at cutover rather than trusting this line, but know what the output looks like first: git grep -n "db\.delete(" convex/ printed FOURTEEN hits on 2026-08-25, and only three matter. winners.ts, scores.ts and teams.ts are the deletes against a copied table. The others are testOtps.ts (three, including the exported takeFor mutation, all against the testOtps table, which the copy never writes), migrate.ts (purgeCopiedData itself) and four *.test.ts files. What would be new information is a delete against players or playerMembership; there is none today.
  - teams. STOP AND READ. cascadeDeleteTeam is the confirmed resurrection path — the creator deletes a team, or the last member leaves one — and the probe on 13.10 saw a deleted team come back reported as inserted=1. A resurrected team brings its monthlyWinners rows back with it. Its scoringSystems rows do NOT come back, because the copy never writes that table, so it returns carrying its v1 base scoring alone.

IF YOU CONFIRM A RESURRECTION — meaning gates A and B are both ruled out and gate C says the row predates the previous copy — delete the row in Convex by hand, after the copy and before the DNS flip, then re-read the 'Convex now holds:' counts. There is no tombstone, so any later copy would bring it back, which after the flip you must not be running anyway. DELETING ON GATE C ALONE IS THE DANGEROUS MISTAKE HERE: a resumed partial copy fails gate C for every row it wrote.

title: Phase 7 — Parity audit + hardening
description: Route-by-route walk of prod vs beta (static pages, /me, error states, sitemap/robots/OG images, maintenance page), fresh copy run + re-verify, cutover runbook written. See epic wt-ksh.
acceptance_criteria: A written checklist of every prod screen has a ✔ against beta.
notes:
ADDED 2026-08-03 (amendment A4): the route-by-route walk must assert CACHE HEADERS per route, not just rendered output.

v1's marketing pages emitted 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' despite being prerendered, so 28-41% of requests to /home, /privacy and /terms missed the edge and invoked a cold function at ~1.9s (40e9940, wordle-teams-jcj). Phase 0 shipped wt-ksh.1.13 enforcing 'no-store' on SSR document responses — correct for authenticated documents, WRONG for the static marketing routes. If that is applied at the worker level to every document, v2 reproduces jcj on a new platform.

ALSO: v1's middleware had NEVER executed in production — it sat at the repo root while Next resolves it at src/middleware.ts, with no warning and no build error, so maintenance mode, the welcome-path PWA redirect and auth cookie refresh were all dead until bdca5f5. Do not assume maintenance mode works in v2 because it exists; test it.
ADDED 2026-08-24 (wt-ksh.13.6): WHEN YOU WRITE THE CUTOVER RUNBOOK, wt-ksh.9's notes carry two required steps that are not obvious from this issue.

The final copy run DISCARDS beta team and player state on purpose — that is the owner's decision (2026-08-24), written up in epic wt-ksh under 'Data Model & Migration', beside the re-runnable claim it follows from. The two steps are (1) read the copy's overwrite report at FIELD level, and (2) check resurrection by hand, because no diff-based report can see a row v2 deleted (wt-ksh.13.10). Both belong in the runbook this issue is scoped to produce; wt-ksh.9 is where they are written down, not where they will be executed from.

BLOCKER FILED 2026-08-24: wordle-teams-b31 (P1). internal.migrate.counts does six unbounded .collect() calls, one on dailyScores, and Convex caps a function execution at 4096 reads. verify-parity.mjs:59 calls it as its FIRST query. At --scope=all - which is what this phase's parity audit runs - the verifier would fail before comparing a single row. migrate.ts itself documents the limit in three other places and works around it in all three; counts is the outlier. Settle this BEFORE the audit, not during it. Quickest first step: run verify-parity.mjs against beta, which already holds ~6950 daily scores, and see whether it is already failing.

title: Phase 5 — Payments (Polar)
description:
Polar checkout, customer portal, idempotent webhook handler writing webhook_events, upgrade/downgrade team-size mutations. See epic wt-ksh and the A1 amendment in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md.

NO LONGER GREENFIELD. v1 migrated Lemon Squeezy -> Polar in place and it has been live in production since 2026-08-03. v2 inherits the Polar orgs, the two Pro products (monthly + annual; Polar has no variants, billing cycle is locked at creation, so they are separate UUIDs passed as a products array to one checkout) and the webhook endpoints. Reference implementation: src/lib/polar/ on this branch.

PORT THESE THREE THINGS OR REPEAT V1'S BUGS:
1. events.ts mapEventToTransition - pure, no I/O, ports to Convex almost verbatim. active/uncanceled -> pro; revoked -> expired; canceled/past_due -> no change. Conflating canceled with revoked strips a paying customer's teams weeks before the period they paid for expires.
2. identity.ts resolvePlayerId - Polar does NOT reliably stamp external_customer_id onto a customer. When a checkout matches an EXISTING customer by email the value stays on the checkout and the customer keeps its own null external id. Webhook delivers, logs succeeded=true http=202, nobody is upgraded. Resolve customer.externalId -> checkout metadata -> checkouts.get(checkoutId), then repair the customer. THIS MATTERS MORE IN V2 THAN V1: at cutover every migrated user already exists as a Polar customer under their email, which is exactly the failing case.
3. Standard Webhooks ids are NOT UUIDs (msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W). Key idempotency on a STRING id read from the webhook-id HEADER, not the body. v1 lost time to a uuid column that rejected them and put Polar into an infinite retry loop.

VERIFY BEFORE ADOPTING @polar-sh/better-auth: v1 rejected @polar-sh/nextjs because its Webhooks helper auto-acknowledges, which destroys the store-then-process-then-500-so-Polar-retries behaviour the idempotency design rests on. The Better Auth plugin may do the same. Raw @polar-sh/sdk is the known-good fallback.
design:
DECIDED 2026-08-25 by the owner, three questions answered before any code.

=== WHAT WE ARE BUILDING, AND WHY ===

Polar billing in v2: checkout, customer portal, an idempotent webhook handler, and
the membership transitions that move a player between free and pro — plus the
non-pro 2-team cap that Phase 4 deferred here.

THIS IS NOT A GREENFIELD INTEGRATION. v1 migrated Lemon Squeezy -> Polar in place
and it has been live in production since 2026-08-03. v2 inherits the Polar orgs,
the two Pro products and the webhook endpoints. src/lib/polar/ on this branch is
a working reference implementation, 563 lines across 8 files, and three of those
files encode bugs that cost v1 real time. Port the lessons, not just the code.

=== THE THREE THINGS TO PORT OR REPEAT V1'S BUGS ===

1. THE EVENT MAP (src/lib/polar/events.ts, pure, no I/O).
   subscription.active / subscription.uncanceled -> pro
   subscription.revoked                          -> expired
   subscription.canceled / subscription.past_due -> NO CHANGE
   Conflating `canceled` with `revoked` strips a paying customer's teams weeks
   before the period they already paid for expires. `canceled` means they
   SCHEDULED a cancellation; `revoked` means access actually ended.
   Note v1 uses a Map, not an object literal, deliberately: the key is an
   arbitrary string from outside, and a Record lookup walks the prototype chain,
   so 'toString' and '__proto__' would both return truthy non-transitions.

2. IDENTITY RESOLUTION (src/lib/polar/identity.ts).
   Polar does NOT reliably stamp external_customer_id onto a customer. When a
   checkout matches an EXISTING customer by email, the value stays on the
   checkout and the customer keeps its own null external id. The webhook is
   delivered, logged succeeded=true http=202, and NOBODY IS UPGRADED. Silent,
   because 202 is not an error.
   Resolve in three steps, cheapest first: customer.externalId -> checkout
   metadata.player_id -> checkouts.get(checkoutId). Then repair the customer so
   later events take the fast path.
   THIS MATTERS MORE IN V2 THAN IT DID IN V1: at cutover every migrated user
   already exists as a Polar customer under their email, which is exactly the
   failing case. It is a cutover prerequisite, not hardening.

3. WEBHOOK IDS ARE NOT UUIDS. Polar follows Standard Webhooks; ids look like
   msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W. Key idempotency on a STRING id read from the
   webhook-id HEADER, not the body. v1 lost a day to a uuid column that rejected
   them, returned 500, and put Polar into an infinite retry loop against an event
   that could never be stored.
   Convex has no unique constraints, so the replay guard is a by_webhookId lookup
   inside the mutation — the schema comment on webhookEvents already says so.

=== KEY DECISIONS, AND WHAT WAS RULED OUT ===

A. THE DOWNGRADE IS SOFTENED. NEW DIVERGENCE FROM V1.
   v1's handle_downgrade_team_removal keeps 2 teams, removes the player from the
   rest, and then DELETES the teams they created beyond the keep list — taking
   every other member's scores and history with it. A billing event on one
   account destroying a third party's data is not a behaviour worth porting.
   v2 keeps 2 teams (creator-owned first, then oldest), removes the player from
   the rest, and NEVER deletes a team that still has members.
   SUB-DECISION, made rather than asked, flag it if wrong: a team the downgraded
   player created and has now left gets its creator reassigned to the
   earliest-joined remaining member. If NO members remain, the team is deleted —
   nobody loses anything, and copy-filters.mjs already establishes that a team
   with nobody on it is not a team.
   RULED OUT - leaving the team creator-less. V2-ADDENDUM already records that a
   creator-less team cannot be edited by anyone; deliberately manufacturing that
   state is worse than reassigning.
   This becomes divergence 12 in V2-ADDENDUM 7a and must be written there.

B. THE 2-TEAM CAP (wordle-teams-44o) IS IN SCOPE.
   Phase 4 deferred it here, and it is genuinely coupled: the cap parks an
   over-cap invitee's address in teams.invited and increments a pending-upgrade
   count; the upgrade transition is what releases them. Phase 5 has to build the
   release half regardless, so building the cap elsewhere means shipping half a
   mechanism twice.
   It also closes the window where v2 is MORE PERMISSIVE than production. The
   retrofit hazard is the point: enforcing later means removing people from teams
   they have already joined, and the longer it waits the more of them there are.
   PORT THE REAL V1 BEHAVIOUR. An earlier claim that v1's
   handle_add_player_to_team cap branch is broken in production is FALSE and was
   corrected on 2026-08-22: the invited_id bug was real but was fixed on
   2024-04-29 (20240429204119), and the current definition (20240501180309) caps
   correctly. Both v1 cap branches work.

C. BUILD EVERYTHING, THEN ONE VERIFICATION PASS. Owner's choice over the
   backend-first split. The stated risk is that the identity bug surfaces late,
   after the UI already depends on it.
   MITIGATION, and it is a requirement not a nicety: the silent-202 case must be
   pinned by a UNIT TEST — customer.externalId null, metadata.player_id present,
   resolution succeeds — so the sandbox is confirming a bug we already proved
   closed, rather than discovering it.

D. THE PENDING-UPGRADE COUNTER IS NOT MIGRATED, and does not need to be.
   v1 stores invites_pending_upgrade in auth.users.raw_app_meta_data, which the
   copy script does not read and should not start reading. It does not matter:
   the actual parking lives in teams.invited, which IS copied, and the release
   mechanism keys off teams.invited rather than the counter. A v1 user with
   parked invites therefore still gets released correctly on upgrade in v2.
   v2 stores the count on the players doc (v1's auth metadata store has no
   equivalent), starting at 0 for everyone.

=== SCOPE BOUNDARIES - EXPLICITLY OUT ===

  - Any change to convex/migrate.ts or the copy scripts. playerMembership and
    webhookEvents are already copied. Phase 5 is the first phase where v2 WRITES
    either table, which is worth knowing but changes nothing here.
  - wordle-teams-b31 (internal.migrate.counts blows the read limit). P1, real,
    and flagged on Phase 7 — but it is a verifier problem, not a billing one.
  - wordle-teams-g3k, the paying customer's unbounded grace period, to be
    resolved by hand on 2026-09-05 against v1/production. Not a v2 task.
  - The comped 'pro' accounts (the owner's and their spouse's). They come across
    with membershipStatus 'pro' via the copy and nothing in v2 revokes them,
    because no Polar event references them. Correct by construction; no work.
  - Re-typing or reviving the dropped player_customer columns. The schema comment
    is explicit: nothing branched on the variant, every gate is just "are they
    pro". Do not port the dropped columns back into existence.

=== HOUSE RULES THAT APPLY (learned, expensive) ===

  - Put every rule in the ...For helper, never in a query/mutation wrapper.
    convex-test cannot stand up a Better Auth session, so authed wrapper bodies
    are untestable (wordle-teams-obw).
  - Throw ConvexError via accessError, never a plain Error.
  - `enabled:` does not gate a Convex query and is not a security boundary.
  - Gates from v2/: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test:once && pnpm build.
    pnpm e2e is NOT in the gates - run it by hand when you touch what it drives.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

  1. Sandbox subscribe / upgrade / downgrade / cancel all mutate team limits
     correctly, confirmed by the owner on beta.
  2. A checkout that resolves to a PRE-EXISTING Polar customer with a null
     external id still upgrades the right user — the v1 silent-202 failure —
     and this is pinned by a unit test before the sandbox ever runs.
  3. A duplicate webhook-id returns success WITHOUT reprocessing.
  4. subscription.canceled and subscription.past_due change no membership and
     remove no teams; only subscription.revoked downgrades.
  5. A downgrade never deletes a team that still has members, and the divergence
     is recorded in V2-ADDENDUM 7a.
  6. A non-pro invitee at the 2-team cap is parked in teams.invited rather than
     added, and upgrading releases every parked invite.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox subscribe/upgrade/downgrade/cancel all mutate team limits correctly. PLUS: a checkout that resolves to a pre-existing Polar customer with a null external id still upgrades the right user (the v1 silent-202 failure), and a duplicate webhook-id returns success without reprocessing.
