title: v2 re-platform: Cloudflare + TanStack + Convex
description:
# Re-platform to v2: Cloudflare + TanStack + Convex — Design

**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Status:** Approved design, pending implementation plan

## Summary

Rewrite wordle-teams as a new app (`v2/`) on a new platform stack, built in parallel
with the existing production app, tested at `beta.<domain>`, and cut over via DNS flip
when feature parity is verified. Strict 1:1 functional parity — no new features, no
redesigns — with two sanctioned exceptions: Convex reactivity making scoreboards
live-update (free win), and passkey enrollment (near-zero marginal cost inside the
Better Auth slice).

## Context & Drivers

- **Cost:** Vercel pricing grows steeply with scale; Cloudflare's curve is much flatter.
  Get ahead of growth.
- **DX/architecture:** the app is a client-heavy dashboard — TanStack's client-first
  model fits better than Next.js RSC/server actions.
- **Vendor reduction:** ~10 vendors today, ~6 after.

**Constraints:** ~40 DAU in production daily, small data, solo developer with a few
hours/week. Existing app must remain fully live and supported throughout. One paying
customer (~$2/mo Lemon Squeezy subscription) who must be personally migrated.

## Decisions Made (and alternatives ruled out)

| Decision | Chosen | Ruled out / why |
|---|---|---|
| Database | **Convex** | Neon — data layer must be rewritten either way (RLS + DB functions are Supabase Auth–coupled), so Convex's rewrite penalty evaporates; its reactive model fits a client-heavy dashboard best; generous free tier |
| Auth | **Better Auth** via `@convex-dev/better-auth` | Clerk/Convex Auth — user preference; open source; Polar has a first-party Better Auth plugin |
| Payments | **Polar.sh** via `@polar-sh/better-auth` | Built into new app from day one; no in-place Lemon Squeezy→Polar phase (only 1 subscriber) |
| Notifications | **No vendor** — Convex cron + `web-push` + Resend | Knock — one workflow doesn't justify a platform; Convex scheduling replaces both Novu and QStash |
| Strategy | **Vertical slices on a walking skeleton** (Approach A) | Layer-first (nothing testable end-to-end for weeks); strangler proxy on prod domain (sessions can't span two auth/db systems; machinery costs more than the rewrite at 40 DAU) |
| Repo | **`v2/` folder in this repo**, fully self-contained | Separate repo — same-workspace old code is superior reference material during porting |
| Beta data | **One-shot re-runnable copies** from Supabase | Live/two-way sync — sync machinery is where solo projects die; buys nothing at this scale |
| Parity | **Strict 1:1** | Redesigns/new features go to a post-cutover backlog |

## Target Architecture

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Framework | TanStack Start (Router + Query + server functions), Vite, React 19 | Server functions only where needed (webhooks, auth) |
| Hosting | Cloudflare Workers (TanStack Start Cloudflare target) | Wrangler; `beta.` subdomain during parallel run |
| Data | Convex — schema, queries/mutations, crons, scheduled functions | `@convex-dev/react-query` for live-updating TanStack Query data |
| Auth | Better Auth on Convex | Email OTP + Google, Azure, GitHub, Twitter/X + passkey plugin |
| Payments | Polar.sh via Better Auth plugin | Checkout, customer portal, webhooks |
| Email | Resend + react-email | Ports nearly as-is; also sends Better Auth OTP emails |
| Reminders | Convex cron → `web-push` + Resend | Replaces Novu + QStash + both reminder API routes |
| PWA | vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox) | Replaces Serwist; manifest ports as-is |
| Errors | Sentry (Cloudflare/TanStack SDK) | Wired from Phase 0 |
| Analytics/logs | Cloudflare Web Analytics; Workers Logs; keep LogSnag | Drop Vercel Analytics/Speed Insights, next-axiom, Axiom |

**Killed with no replacement:** Novu, QStash, Vercel KV, Edge Config, Lemon Squeezy SDK,
Serwist, next-axiom, Axiom.

**Open checklist item (verify in Phase 0):** whether Supabase Storage buckets hold real
user files (e.g. avatars). If yes → Convex file storage; if unused → nothing to do.

## Repo Layout & Environments

```
wordle-teams/            ← repo root unchanged; Vercel keeps building it
├── src/ ...             ← current Next.js app, untouched until cutover
├── supabase/
└── v2/                  ← new app, fully self-contained island
    ├── package.json     ← own deps, own pnpm-lock.yaml (NOT a workspace member)
    ├── wrangler.jsonc
    ├── convex/          ← schema, functions, crons, auth config
    ├── src/             ← TanStack Start app
    └── scripts/         ← copy-from-supabase.ts + parity verification
```

**Island rule:** no imports across the `v2/` boundary, no shared lockfile, no root
tooling changes. Old code is reference material only.

| Env | Hosting | Convex | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local dev | `vite dev` + `convex dev` | personal dev deployment | localhost |
| Beta | Cloudflare Workers | prod deployment of the project | `beta.<domain>` |
| Prod (post-cutover) | same Worker, promoted | same Convex project — beta *becomes* prod | main domain |

The beta Convex project becomes the prod project at cutover: final data copy overwrites
beta test data, domain flips. No second migration.

**Deploys:** GitHub Action on `v2/`-touching pushes → `convex deploy` + `wrangler deploy`.
Vercel's existing auto-deploy of `dev` continues untouched (never trigger Vercel manually).

**DNS:** nameservers move to Cloudflare early (free plan) — prerequisite for beta
subdomain and cutover; Vercel keeps serving apex/www through the same records.

## Data Model & Migration

**Tables (6, port near-1:1):** `players`, `teams`, `daily_scores`, `monthly_winners`,
`player_customer` (becomes Polar customer mapping), `webhook_events`. Docs keep a
`legacyId` for idempotent re-copying (or wipe-and-reload — fine at this size).
Relations become Convex ID references + indexes.

**Postgres logic relocation:**

| Today (in the DB) | In Convex |
|---|---|
| RLS policies | Access checks at top of each query/mutation, centralized in small helper functions |
| `handle_invited_signup`, `handle_add_player_to_team` | Mutations in invite/onboarding flow (Phase 4) |
| `handle_upgrade_team_invites`, `handle_downgrade_team_removal` | Mutations called by Polar webhook handler (Phase 5) |
| `update_monthly_winners` (trigger) | Logic inside score-submission mutation (transactional, so trigger semantics port cleanly) |
| `get_players_for_reminder`, `update_last_board_entry_reminder` | Internal functions called by reminder cron (Phase 6) |
| `custom_access_token_hook` (JWT claims) | Not needed — claims fed RLS; checks now read membership directly |

**Auth migration:** login is passwordless (email OTP) → no password hashes to migrate.
Copy script creates Better Auth users by email (+ name, verified flag). Sessions do not
carry over — the only user-visible cost of the entire migration is one extra login.

**Social OAuth:** trim to Google, Azure, GitHub, Twitter/X. Safe because OTP on the same
email is the universal fallback for users of dropped providers. Better Auth links social
logins to existing accounts by verified email; Twitter/X doesn't always return an email —
OTP is the fallback there too. Each provider needs OAuth app registrations with beta
callback URLs (during build) and prod callbacks (at cutover) — explicit checklist work
in Phase 1.

**Passkeys:** Better Auth passkey plugin + one "Add passkey" button in account settings.

**Copy script** (`v2/scripts/copy-from-supabase.ts`): reads Supabase with service-role
key, writes via Convex internal mutations. Re-runnable on demand; run once more during
the cutover window.

**What the re-run overwrites, and why that is the point.** Beta team and player state is
discarded at cutover — the final copy is *meant* to overwrite it. Owner's decision
(2026-08-24): everything in the beta deployment is testing data, permanently, and that
includes rows created by anyone brought in to help test. "But someone else made that
team" is not an objection; it is still test data.

Which rows are actually at risk is easy to get backwards. A row **born in v2 is the safe
one**: it carries no `legacyId`, and `byLegacyId` is the entire upsert key for `players`
and `teams`, so the copy can never match it and never patches it. What a re-run reverts
is a **copied** row that v2 has since edited — a renamed team, a changed roster, an
invite added or cancelled. `monthlyWinners` is the exception: it matches on `(teamId,
year, month)`, not `legacyId`, so a winner row v2 computed itself *is* matched, adopted
and overwritten.

So the copy reports what it overwrote (`wt-ksh.13`): `upsertPlayers`, `upsertTeams` and
`upsertMonthlyWinners` return per-field counts of the rows they patched to a different
value, and the script prints a framed block when non-zero, one quiet line when zero. Not
to protect beta rows — nothing there needs protecting — but so that a copy run at the
**wrong** moment, after cutover with real users on v2, announces itself. It reports the
difference, never its author: a count means the incoming v1 value differs from the stored
one, which is a lost v2 edit *or* ordinary v1 drift since the last copy, so reading it is
a per-field judgement. `scoring` is always the latter — v2 never writes those eight
fields after `createTeam` — which does not make it harmless: an imported v1 scoring edit
lands as the team's base system, and any month with no `scoringSystems` version before
it falls back to exactly those fields, so the import re-scores it (`wordle-teams-1j3`).
It is not total, and its clean line names the tables it is not speaking for:
`dailyScores` is left undiffed (`wordle-teams-r9d`), and nothing in v2 writes
`playerMembership` or `webhookEvents` yet. Array fields compare as multisets, so a
re-copy can silently reorder `playerIds` and `invited` — the orders `getMyTeamsFor` and
`getTeamInvitesFor` hand to the UI — accepted, because order-sensitive comparison would
fire on every run and train everyone to ignore the report. And a row v2 **deleted** is
invisible to any diff by construction: nothing remains to compare against, so the copy
re-inserts it and reports it as `inserted` (`wt-ksh.13.10`). That needs a tombstone, and
until it has one the cutover runbook checks it by hand (`wt-ksh.9`).

## Phase Plan

Each phase is independently shippable to beta, sized for 1–2 weeks of a few-hours/week
solo pace. **No phase starts until the previous phase's done-when is met.**
Phases 2→4 are strictly ordered; Phases 5 and 6 are independent of each other and may
interleave; nothing else may.

- **Phase 0 — Walking skeleton.** TanStack Start scaffold in `v2/`, Convex project,
  Better Auth email OTP only, deploy pipeline, `beta.` DNS, Sentry.
  ✅ *Done when: OTP login works at `beta.<domain>` and a page renders one value
  round-tripped through Convex.*
- **Phase 1 — Auth complete + data copy.** Full Convex schema, copy script (users +
  6 tables), social providers incl. OAuth console registrations, passkey plugin,
  account linking.
  ✅ *Done when: your real copied account logs in via OTP and via Google on beta, and
  enrolls a passkey.*
- **Phase 2 — Core loop.** Board entry (porting the recent mobile keyboard/viewport
  work faithfully), scoreboard, month navigation, monthly-winner logic in the score
  mutation, access-check helpers.
  ✅ *Done when: a full fake day works on beta — enter board, live score updates,
  correct monthly winner.*
- **Phase 3 — Teams.** Create/switch/manage, member lists, settings, team-scoped
  access checks.
  ✅ *Done when: a multi-team account behaves identically to prod side-by-side.*
- **Phase 4 — Invites & onboarding.** Invite flow, invited-signup + add-player
  mutations, complete-profile flow, invite emails via Resend.
  ✅ *Done when: a fresh email invited on beta lands on the right team with the right
  profile.*
- **Phase 5 — Payments (Polar).** Sandbox → Better Auth plugin, checkout, customer
  portal, idempotent webhook handler writing `webhook_events`, upgrade/downgrade
  team-size mutations.
  ✅ *Done when: sandbox subscribe/upgrade/downgrade/cancel all mutate team limits
  correctly.*
- **Phase 6 — Reminders & PWA.** Convex cron → reminder-eligibility port → web-push +
  Resend; vite-plugin-pwa, manifest, install/offline; old-Serwist-SW kill switch.
  ✅ *Done when: beta sends a real push + email reminder at the configured time and the
  PWA installs on a phone.*
- **Phase 7 — Parity audit + hardening.** Route-by-route walk of prod vs beta (static
  pages, `/me`, error states, sitemap/robots/OG images, maintenance page), fresh copy
  run + re-verify, cutover runbook written.
  ✅ *Done when: a written checklist of every prod screen has a ✔ against beta.*
- **Phase 8 — Cutover.** See below.
- **Phase 9 — Post-cutover cleanup** (~2 weeks after cutover). See below.

## Cutover & Rollback

**Pre-cutover (week before):** add prod callbacks to all four OAuth apps; create real
Polar product + webhook config; email the paying customer (what's changing, Polar link
coming, comp offer); in-app maintenance banner on prod ("you'll need to log in again");
one runbook dry-run (copy + verify, no DNS flip).

**Cutover day (target < 1 hour, low-traffic time):**
1. Prod → maintenance mode (existing `/maintenance` page)
2. Final copy-script run (beta Convex data replaced with real snapshot)
3. DNS flip: main domain → Worker; `beta.` stays alive on the same Worker
4. Smoke test on prod domain: OTP login, one social login, board entry, scoreboard,
   PWA opens on phone
5. Switch Polar webhook + OAuth primary URLs to prod domain
6. Send Polar checkout link to the customer
7. Announce done

**PWA continuity:** installs are domain-keyed and survive the flip; new SW takes over on
next visit. The Phase 6 kill switch ensures the old Serwist worker unregisters cleanly so
no one is stuck on a stale cache.

**Rollback (kept 2 weeks):** Vercel deployment and Supabase stay live and untouched;
rollback = flip DNS back. **One-way data rule:** scores entered post-cutover exist only
in Convex — rolling back loses them unless manually re-entered. Accepted at this scale;
breakage would surface within hours, not days.

**Post-cutover cleanup (Phase 9):** cancel/retire Vercel project, Supabase project
(after a final archived pg_dump), Novu, QStash, Lemon Squeezy store (after the
subscription is confirmed moved); promote `v2/` to repo root (old app lives in git
history); delete dead env vars.

## Testing, Error Handling & Observability

**Testing (proportionate, concentrated where rewrite risk lives):**
- **Convex function tests** (`convex-test` + Vitest), priority order: monthly-winner
  computation, invite/signup flows, upgrade/downgrade logic, access-check helpers —
  including negative cases (non-member *cannot* read another team's scores).
- **Parity spot-checks:** after each copy run, a script asserts row counts and known
  aggregates (e.g., a specific month's winner) match Supabase vs Convex.
- **UI:** manual and structured — each phase's done-when plus the Phase 7 route
  checklist. No component-test suite for a 1:1 port.
- **One smoke E2E** (Playwright: OTP login → enter board → see score) before each phase
  merge and on cutover day. One test, not a suite.

**Error handling:**
- Convex mutations throw `ConvexError` with typed codes; UI maps codes → sonner toasts.
- **Webhook handlers idempotent** (Polar retries): `webhook_events` dedup by event ID.
  Reminder cron never double-sends (last-reminder timestamp guard, ported).
- TanStack Router error boundaries per route section + root boundary → Sentry.

**Observability:** Sentry from Phase 0; Workers Logs for request logs; LogSnag continues
for business-event pings; Cloudflare Web Analytics snippet at Phase 7; Axiom dropped.

## Out of Scope

- Any new features or redesigns (except the two sanctioned: live-updating scoreboards
  via Convex reactivity, passkey enrollment)
- Live/two-way data sync between Supabase and Convex
- Zero-downtime cutover machinery (maintenance window is acceptable)
- Notification platform (Knock etc.) — revisit only if notification complexity
  materializes post-cutover
- Migrating Vercel-specific features with no user impact (Speed Insights, Edge Config)

## Acceptance Criteria (project level)

1. New app at the production domain on Cloudflare Workers with TanStack Start + Convex +
   Better Auth + Polar, at 1:1 functional parity per the Phase 7 checklist
2. All migrated users can log in (OTP or retained social provider) and see their full
   score history
3. The paying customer is subscribed via Polar; Lemon Squeezy retired
4. Reminders (push + email) fire correctly from Convex cron
5. Installed PWAs survive cutover without user reinstallation
6. Old stack fully retired within ~2 weeks of cutover; rollback path verified live
   until then
notes:
AMENDED 2026-08-03. dev was merged into feat/v2-replatform after ~93 commits of v1 work that post-date the design: the Lemon Squeezy -> Polar migration (now live in production), the invite->join fixes, and a run of performance/reliability fixes. See the Amendments section at the end of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md — several decisions in the body of that spec are superseded.

Headlines:
 - Phase 5 (wt-ksh.6) is no longer greenfield; v2 inherits live Polar orgs, products and webhooks, plus three hard-won bugs it must port fixes for.
 - Phase 4 (wt-ksh.5) inherits one invite bug that SURVIVES the rewrite: case-sensitive invited[] matching.
 - Parity is now against dev as of 2026-08-03, not the 2026-07-16 snapshot (wt-ksh.3, wt-ksh.7).
 - Phase 8 (wt-ksh.9) loses its paying-customer migration steps; Lemon Squeezy is already retired and there is no active Polar subscriber.
 - The COST driver is contradicted by the funnel data measured since. Open owner decision: wordle-teams-dts.
 - ALL OF v2 IS BLOCKED behind one manual owner step: moving wordleteams.com nameservers to Cloudflare (wt-ksh.1.1).
SEQUENCING SETTLED 2026-08-18 (closes wordle-teams-dts). Owner chose option (b): interleave funnel work with the port. See amendment A7 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md.

Three consequences for this epic:
 1. Cost is demoted from lead driver to secondary benefit. DX/architecture fit and vendor reduction (~10 -> ~6) carry the project. Not an open question any more.
 2. Strict-1:1 parity gains a THIRD sanctioned exception: the login/onboarding surface, alongside reactivity and passkeys. Rationale: wordle-teams-390 was re-measured 2026-08-17 and the leak did not move (163 -> 203 people reaching /login, conversion ~7% -> ~8%) even though Lemon Squeezy — A5's leading mechanical explanation — is gone. 93% abandon at login vs 87% at activation, with zero server-side auth failures. Porting v1's icon-only tooltip provider grid faithfully would reproduce the largest known leak in the product. Parity everywhere else is unchanged and still strict.
 3. Funnel instrumentation (login-page view, provider-button click, callback arrival) is a v2 deliverable, not a post-cutover backlog item.

This does NOT license a general redesign. Every screen outside login/onboarding still ports 1:1, and A3 still governs which version it ports against.

NEW PHASE INSERTED: wt-ksh.12, Phase 1.5 — Design system foundation, sits between Phase 1 and Phase 2 and now blocks wt-ksh.3. See amendment A8. Reason it goes here rather than later: v2/src/components has three files and no component library, so Phase 2 is the first phase to build substantial UI. Landing the design system after Phase 2 means restyling the board and scoreboard.

title: Phase 5 spec/plan: record the Buffer divergence and the wire-shape identity read
description:
Task 10 (wordle-teams-p8m) diverged from the plan on a measurement; neither the design spec nor the plan records it yet. Parent: wt-ksh.6.

WHAT CHANGED: convex/http.ts does NOT use @polar-sh/sdk's validateEvent. On Convex's default runtime it throws 'ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined' (measured against the local backend on 2026-08-27) because its first line is Buffer.from(secret,'utf-8'). Verification goes through standardwebhooks@1.0.0 directly - the same library the SDK verifies through - constructed with { format: 'raw' } over the secret's UTF-8 bytes, byte-identical to what the SDK would have keyed on. standardwebhooks is now a direct dependency of v2 at the version already in the lockfile.

KNOCK-ON, AND IT TOUCHES DECISION F: a verified delivery is JSON.parse of the body, i.e. the snake_case WIRE shape, not the SDK's renamed camelCase. convex/lib/polarIdentity.ts now reads customer.external_id / customer_id / checkout_id. metadata.player_id is unchanged (metadata keys are ours). Nothing runs a per-event zod schema any more, which is deliberate: a strict parse would reject a delivery over any field Polar adds later.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE DOCS: the failure was invisible to the entire quality gate. vitest's edge-runtime environment DOES define Buffer, and npx convex codegen analyses modules without serving a request, so lint/typecheck/test/build were all green while every real delivery would have answered 400. Task 13's sandbox pass should re-confirm the endpoint on beta rather than assume the local backend and the cloud runtime agree.

DONE WHEN: the design spec's decision F and the Phase 5 plan's Task 10 both describe the wire shape and the standardwebhooks verification, and the divergence log carries this alongside 8/12/13.
notes:
STATUS 2026-08-27: the verifier is confirmed LIVE on the deployment - a bogus signature returns 403 'Invalid signature' from https://fabulous-goldfish-949.convex.site/polar/webhook. That proves standardwebhooks is running and rejecting.

WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN IS EXACTLY ONE THING: that Polar's OWN bytes verify. The key derivation is proven byte-identical to the SDK's (sign under the SDK-derived key, verify under the shipped key, across 8 secrets including non-ASCII, CJK and emoji), and convex/http.test.ts drives the whole protocol with REAL Standard Webhooks signatures. So the mechanism is sound; what no test here can produce is a genuine Polar delivery.

THE FIRST REAL DELIVERY IS THE TEST. If it 403s, the secret registered in Polar does not match POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET on the deployment - check that before suspecting the verifier, since a mismatched secret and a broken verifier are indistinguishable from the status code alone.

WATCH FOR: a 403 on every delivery means the secret is wrong or empty (an empty key is accepted by standardwebhooks and would 403 everything - http.ts:120-124 guards construction against that, so an empty secret gives 500, not 403). A 202 on every delivery means signatures verify but identity does not resolve - that is decision F territory, not this issue.

title: e2e prune cannot reach the betterAuth component tables, which still grow without bound
description:
FOUND 2026-08-26 alongside the e2ePrune work (wordle-teams-1cd).

convex/e2ePrune.ts empties every application table it is pointed at - after the first run the local backend held 0 players, 0 teams, 0 dailyScores, 0 monthlyWinners, 0 scoringSystems, 0 playerMembership. The betterAuth component tables were untouched and still held:

  _components/betterAuth/user      2617
  _components/betterAuth/session   2672   (2392 of them not yet expired)

Every e2e sign-in creates a user and a session there and nothing removes either. ctx.db in a normal Convex function cannot see component tables, so the prune structurally cannot reach them - it would need the betterAuth component's own API, not a wider query.

NOT known to matter yet: the flake this came out of was disconfirmed as data-volume-related, and better-auth looks these rows up by indexed token/email rather than by scanning. Filed because it is the one unbounded accumulation the prune does NOT solve, and because 'the prune ran, so the deployment is clean' is now an easy and wrong inference.

title: e2e invites spec flakes on the local backend: OTP sign-in navigation times out
description:
e2e/invites.spec.ts:119 'an invited address joins the team after completing a profile' fails in the FULL suite and passes in isolation, on the local anonymous Convex backend.

FAILURE
  Locator: getByRole('region', { name: 'Current Team' })
  Timeout: 5000ms, element(s) not found
  Call log: waiting for "http://localhost:3000/?signin=otp" navigation to finish...
at e2e/invites.spec.ts:160, the expect(teamCard(owner)).toBeVisible() straight after signInWithOwnTeam. The sign-in OTP navigation has not completed, so this is auth/navigation timing, not a team-rendering bug.

NOT CAUSED BY THE creator->owner RENAME. Verified by stashing the follow-up changes and running the full suite at the committed rename state (68e7795), which had been green earlier the same session: it reproduces there too. So this is environmental drift in the local backend, not a code regression.

LIKELY CAUSE: accumulated local e2e data. internal.migrate.backfillTeamOwner reported 'teams scanned 1624' against the local backend, against ~171 teams in production. Every e2e run adds accounts and teams and nothing prunes them. schema.ts's teams comment already flags that there is no index for 'teams containing player X' and says to revisit if the count changes by an order of magnitude - it now has, locally.

REPRODUCTION: pnpm e2e from v2/ (fails 1/15); pnpm exec playwright test e2e/invites.spec.ts:119 (passes).

SUGGESTED FIX: a way to reset or prune the local anonymous backend between e2e runs, or raise the 5s expect timeout on the post-sign-in assertion. Decide which before it trains people to ignore a red e2e - see the standing note that e2e sits outside the quality gates and a spec once stayed red for three tasks.
notes:
CONTROLLER VERIFICATION 2026-08-27: two independent e2e runs after the fix, 17 passed / exit 0 both. Combined with the implementer's 9/9, that is 11 consecutive clean runs against a measured 3/5 baseline and 1/6 the day before.

THE CONTENDING-SIGN-INS DIAGNOSIS RECORDED EARLIER ON THIS ISSUE WAS WRONG, and the correction matters. A headless probe driving full OTP sign-ins through the real /api/auth endpoints measured 6 CONCURRENT sign-ins at 1.2-1.5s each against 0.58s for one alone - 2.2x wall-clock for 6x concurrency. Sublinear, so nothing on the auth path serialises, and there is no shared state (unique e2e+<stamp>-<rand> per sign-in, testOtps read by_email, Better Auth's verification indexed by identifier).

THE REAL MECHANISM: e2e/sign-in.ts returned the instant the Verify click was dispatched, but login.tsx's verifyCode ends with window.location.href = '/?signin=otp' - a FULL DOCUMENT LOAD. So the caller's next assertion, on Playwright's 5s default, had to absorb the verify round-trip, a fresh SSR of / (beforeLoad awaits needsProfile, then the loader awaits getMyTeams, amIPro and getMyPlayerId SEQUENTIALLY), several hundred dev-server module requests, and hydration. Instrumented and measured: 54 sign-ins over three runs, min 0.76s, MAX 3.96s, median ~2.2s. The worst legitimate case sat at 0.8 of the deadline.

That also explains the correlation the earlier diagnosis mistook for contention: more sign-ins meant more chances to draw a slow one, not sign-ins interfering with each other. And it explains why the failing spec was never the faulty one.

THE FIX IS THE HELPER'S CONTRACT, NOT THE CEILING: sign-in.ts now awaits page.waitForURL(url => !url.pathname.startsWith('/login'), { timeout: 20_000 }), so it returns when the sign-in has LANDED. Every downstream assertion keeps the strict 5s, so a real rendering regression still fails fast; only the sign-in wait is generous. 20s is ~5x the measured worst case and inside the 30s test timeout, so a sign-in that never lands is reported AS a sign-in failure rather than as a missing team card. No assertion was weakened.

Blanket timeout raise, serialising sign-in and cutting workers were all rejected on the probe evidence - there is nothing to serialise.

HONEST CAVEAT: 11/11 does not prove the tail is gone, only that it moved well clear of the ceiling on this machine.
close_reason: Fixed in 10e4ce1: sign-in.ts waits for its own landing. 3/5 clean before, 9/9 after.

title: Task 12: checkout return leg + record the pro-gate enforcement decision
description:
Phase 5. CLOSES wordle-teams-6tn, whose acceptance criterion is that Phase 5's scope names CheckoutReturn AND states whether the pro gates are enforced server-side. Both answered.

THE RETURN LEG IS MOSTLY UNNECESSARY IN V2. v1's checkout-return.tsx exists to defeat JWT staleness: user_member_status is stamped into the Supabase token, so it calls refreshSession() and schedules a 2s retry against a racing webhook. v2 reads membership through api.teams.amIPro via convexQuery + useSuspenseQuery (src/routes/index.tsx:66) - a REACTIVE websocket subscription. When the webhook mutation patches playerMembership, subscribed clients update on their own.

So the refresh, the timer, and v1's Strict-Mode 'handled' ref (which existed only to stop the refresh running twice) are all DEAD CONCEPTS, not things to port. What survives: strip ?checkout=success, and show an honest pending state that resolves by itself.

THE GATES STAY AS ENFORCED AS V1'S (decision K): invitee cap server-side (v1 enforces it in the RPC); createTeam and the scoring editor UI-only (v1 does not enforce either). The asymmetry is v1's - it guards the path where SOMEBODY ELSE adds you to a team and leaves the paths you drive yourself to the UI.

Rewrite isProFor's doc comment (access.ts:200-209), which currently defers this question to a phase that has now happened.

DONE WHEN: returning from checkout shows a pending state that resolves with NO reload; ?checkout=success is stripped; isProFor's comment records the decision; gates green; e2e by hand.
close_reason: Return leg shipped as decision L describes: src/lib/checkout-return.ts (pure, 16 tests), src/components/checkout-return.tsx (hook + notice), mounted in all three of routes/index.tsx's returns. No refreshSession, no timer, no handled ref. isProFor's comment verified against v1's SQL and server actions and extended with the month window, the fourth gate 6tn names. Gates: lint 0, tsc 0, test 0 (596, was 580), build 0. e2e 16/17, the failure being wordle-teams-1cd at invites.spec.ts:119, reproduced 2/2 with this task's spec block stashed out. Commit a8e76d1.

title: Task 13: divergences 8/12/13, sandbox verification, phase close
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. The closing task. Everything is built before verification - owner's decision C - so this task carries the whole verification load.

WRITE DOWN THE SOFTENED DOWNGRADE. New DIVERGENCE 12 in docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md 7a: v1 deletes teams the downgraded player created beyond their kept 2, destroying other members' scores and history; v2 removes the player, reassigns the creator, and deletes only a team nobody is left in. Update the section's 'Eleven known differences' header - it is load-bearing and has already been the subject of one stale-figure bead (wt-ksh.13.11).

UPDATE DIVERGENCE 8 if Task 6 has not already: the 2-team cap now exists in v2, so v2 is no longer more permissive than prod.

CHECK THE DELETE-SITE INVENTORIES. Task 3 adds a new db.delete site. wt-ksh.13.10's runbook step 2 on wt-ksh.9 and the grep breakdown in scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs both enumerate delete sites; a new one makes both stale.

PHASE 5 IS THE FIRST PHASE WHERE V2 WRITES playerMembership AND webhookEvents. convex/migrate.ts's blind-spot list says in as many words that neither table is at risk today 'because nothing in v2 writes either table yet - Phase 5's Polar work is what would change that'. That sentence becomes false with this phase. It is asserted in FOUR places per wordle-teams-r9d's notes: migrate.ts, scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs, the wt-ksh epic description, and wt-ksh.9's notes. Fix all four.

OWNER VERIFICATION ON BETA, against the Polar SANDBOX - parent acceptance criterion 1. Subscribe, upgrade, downgrade, cancel, and confirm team limits move correctly each time. Confirm specifically that subscription.canceled does NOT remove teams and subscription.revoked does.

DONE WHEN: e2e covers what it can; all four blind-spot sites are corrected; divergences 8 and 12 are written with the header count updated; the owner has run the sandbox pass on beta and confirmed it; and wt-ksh.6's six acceptance criteria are each closed against evidence.

title: Task 11: the upgrade and portal UI
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. The player-facing surface for Task 7.

v1 has three upgrade buttons and they are all IDENTICAL - no plan selection, because the customer chooses monthly vs annual on Polar's hosted page (Task 7). Do not invent a plan picker.

Needs, at minimum: a way to start a checkout, a way to reach the customer portal for anyone who already has a Polar customer, and an honest empty state for a player who has never checked out - Task 7's 'no-customer' result exists so this can say something true.

Reflect membership state the player can actually see. A player who just completed checkout lands back in the app before the webhook may have been processed; decide what they see in that window and make it deliberate rather than accidental.

Follow the existing v2 UI conventions - components under v2/src/components/ui/, import alias #/, and the design system in docs/design-system/. Phase 4's invite dialog and pending-invites section are the closest precedent for a card-with-actions surface.

DONE WHEN: a free player can reach a Polar checkout; a subscribed player can reach the portal; a player with no Polar customer sees an honest state rather than a broken portal link; and the surface works on a phone, since that is the product's primary device.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-27. Commits 681407f + 8bb41d0. 580 tests / 36 files; four gates exit 0; e2e 17 passed, exit 0, no flake.

THE PLAN'S STEPS 2 AND 3 WERE FATAL, NOT WRONG IN DETAIL. Both put Convex React hooks in Header.tsx, which was rendered by the root route's shellComponent - and @tanstack/react-router renders that OUTSIDE the root route's component, therefore outside ConvexBetterAuthProvider. Measured: useConvexAction there answers GET /login with 500, 'Could not find Convex client! useAction must be used in the React component tree under ConvexProvider'. Fixed by moving Header from RootDocument into RootComponent, with rendered DOM order (header, nav, main, footer) verified byte-identical before and after.

THE PLAN ALSO NAMED THE WRONG REACT API. It imports useAction from 'convex/react'; this codebase has ZERO hits for that import. The house pattern is useConvexAction/useConvexMutation from @convex-dev/react-query. The wrong import also failed CONFUSINGLY rather than clearly - 'Cannot read properties of null (reading useContext)', a second React instance from Vite's SSR dep-optimizer, which hides the real cause.

A REAL UI BUG IN THE PLAN'S SNIPPET: '{!isPro && pendingInvites > 0}' has no auth gate and the wrong truthiness test. isPro is undefined while the query is in flight, and !undefined is true, so A PRO PLAYER FLASHES 'N Invites Pending' ON EVERY COLD LOAD. Shipped as 'isPro === false'.

CORRECTION TO THE CONTROLLER: e2e does NOT drive the beta backend. v2/.env.local sets VITE_CONVEX_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3210, a LOCAL Convex backend. Every e2e measurement in this phase was against local. The POLAR_* consequence is unchanged (none set anywhere), so assertion design was unaffected - but the controller said 'beta' repeatedly and that was wrong.

A MEASUREMENT THAT REVERSED A DESIGN INSTRUCTION: the controller said to follow the route loader's ensureQueryData prefetch pattern. Header's reads feed a plain useQuery, so nothing waits on them - there is no waterfall to remove, only latency to add ahead of every child loader. Prefetch removed after measuring.

NOT TESTABLE YET, filed as wordle-teams-ksh.1: the badge above zero needs a second account with a team plus a parked invite - two sign-ins and two contexts, which is exactly the load this suite cannot absorb (see wordle-teams-1cd). The ZERO case is asserted, which catches a badge rendering '0 Invites Pending'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Task 9: convex/polar.ts - checkout and portal actions on the raw SDK
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. Port src/lib/polar/checkout.ts and portal.ts. Both need network, so both are Convex ACTIONS.

CHECKOUT. Both Pro products - monthly and annual - go into ONE session as a products array. Polar has no variants and a product's billing cycle is locked at creation, so the two intervals are separate product UUIDs. A multi-product checkout renders them side by side on Polar's hosted page, which is why NO PLAN-SELECTION UI IS NEEDED and no caller passes a plan.

Pass BOTH externalCustomerId AND metadata.player_id. Belt and braces, and the belt is load-bearing: Polar does not stamp external_customer_id onto a customer that already exists under that email, so the webhook's customer.externalId comes back null and metadata is what Task 4 falls back to. Costs no extra API call.

PORTAL. Resolved by externalCustomerId - the player's own id - rather than a stored Polar customer UUID. That is exactly what let v1 DROP player_customer.customer_id instead of retyping it, and the v2 schema comment says not to bring the dropped columns back.

Portal URLs are short-lived: create at the moment the player clicks, never store the result.

PORT v1's THREE-WAY PORTAL RESULT. { url } / { url: null, reason: 'no-customer' } / { url: null, reason: 'error' }. no-customer is the EXPECTED state for anyone who has never checked out, and is distinguished from a genuine failure so the UI can say something true rather than 'try again later' about a condition retrying will never fix.

successUrl should land somewhere that reconciles membership immediately rather than waiting for a session refresh - v1 uses /me?checkout=success for that reason.

DONE WHEN: a checkout session is created carrying both product ids, the external id and the metadata; the portal returns all three result shapes; and the no-customer case is distinguishable from an error in whatever the UI receives.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-27. Commits 7fb128c + 19a6fcc. 535 tests / 34 files; four gates exit 0; deployed to beta green. Absorbed Task 5's two SDK-dependent identity pieces.

'use node' IS NOT NEEDED, measured three ways: the SDK reaches no Node built-in (one hit, its own unreachable test file); a codegen push succeeded on the DEFAULT runtime; and ADDING the directive BROKE the local push with DeploymentNotConfiguredForNodeActions. It would have cost local development for nothing. Also clears Task 10: standardwebhooks reaches only @stablelib/base64 and fast-sha256, both pure JS.

POLAR_SERVER IS A FIFTH REQUIRED VAR, and this is a correction to v1 rather than a port of it. v1 selects the Polar instance with ENVIRONMENT === 'prod' ? 'production' : 'sandbox'. ENVIRONMENT DOES NOT EXIST IN CONVEX - the only one in the tree is a Cloudflare worker var (wrangler.jsonc:57) a Convex function cannot see. And v1's own value was 'prod', never 'production', so even where the var existed the expression could not select production. Worse, a ternary resolves any typo to sandbox, which after cutover means real subscribers transacting against an instance holding NONE of their data. v2 requires an exact 'production' | 'sandbox' match, so server and credentials move as one list.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS TASK - wordle-teams-1m6, closed. getCustomerPortalUrl looked customers up in ONE namespace while the webhook resolves in TWO (decision F). A subscriber migrated from v1 carries their v1 uuid as Polar's external_id, so the portal would have told A PAYING SUBSCRIBER THEY HAVE NO BILLING ACCOUNT - the exact 'say something true' failure the three-way PortalResult exists to prevent. repairCustomerExternalId heals them only on their next subscription event, months away on an annual plan.

Fixed by mirroring decision F outbound: try the Convex id, fall back to legacyId ONLY on no-customer, and repair on a legacy win. A v2-native player has no legacyId, so the second call never happens for them and the cost decays to zero as customers heal. THE SHARPEST TEST covers a failure mode worse than the original bug: a 500 on the first identity silently retried as the second and reported as no-customer would turn an outage into 'you have no subscription' for EVERYONE, not just migrated users.

TASK 13 NEEDS A NEW CHECKLIST ITEM: 'a migrated subscriber can open the portal'. That path exists only because of this fix and can only be observed end to end.

THIRTEEN WRONG PLAN SNIPPETS, including: 'use node' (wrong); generated-module imports with .ts extensions; a snippet importing 'api' while using 'internal', contradicted by prose two lines below it; ENVIRONMENT === 'production' (wrong var AND wrong value); no server selector in the four-var list at all; and checkoutIdentity placed in billing.ts, whose docblock says it is 'deliberately not the Polar module' - it would have been falsified in the commit that added it.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] update_monthly_winners RPC failed in prod, and its error context logged as null
description:
Axiom (vercel dataset) has exactly one error-level row in the 30h to 2026-08-24T17:00Z:

  _time 2026-08-24T13:12:45.417Z  level=error  message='Failed to update winners table'
  fields.error=null  fields.message=null  fields.stack=null  request.path=null

Source: src/components/action-buttons/board-entry/form.tsx:104 — after a board saves, the client calls supabase.rpc('update_monthly_winners', { winners_data }); on error it logs and shows the 'standings could not be updated' toast. So a real user entered a board successfully at 13:12:45Z and got the degraded-standings warning.

Two problems:

1. The RPC itself failed in prod. Cause unknown — see 2.
2. log.error('Failed to update winners table', { error }) reached Axiom with the message intact but every field of the context object null. Without error.code/message/details there is nothing to diagnose from. This is the same next-axiom context-loss family as wordle-teams-844 (server-action logs never flushing), but a distinct symptom: here the record arrives and the payload is empty, rather than the record never arriving.

Not related to the two 2026-08-24 signups — it fired for an established user mid-session, and neither new account has entered a board.

Acceptance criteria: (a) a deliberate update_monthly_winners failure produces an Axiom row whose fields carry the Postgres error code and message; (b) with that instrumentation in place, determine why the 13:12:45Z call failed and either fix it or record it as understood. Note the v2 replatform may retire this RPC — confirm whether that makes (b) moot before spending on it.

title: [bug] next-axiom webVitals throws 'Converting circular structure to JSON' on /login
description:
Sentry issue 7689138695, prod, first+last seen 2026-08-24T10:04:06-07Z, 3 events / 1 user (Chrome Mobile 151, Android 10). Unhandled TypeError, mechanism=instrument, transaction=/home, url=https://wordleteams.com/login, release 4bcbb9ac71f0e04ac7e643efe8595a4319c47ae3.

Stack (innermost last):
  @sentry/browser 9.46.0 helpers.js:93 in r
  next-axiom 1.9.1 dist/shared.js:129 in n
  next-axiom 1.9.1 dist/webVitals/webVitals.js:20 in a
  JSON.stringify

next-axiom's webVitals reporter calls JSON.stringify on the raw web-vitals metric. For INP the metric carries an attribution object holding a live DOM node reference (Sentry's message names 'starting at object with constructor HTMLButtonElement'), so stringify throws on the cycle. Breadcrumbs confirm it: two ui.click events on a button immediately precede both sentry.event entries.

Impact is bounded — it throws inside the vitals reporting callback, not in app logic, and the session it fired in went on to complete signup and team creation with no failed requests. But it is an unhandled error reaching Sentry on every INP-on-a-button in that browser, it drops the web-vital, and it adds noise that masks real errors: it was the ONLY error-level Sentry event in the last 24h.

Same library as wordle-teams-844, different failure: 844 is server-action logs never flushing; this is the client vitals path throwing.

Acceptance criteria: no 'Converting circular structure to JSON' events from the next-axiom webVitals path in prod Sentry — via a next-axiom upgrade if a fixed release exists, or by wrapping/replacing the reportWebVitals handler so the metric is serialized without its attribution DOM refs. Confirm the web-vital still lands in the Axiom vercel dataset (/_axiom/web-vitals POSTs return 200) after the fix.

title: The copy silently reverts v2 board edits too, and un-deletes deleted boards
description:
Found while implementing wt-ksh.13.4 (the clobber report), 2026-08-24. NOT in that task's scope, and deliberately not fixed there. Belongs with wt-ksh.13.

wt-ksh.13 scoped the overwrite problem to teams and players, on the reading that "Phase 2 only ever wrote dailyScores" — i.e. that scores are the one table the copy is entitled to re-import. That reading is not quite safe, and nothing wrote down why it was accepted.

v2's upsertBoardFor (convex/scores.ts) finds a row by (playerId, puzzleDay), then:
  - PATCHES it with { answer, guesses } when the board is edited, or
  - DELETES it outright when the board is cleared.

Neither path cares whether the row was born in v2 or copied from Supabase, and neither is keyed on legacyId — so unlike teams and players, the "v2-born rows are structurally unreachable" argument does NOT apply here. A copied score row is reachable and editable.

So a re-run of the copy against a used deployment:
  - reverts a board a player edited in v2 during dual-running, back to the v1 value
  - RESURRECTS a board the player deleted in v2: upsertDailyScores keys on legacyId, the deleted row no longer exists, so it re-inserts

Both are silent, and both change monthly totals and therefore winners.

Whether it matters depends on the dual-running rules, which is why this is a decision and not just code:
  - if players only ever enter boards in v1 during dual-running, the copy re-importing v1's truth is CORRECT and there is nothing to do but say so
  - if they enter boards in v2, the copy is destroying real data, and the deletion case is the worse half: a resurrected board cannot be told from a never-deleted one

MINIMUM: write down which it is, next to the discard decision from wt-ksh.13.6.
IF WORTH MORE: upsertDailyScores can report clobbers the way upsertTeams and upsertPlayers now do — sameFieldValue and recordClobbers in convex/migrate.ts already take a groups map. The resurrection case is NOT covered by a clobber report, because there is no existing row to diff against; it needs a separate signal.
notes:
2026-08-24, from the wt-ksh.13.5 review: wiring upsertDailyScores into the clobber report ALSO trips wordle-teams-ct3. The report's headline is unwrapped, and dailyScores is the fourth reporting table that pushes it to 90 columns, outside its own 80-column frame. Do ct3 in the same change.
2026-08-24, from the wt-ksh.13.6 review: wiring upsertDailyScores into the clobber report ALSO makes a documented blind-spot list wrong in two more places. 'dailyScores is left undiffed (wordle-teams-r9d)' is currently asserted in FOUR places — convex/migrate.ts (the clobber block at the top), scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs (formatClobberReport's doc comment), the epic wt-ksh description under 'Data Model & Migration', and wt-ksh.9's notes. The first two are next to the code and hard to miss; the last two are not. Update all four in the same change, or the cutover operator reads a runbook that tells them a table is undiffed when it is not.

Same applies to the other half of that list if Phase 5 lands first: 'nothing in v2 writes playerMembership or webhookEvents yet' is asserted in the same four places and stops being true when Polar's webhook handler ships (wt-ksh.6).

title: Task 5: settle whether skipped players carry playerMembership rows
description:
The open question in the parent's 9lt section. BLOCKED ON A PRODUCTION QUERY the owner must run.

The copy narrows only players and teams. Scores, winners, memberships and webhooks are left to each upsert mutation to drop as orphans and count into its own skipped tally. The Phase 4 design measured that nameless players own 0 boards and 0 monthly-winner rows - which is why 9lt names only players and teams - but it says nothing about playerMembership.

IF those 151 nameless players carry membership rows, then check('playerMembership', src.memberships.length, counts.playerMembership) is a false shortfall too, and Task 4 leaves 9lt half fixed.

THE QUERY: count rows in the scoped membership set whose player has no first or last name. Non-zero means Task 4 must narrow memberships as well.

Do NOT guess this. The whole value of the verifier at the Phase 7 audit is that its numbers are exact, and a filter added on a hunch is as bad as a filter missing.
notes:
THE QUERY, for the owner to run against PRODUCTION in the Supabase SQL editor. Recorded 2026-08-24 so it does not have to be reconstructed.

Note the table is player_customer in Supabase - playerMembership is only the Convex name (see scripts/lib/supabase-scope.mjs:47, which reads 'player_customer' into the variable it calls memberships).

  select
    (select count(*) from players)                            as players_total,
    (select count(*) from players
      where coalesce(first_name, '') = ''
         or coalesce(last_name,  '') = '')                    as players_nameless,
    (select count(*) from player_customer)                    as memberships_total,
    (select count(*)
       from player_customer pc
       join players p on p.id = pc.player_id
      where coalesce(p.first_name, '') = ''
         or coalesce(p.last_name,  '') = '')                  as memberships_of_nameless,
    (select count(*)
       from player_customer pc
       left join players p on p.id = pc.player_id
      where p.id is null)                                     as memberships_orphaned;

The nameless predicate mirrors isNamed in scripts/lib/copy-filters.mjs exactly - Boolean(first_name && last_name) is falsy for null AND for the empty string, which is what coalesce(...,'') = '' reproduces. If the two ever diverge the verifier goes wrong in the direction nobody checks.

HOW TO READ IT:
 - players_nameless should be 151. If it is not, the Phase 4 measurement has drifted and that is its own finding before this task proceeds.
 - memberships_of_nameless is the answer. NON-ZERO means wt-ksh.13.7 is incomplete as written: verify-parity.mjs compares src.memberships.length against Convex, upsertMemberships drops those rows as orphans, and that is a SECOND false shortfall beside the players/teams one this plan already fixes.
 - memberships_orphaned is a free sanity check. Rows pointing at a player that does not exist at all would be a pre-existing data problem, unrelated to this plan but worth knowing.

DELIBERATELY UNSCOPED. The --scope=mine copy against beta is a handful of rows; the number that matters is the FULL copy at the Phase 7 audit, which is the one moment the verifier's answer is load-bearing.
close_reason:
ANSWERED by the owner against production, 2026-08-24:

  players_total            535
  players_nameless         151
  memberships_total        535
  memberships_of_nameless  151
  memberships_orphaned       0

YES - every one of the 151 skipped players carries a player_customer row, so wt-ksh.13.7 (Task 4) is incomplete as originally written and its scope is widened accordingly.

THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT MAKES THE FIX CLEAN: memberships_total == players_total == 535, so player_customer is exactly 1:1 with players. The membership shortfall is therefore not merely non-zero, it is EXACTLY the player shortfall - 151 - because each skipped player takes exactly one membership row with it. A verifier that narrows players and memberships by the same predicate will agree on both counts by construction, not by coincidence.

memberships_orphaned = 0 means no player_customer row points at a missing player, so there is no pre-existing data problem hiding behind this one.

players_nameless = 151 matches the Phase 4 measurement exactly, so the copy filter's premise has not drifted.

ONE DRIFT WORTH RECORDING: players_total is 535, not the 533 the Phase 4 design and V2-ADDENDUM row 7 state - two signups since 2026-08-20. The 151 figure those documents rest on is unchanged, so no conclusion moves, but the audit will compare against the stated total and should not be surprised by it.

title: CI never typechecks v2 - add a typecheck step
description:
Found during wordle-teams-9lh, 2026-08-22.

.github/workflows/deploy-v2.yml runs: lint -> unit tests -> 'convex deploy --cmd pnpm build' -> wrangler deploy -> smoke test.

NOTHING IN THAT LIST TYPECHECKS. vite build does not typecheck - it transpiles and strips types. v2/package.json has no typecheck script either. So a type error reaches beta as long as the tests pass, and the only thing catching it today is a human remembering to run 'pnpm exec tsc --noEmit' by hand.

This matters more than it looks, because tsc is genuinely load-bearing here and in one case is STRICTER than the linter: noUnusedLocals follows JSDoc @link tags where @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars does not (see the chunkNote suppression in convex/migrate.ts).

FIX: add "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit" to v2/package.json and a CI step beside Lint. It exits 0 on the tree today, so this is purely about keeping it that way.

Not bundled into 9lh because that issue was about one import rule, and adding a second CI gate is its own change.
close_reason:
Fixed in a86b63f2. v2 gained a 'typecheck' script (tsc --noEmit) and a Typecheck step in deploy-v2.yml, beside Lint and ahead of the unit tests.

THE GAP WAS REAL AND I MEASURED IT rather than assuming. With 'export const n: number = "not a number"' added to src/:
  pnpm build      exit 0
  pnpm test:once  exit 0   <- under the old pipeline it shipped to beta
  pnpm typecheck  exit 2

Caught in src/, convex/ AND e2e/ alike - tsconfig includes all three, so this covers the parts of the tree the client bundle never touches and the unit suite only partly reaches.

Placed ahead of the tests because both are static checks and it is the cheaper failure. It also catches a stale routeTree.gen.ts: the vite plugin regenerates that on build, so a new route that was never committed typechecks green locally after a build and fails in CI, which is the right way round.

Verified: frozen-lockfile install, lint, typecheck, 328 unit tests, build, and e2e 15/15 all exit 0; the CI run for the preceding commit already showed the Lint step green, and this adds Typecheck beside it.

title: Make e2e mail suppression structural before Phase 6 adds a third sender
description:
Raised by the wordle-teams-96l review, 2026-08-22.

There are exactly two resend.sendEmail call sites today - auth.ts (sign-in codes) and teams.ts (invites) - and both are now guarded by isE2eTraffic. e2eSeed.ts sends nothing.

THE PROBLEM IS THAT THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THE GUARD HAD TO BE ADDED AFTER THE FACT. auth.ts had it from the start; invitePlayer shipped without it and sent real mail from the production sending domain on every e2e run until it was caught. Nothing makes the third one hard to forget: there is no choke point, no lint rule, and convex/email.ts still exports a raw Resend client constructed with testMode: false.

wt-ksh.7 (Phase 6 - Reminders & PWA) will add that third sender, and reminders go out in BULK - the blast radius is larger than invites.

SUGGESTED FIX: a thin wrapper in convex/email.ts that applies the guard itself and is the ONLY export:

  export async function sendEmail(ctx, opts) {
    if (isE2eTraffic(opts.to, process.env.E2E_TEST_MODE)) return
    return rawResend.sendEmail(ctx, opts)
  }

One line to change at each existing call site, and Phase 6 is covered by construction.

DO NOT instead set the Resend component's testMode: true under the flag - @convex-dev/resend restricts recipients to *@resend.dev in that mode, which would break the owner's own sign-in mail on localhost.

Note the guard reads opts.to, so a wrapper must handle the bulk case: a reminder run addressing many recipients needs the check per recipient, not once for the batch.
close_reason:
Fixed in the commit that renames convex/email.ts's export surface. sendEmail is now the only export; the Resend client is module-private; both senders (auth.ts sign-in codes, teams.ts invites) route through it; teams.ts's per-site guard was deleted rather than left as a second copy of the rule.

FILTERED PER RECIPIENT, not per message. The fix this issue proposed - isE2eTraffic(opts.to, ...) - would have been wrong: to, cc and bcc are each string | string[] TODAY, so it passes an array to a string predicate. realRecipients filters instead, so a batch holding a throwaway account beside a real one still reaches the real one. That is the case Phase 6's bulk reminders will actually hit.

Also added, not in the original scope: an empty recipient list from the CALLER now throws rather than returning the same quiet null a suppression does. Phase 6 builds recipients from a query, and one returning nothing through a filter mistake would otherwise be indistinguishable from correct suppression - in the return value and in the mail oracle alike.

auth.ts keeps its own check because it ROUTES the OTP to the capture oracle rather than merely suppressing a send; it now carries a comment saying so, because it otherwise reads as exactly the duplicate that was deleted from teams.ts, and removing it breaks every e2e sign-in.

The choke point is TESTED, not merely documented - convex/email.test.ts drives sendEmail against the real Resend client with a fake ctx. That was the gap that let this class of bug ship twice: a predicate test cannot see a wrapper that ignores the predicate. 6/6 mutants on realRecipients, 6/6 on the wrapper (including the inverted guard that would silently stop ALL real mail), plus the loud/quiet split, each with control, sanity and byte-identical restore. 328 unit tests, tsc, build clean; e2e 15/15 across three runs; mail oracle unchanged at 11:25:30 twelve suite runs later.

NOT DONE: the third gap this issue named - a lint rule stopping a new module importing Resend directly - is filed separately, because v2 has no ESLint config at all.

title: Convex query/mutation wrapper bodies are unreachable by any test
description:
Found while implementing Phase 4 Task 2 (wt-ksh.5.14), 2026-08-21.

convex-test cannot stand up a Better Auth session, so authComponent.getAuthUser
never resolves under test. That means the BODY of every authed query/mutation
wrapper in this codebase is unreachable by the unit suite — players.ts, me.ts,
teams.ts and scores.ts all have the exposure.

This is exactly why access.ts gives its checks an explicit-playerId shape
(requireTeamMemberFor rather than a ctx-only wrapper): the rules live in
testable helpers. Task 2 followed that and pushed validation, normalisation and
the today-bound down into completeProfileFor, leaving only getAuthUser, the
!user?.email guard, and argument forwarding in the wrapper.

WHAT IS STILL UNCOVERED, and the mutations that prove it survive:
 - needsProfile inverted  -> either an infinite redirect loop to the profile
   form, or an onboarding form nobody ever sees. THIS IS THE VALUABLE ONE.
 - needsProfile returning true when unauthenticated -> bounces signed-out
   visitors into onboarding instead of /login.
 - completeProfile dropping its UNAUTHENTICATED guard.
 - a wrapper passing a hard-coded `today` instead of forwarding the argument.

None is caught by anything today.

The cheap fix is an e2e assertion rather than a session harness: Task 6 adds
/complete-profile and the dashboard guard, and driving a brand-new address
through it exercises needsProfile in both directions for real. Do that there,
and note here that the other three remain wrapper-only exposure.

Do NOT "fix" this by extracting a needsProfileFor helper for a single
row-existence check — that breaks the ...For convention (which means "takes
explicit ids") for no branching logic.
acceptance_criteria: Either the wrapper bodies are covered (e2e or a session harness), or the exposure is documented so nobody assumes convex-test covers them.
notes:
PARTIALLY CLOSED by Phase 4 Task 6 (wt-ksh.5.18), 2026-08-21. The valuable exposure - needsProfile inverted - is now closed by e2e/complete-profile.spec.ts, which drives a brand-new address through the route and exercises the predicate in BOTH directions. Verified by review: needsProfile inverted fails 9 of 10 e2e tests; always-false fails 3; always-true fails 8; removing the dashboard guard fails 3.

THE OTHER THREE REMAIN WRAPPER-ONLY EXPOSURE, uncaught by anything:
 - needsProfile returning true when unauthenticated. NOT reachable by e2e, because both routes check context.isAuthenticated BEFORE querying it.
 - completeProfile dropping its UNAUTHENTICATED guard.
 - a wrapper passing a hard-coded today instead of forwarding the argument. Invisible to e2e by construction.

Note also that e2e cannot mutation-test needsProfile itself without a convex deploy, which is forbidden - the e2e mutants above were run against route consumers, not the server predicate.

title: Task 8: e2e invite path, divergence list, beta verification, phase close
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 8

The e2e spec generates its invited address per run so the account is genuinely
new - completeProfile creating the player is the thing under test, and a reused
address would already have one.

Reuse the sign-in helper e2e/teams.spec.ts already has. Do NOT invent a second
sign-in implementation.

pnpm e2e is NOT part of test/tsc/build. In Phase 2 a spec stayed silently red for
three tasks because nothing ran it.

V2-ADDENDUM 7a goes from five divergences to ten. Also record the two
non-divergences: inviting an existing player sends no email (parity), and
NO_PLAYER's copy changed while its code and condition did not.

Then wt-ksh.5.4 on beta with two real browsers and two real accounts, through the
REAL invite path - which is why it was deferred from Phase 3 rather than done
with hand-seeded data.

Before closing the epic, file the Phase 5 issue for the deferred non-pro 2-team
invitee cap. The retrofit hazard is the point: enforcing it later means removing
people from teams they have already joined.
acceptance_criteria: The e2e spec drives invite to sign-in to profile to landing on the team, and the creator's Pending list clears reactively. V2-ADDENDUM 7a records divergences 6-10. The real invite path is verified on beta and wt-ksh.5.4 is met.
notes:
ADDED 2026-08-22 from the Task 7 quality review. Task 8's e2e MUST pin the invite outcome-to-copy mapping specifically, not just the happy path.

Nothing in Task 7's commit has automated coverage at any layer. Measured: swapping the 'resent' and 'invited' toast copy, or dropping the 'return' that keeps the dialog open on already_member, keeps ALL of it green - 294 unit tests, tsc, build, and all 12 e2e specs. That mapping IS divergence 9's entire deliverable (v1 reports all four outcomes as 'Successfully invited player', including already_member where nothing happened).

There is also no component-test harness: vitest.config.ts sets include: ['convex/**/*.test.ts', 'src/**/*.test.ts'] - .tsx is not matched - with a global environment: 'edge-runtime'. @testing-library/react and jsdom ARE already dev deps, so the cost is a config line plus a // @vitest-environment jsdom pragma if a component test is ever wanted. e2e is the cheaper pin.

Recommended shape: extend e2e/teams.spec.ts (its two-account seeding harness already exists) - invite -> pending row appears -> cancel -> row gone, plus a member-leaves assertion, and assert the toast TEXT for each of the four outcomes plus that already_member leaves the dialog open with the field cleared.

Hand-driven verification is currently the only evidence for all of Task 7, and it does not persist. See the memory note that a spec once stayed red for three tasks because pnpm e2e is not in the gates.

title: Task 7: Invite dialog, Pending invites section, Leave control
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 7

Creates invite-player-dialog.tsx (ports v1's invite-player.tsx) and extends
current-team-card.tsx with a creator-only Invite button beside Settings, a
Pending section with per-address cancel popovers, and a Leave control.

FOUR OUTCOMES, FOUR MESSAGES. already_member is the one that keeps the dialog
OPEN: nothing the user wanted actually happened, and the likeliest next action is
correcting the address, so closing would make them reopen it. The field is
cleared so the next attempt starts fresh. Divergence 9.

Leave and remove are COMPLEMENTS, never both on one row. The card already gates
remove on isCreator AND not-my-row; Leave is not-isCreator AND my-row. A creator
sees remove on everyone else and nothing on their own row; a member sees Leave on
their own row and nothing on anyone else's.

Leaving the team you are viewing leaves the team search param pointing at a team
you are no longer on - the same broken-param problem deleting a team already has.
Reuse index.tsx's existing onDeleted handler shape.

WATCH IN REVIEW: getTeamInvites is fetched with enabled: isCreator. If that is
dropped, every member's browser issues a query that throws - a console error
rather than a broken page, so it is easy to miss.

Screenshots: 390x844 with touch emulation, both themes, with at least two pending
invites and a long team name. Watch for a page-wide horizontal scrollbar (the
Phase 3 bug) and a long address overflowing the Pending row instead of
truncating. Wait for Radix animate-in to settle before capturing.
acceptance_criteria: All four invite toasts correct; already_member keeps the dialog OPEN with the field cleared; Leave and remove never both render on one row; leaving the selected team lands on another team rather than the error boundary. Screenshotted light and dark on a touch viewport.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-08-22 during implementation. This issue's watch item said: 'getTeamInvites is fetched with enabled: isCreator. If that is dropped, every member's browser issues a query that throws - a console error rather than a broken page.' BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG.

1. enabled: isCreator DOES NOT GATE THE QUERY AT ALL. @convex-dev/react-query's subscribeInner opens the websocket watch from the query cache's 'added' event, which TanStack fires even for a disabled query, and it never consults enabled. Only convexQuery(..., 'skip') short-circuits it - isConvexSkipped is checked before the switch, and it sets enabled: false itself. Measured at the websocket: under the plan's form a member's browser sends ModifyQuerySet for teams:getTeamInvites and receives a QueryFailed Transition carrying NOT_TEAM_CREATOR; under 'skip' it sends zero frames. The shipped code uses the 'skip' form.

2. IT DOES NOT SURFACE AS A CONSOLE ERROR. The adapter catches the refusal and writes it into query state via query.setState({status:'error'}), so nothing reaches the console - zero console errors, zero page errors. A reviewer grepping for a red line would have passed the bug. The correct probe is the websocket frames, not the console.

This matters beyond Task 7: any future creator-only or otherwise access-gated Convex query must use the 'skip' form, and enabled: is not a security boundary. These are real email addresses.
close_reason:
Task 7 shipped in 8fa7aed (plus 590d653 deflaking the offline spec). Invite dialog with four outcomes/four messages, creator-only Pending invites section with per-row cancel, Leave control as remove's exact complement, onLeft wiring. 294 unit tests, tsc, build all clean; e2e 12/12 verified across four consecutive runs after the deflake; beta deploy 32575046565 green incl. smoke test. Screenshots light and dark at 390x844 touch, no horizontal scroll in any of six measurements.

BIGGEST FINDING: the plan's 'enabled: isCreator' does not gate a Convex query AT ALL, and its predicted symptom was also false. Measured at the websocket - under enabled: a non-creator's browser sends ModifyQuerySet for teams:getTeamInvites and receives a QueryFailed Transition with NOT_TEAM_CREATOR; under convexQuery(..., 'skip') it sends zero frames. The refusal never reaches the console (the adapter writes it into query state), so grepping for a red line would have passed it. These are real email addresses. Recorded on this issue and in bd memory.

Also found: exact duplicates in team.invited are reachable from v1's live code (invited.includes is nested inside the player-exists branch, so re-inviting an address with no account appends it twice), so key={email} was unsafe - deduped with an order-preserving Set. Pending rows truncated the TAIL, making two addresses differing only in domain visually identical, which defeats divergence 6's stated purpose of telling a typo from a slow responder - now min-w-0 break-all. The implementer's own dialog-overflow 'Verified:' claim was falsified in review and then traced to breakage it had introduced in its own first draft; __root.tsx's body already carries [overflow-wrap:anywhere]. Envelope icon sat mid-block on wrapped rows (off by one full line box on 3-line, half on 2-line) - now items-start with mt-[5px].
