title: Task 6: /complete-profile route + dashboard profile guard
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 6

Ports v1's /complete-profile, which A7 makes a sanctioned parity exception - this
is the onboarding surface, and it is the largest measured leak in the product
(wordle-teams-456: 87% of prod signups never enter a board; wordle-teams-390:
~93% abandon at login).

Every v2 account passes through this screen, because completeProfile is what
CREATES the player row.

The guard on / closes wt-ksh.5.1's observed dead end: before this, a cold signup
reached the dashboard anyway - getMyTeams returns [] rather than throwing -
pressed the one call to action, and got NO_PLAYER rendered as 'Your session
expired', which misdescribed the cause and could not be fixed by signing in
again.

CORRECTED 2026-08-21 during implementation. This issue previously claimed 'the
form's submit-enabled predicate, the server's validation and the route guard all
go through isCompleteName, so a name that saves always clears the guard.' That
was wrong twice over. The route guard reads needsProfile, a ROW-EXISTENCE check,
not isCompleteName. And the owner ruled during review that the form should NOT
gate its submit button on isCompleteName at all: a content-gated disabled button
strands the user (it leaves the tab order, Enter does nothing, and no error text
appears anywhere), which is indefensible on the product's biggest funnel screen.
The form now mirrors login.tsx - submit gated only on hydration, with an inline
role=alert error - and the loop is closed more strongly instead: completeProfileFor
validates before it writes and always leaves a row, so a name that saves always
clears the guard.

Do NOT run tsr generate by hand - the vite plugin is the only generator; see the
note in package.json.

Kill stray dev servers by port first: a second pnpm dev silently binds 3001 and
you end up testing a stale server.
acceptance_criteria: A cold signup lands on the profile form rather than the dashboard, and after submitting reaches the dashboard where Create a Team works. A one-character name saves and does NOT bounce back. Screenshotted light and dark on a touch viewport.
close_reason:
Task 6 shipped in ff3d50f. /complete-profile route + dashboard needsProfile guard; 294 unit tests, tsc, build, and pnpm e2e 12/12 all green (I re-ran all four); beta deploy 32549529416 green incl. smoke test. Screenshots verified light and dark at 390x844 touch, no horizontal scroll.

Owner rulings during this task: (1) a skewed device clock no longer blocks account creation - completeProfileFor creates the player regardless and falls back to the server date for the recompute, because the strict bound would have locked the user out of the whole product via the guard's redirect loop. This drops requirePlausibleToday to six call sites; access.ts and scores.ts enumerations updated. (2) the form mirrors login.tsx rather than gating submit on isCompleteName - a content-gated disabled button left the tab order, ignored Enter, and showed no error text anywhere, indefensible on the product's biggest funnel screen.

Review found: login.spec.ts would have gone red (its account has no player row, so the new guard redirects it) and the plan never mentioned it; the plan's controlled inputs reintroduced wordle-teams-2.2 on the account-creation screen (verified by driving with the client entry delayed 6s - the plan's draft wiped pre-hydration typing); the plan's comment overclaimed that the route guard goes through isCompleteName when it reads needsProfile; and two vacuous e2e assertions - both canSubmit and both onChange handlers could be deleted with the suite green, because every fill() landed pre-hydration. wordle-teams-obw's headline exposure (needsProfile inverted) is now closed by e2e; the other three remain wrapper-only and are recorded on that issue.

title: Task 5: leaveTeam - a member can remove themselves
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 5

Divergence 10, owner-sanctioned. v1 has no self-removal at any layer - its UI
hides remove on your own row and the only exit is asking the creator. Phase 3
ruled it out on parity grounds; the owner has now sanctioned it.

THE ONE TEAM MUTATION THAT IS NOT CREATOR-ONLY, and the exact mirror of
removeMember: that one lets the creator remove anybody but themselves, this one
lets anybody remove only themselves.

THE CREATOR CANNOT LEAVE - reusing CREATOR_NOT_REMOVABLE. Their exit is
deleteTeam. That keeps the Phase 3 invariant that a team always has somebody who
can administer it, and means no team can be emptied by leaving.

EXCEPT a creator-less team - the scoped-copy case Phase 3 recorded, where creator
is undefined and nobody is refused. If the last member leaves one, the team is
deleted with the same manual cascade deleteTeamFor uses, rather than being left
as an unreachable orphan.

Extracts cascadeDeleteTeam from deleteTeamFor so both use it. The pre-existing
deleteTeamFor tests must still pass - that is what proves the extraction changed
nothing.

Recomputes every month with a winner row: the leaver stops being eligible to have
won them, which is divergence 5's reasoning applied in reverse.

MUTATION-TEST STEP: delete the creator guard and confirm that test fails.
acceptance_criteria: A member leaves and every month with a winner row recomputes; the creator is refused by the mutation; a non-member is refused; and the last member of a creator-less team deletes it and cascades, leaving dailyScores intact.
close_reason: Task 5 shipped in 4cc66b5. leaveTeamFor/leaveTeam - the one mutation on an existing team that is not creator-only; creator refused with CREATOR_NOT_REMOVABLE; last member of a team with no creator on its roster deletes it via the extracted cascadeDeleteTeam; recomputes every month with a winner row; dailyScores survive. 292 tests, tsc/build clean, beta deploy 32545325059 green incl. smoke test. Review found and fixed: the plan's recompute test set up ONE month while named for every month (a first-month-only mutant survived it); nothing pinned requirePlausibleToday (that mutant survived all five drafted tests); all five drafted tests used bare rejects.toThrow, so a guard throwing the wrong code survived; the cascade comment claimed a creator-less team could not be JOINED, false because completeProfileFor scans every team with no creator check; the clock-ordering promise was untested on both leaveTeamFor and removeMemberFor; and access.ts/scores.ts still enumerated six requirePlausibleToday call sites when there are now seven. cascadeDeleteTeam now takes Doc<'teams'> so an unauthorized call is visually anomalous. 21 mutants, zero survivors; I independently re-verified the two headline mutants against a valid control.

title: Task 4: cancelInvite + getTeamInvites, creator-only
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 4

Divergence 6. v1 exposes pending invites nowhere - a creator cannot see who they
invited, tell a typo from a slow responder, or cancel. Production carried 44
pending invites across 33 teams when this was written.

DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED INTO getMyTeams. That query picks its fields explicitly
so invited cannot reach the wire, and it is fetched by every connected client.
These are real email addresses. This is a separate, creator-scoped read of ONE
team.

The refusal must be in the query, not merely a hidden button - that is what the
negative test pins.

Cancel compares case-insensitively for the same reason completeProfileFor does:
copied rows predate v1's own case fix, so a stored address cannot be assumed
lowercase, and an invite that cannot be cancelled is exactly the trap this
surface exists to remove.
acceptance_criteria: The creator sees pending invites and can cancel one case-insensitively; a member who is not the creator is refused by the QUERY as well as the mutation.
close_reason: Task 4 shipped in c613d66. getTeamInvitesFor/getTeamInvites (creator-only, one team) and cancelInviteFor/cancelInvite (creator-only, case- and whitespace-insensitive). 280 tests, tsc/build clean, beta deploy 32529253966 green incl. smoke test. Review found and fixed: the plan's cancel filter was missing .trim(); the plan's case-insensitivity test could not detect any case defect (odd casing was on the submitted side, which normaliseInviteEmail flattens first); the unnormalised-read doc claim was unpinned; the read-normalise comment overclaimed that mixed case can reach v2 (the copy lowercases twice) and contradicted players.ts; cancelInviteFor patched unconditionally, paying a getMyTeams broadcast on a no-op. wt-ksh.5.3 deliberately left open - it needs Task 7's UI. Follow-up filed: wordle-teams-bxu.

title: Task 3: invitePlayer with four reported outcomes + invite email
description:
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md, Task 3

Invites live in convex/teams.ts because its module header already says so:
adding and removing people is membership, and removeMember is their nearest
sibling.

Ports v1's invitePlayer, whose three branches are kept and whose reporting is
not. v1 returns "Successfully invited player" for ALL of them - including the
case where nothing happened at all, which is an outright lie. Divergence 9.

Returns a discriminated InviteOutcome rather than void. The added branch carries
firstName because it confirms the address matched a real account, which is the
most useful thing to learn after inviting by email.

The email SEND is left to the mutation wrapper so invitePlayerFor stays db-only
and testable through convex-test's ctx.run - the same split every other helper in
this module uses. resend.sendEmail accepts a MutationCtx, so the send enqueues
inside the same transaction as the invited write; no action hop.

NO EMAIL is sent when an existing player is added directly. That is v1's
behaviour - they are simply on the team next time they look. Parity, deliberately
kept and recorded in the design.

Hand-written HTML in convex/inviteEmails.ts, matching authEmails.ts. No
react-email; that is Phase 6.

MUTATION-TEST STEP: drop the toLowerCase from normaliseInviteEmail and confirm
the case-insensitive tests fail.
acceptance_criteria: All four branches proven: an existing player is added and past months recompute; an already-member reports already_member and changes nothing; an unknown address is parked lowercased; a repeat reports resent without duplicating. A non-creator is refused by the mutation.
close_reason: invitePlayer with four reported outcomes + invite email; 36-mutant battery, 0 survivors. Review caught the added branch not clearing invited (would have shown a member as permanently pending in Task 7) and v1's fourth branch, now divergence 11

title: Confirm the live cross-player scoreboard update on beta, using the real invite path
description:
OWNER DECISION, 2026-08-20: deferred from Phase 3 to Phase 4.

The manual two-browser check of the live scoreboard update — enter a score as one player, watch it appear on a teammate's dashboard with no refresh — is deferred until invite functionality exists.

Why: getting a second real player onto a team on beta today would need hand-seeding, because a v2 signup has no players row at all (wt-ksh.5.1) and players.legacyId is a required Supabase auth uuid, so creating one means either widening the schema or inventing a fake Supabase identity. The owner declined to do that just to unblock a test. Doing the check after invites land means exercising the real path rather than data assembled by hand.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN, and does not need redoing:
wt-ksh.4.1 is closed and AUTOMATED. v2/e2e/teams.spec.ts drives two independent Playwright browser contexts — separate storage state, two different signed-in players, one shared team — has player A enter a board, and asserts player A's cell as rendered on player B's page, with no reload anywhere in B's path and no interaction with B. It was proven load-bearing by taking B's context offline and confirming the test fails identically. It runs on every pnpm e2e.

So the mechanism is proven. What is deferred is the confirmation against the beta deployment with two real browsers and two real accounts, as part of wt-ksh.4's side-by-side done-when.

DO THIS once invites work: invite a second real address to a team on beta, sign in as both in two browsers, enter a board as one, confirm the other's table updates untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Two real accounts on one team on beta: a board entered by one appears in the other's browser with no refresh.
notes:
READY FOR THE OWNER, 2026-08-22. Everything this needs is deployed to beta; the check itself cannot be done by an agent.

WHY NOT: beta does not run E2E_TEST_MODE (no reference in .github/workflows/deploy-v2.yml or the wrangler config), so sign-in OTPs go to real inboxes. There is no way for me to receive them. That is also correct behaviour - see wordle-teams-7az.

DO wordle-teams-96l FIRST (P1). invitePlayer has no isE2eEmail guard and convex/email.ts constructs Resend with testMode: false, so invites send real mail over the PRODUCTION sending domain. That does not block a check using two of your own real addresses, but it does mean do not use throwaway addresses that will bounce.

THE CHECK: on beta, with two real browsers and two real accounts, through the REAL invite path - invite the second address to a team, complete its profile, then enter a board as one and confirm the other's table updates with NO refresh and NO interaction. It was deferred from Phase 3 precisely so it could run through invites rather than hand-seeded data.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN LOCALLY: e2e/invites.spec.ts drives the whole invite -> sign-in -> complete-profile -> land-on-team path, and e2e/teams.spec.ts already pins 'a board entered by one player updates a teammate's table with no reload'. What this issue adds is that both hold on beta, with real accounts, reached through invites.

wt-ksh.5 (the Phase 4 epic) stays OPEN until this closes - it is acceptance criterion 7.
close_reason:
CONFIRMED WORKING BY THE OWNER on beta, 2026-08-24, through the real invite path with two real accounts and two real browsers: a board entered by one appeared in the other's table with no refresh and no interaction.

This was deferred from Phase 3 precisely so it could be exercised through invites rather than hand-seeded data, and it could not be done by an agent - beta does not run E2E_TEST_MODE, so sign-in OTPs go to real inboxes.

What backs it up in automation: e2e/invites.spec.ts drives the whole invite -> sign-in -> complete-profile -> land-on-team path locally, and e2e/teams.spec.ts pins 'a board entered by one player updates a teammate's table with no reload'. What the owner's check added is that both hold on beta, with real accounts, reached through invites.

title: Completing a profile does not recompute the months that player was excluded from
description:
Found by the whole-phase review of Phase 3, 2026-08-19. Inert today, live the moment Phase 4 ships.

hasCompleteProfile (convex/lib/player.ts) excludes a player with no firstName/lastName from the scores table, the team card and the monthly-winner computation. That is correct — a just-accepted invitee has no name yet, and v1's own code crashes on one.

But NOTHING RECOMPUTES WINNERS WHEN A PROFILE BECOMES COMPLETE. There is no players write mutation in v2 today, so this cannot happen yet. Phase 4 adds the complete-profile flow, and from that moment: a player finishes onboarding, and every past month they could have won stays wrong forever.

monthsWithWinners does not help — it returns months that already have a winner row, and the newly-complete player was excluded from every one of those computations. Only a board entry for the CURRENT month recomputes anything.

Fix direction: whatever mutation sets firstName/lastName should call recomputeTeamMonths for every team the player is on, across monthsWithWinners. winners.ts already exposes exactly that entry point — this is the third caller it was extracted for (wordle-teams-4gj).
acceptance_criteria: Setting a player's name recomputes every month their team has a winner row for.
close_reason: Closed by Phase 4 Task 2 (wt-ksh.5.14). completeProfileFor claims every invite waiting on the address and recomputes each month those teams already have a winner row for, via monthsWithWinners + recomputeTeamMonths. Unit-tested with a two-month fixture at fixed past months (2025-06 and 2025-07); mutation-tested - recompute-only-the-current-month and recompute-only-the-first-month mutants both die. The original one-month fixture in the plan could not detect either, which the review caught. Was correctly blocked on wt-ksh.5.1 until Task 6 shipped the route that makes profile completion reachable at all.

title: Split the scoring-system slice out of convex/teams.ts
description:
Recommendation from Task 8's code review, to act on once Phase 3's UI tasks are done.

convex/teams.ts is now the largest file in convex/ — a read query, five mutations and three private guards.

The seam is NOT arbitrary line count. createTeam / updateTeam / deleteTeam / removeMember / getMyTeams / amIPro all read or write team IDENTITY and MEMBERSHIP: name, playerIds, creator, playWeekends, showLetters. setScoringSystemFor / setScoringSystem / SYSTEM_FIELDS / requireValues are the one cluster that never touches those fields and only touches the scoringSystems table. That is a genuinely separable concern.

Suggested: extract that block to convex/scoringSystems.ts — plural, because convex/lib/scoringSystem.ts already owns the singular name and a bare scoringSystem.ts in convex/ would confuse.

It needs requireTeamCreatorFor, monthOf, recomputeTeamMonths, monthsWithWinners and the ScoringSystem type — all already imported elsewhere — plus a decision on requirePlausibleToday, which teams.ts currently shares across three call sites and would need to export.

requireName and TeamSettings stay with createTeam/updateTeam; they are identity concerns.

Deliberately deferred during the phase: splitting mid-phase, after only three of five mutations existed, would have drawn the boundary in the wrong place.
acceptance_criteria: convex/teams.ts holds team identity and membership; the scoringSystems mutations live in their own module.
notes: Whole-phase review, 2026-08-19: the seam is confirmed correct and teams.ts is now 391 lines — but the TIMING argument has flipped. This issue said splitting mid-phase would draw the boundary wrong, which was right at the time. Phase 4 adds INVITE mutations to this same file, and invites are team-identity concerns that would land on the wrong side of an un-drawn line. Do it BEFORE Phase 4 starts, not 'sometime'.
close_reason:
Done in 81ddda4 (the split) and 1e3d8b0 (boundary declared from both sides).

teams.ts 391 -> 288 lines, holding only team identity and membership. New convex/scoringSystems.ts, 105 lines, touching only the scoringSystems table. requirePlausibleToday moved to access.ts alongside the other require* guards, and scores.ts's inline copy of the same bound was folded onto it — three call sites became four.

Spec review confirmed behaviour-preserving: the moved code is byte-identical aside from imports, the moved tests' assertions are byte-identical, the total is unchanged at 209, and — the subtle one — boardIsValid still runs BEFORE the date bound in upsertBoardFor, so the code thrown first for a doubly-invalid request is unchanged.

Quality review found the boundary was declared in scoringSystems.ts but not in teams.ts — the same-decision-in-one-file-not-its-sibling failure this codebase keeps hitting. Fixed, and teams.ts now says explicitly that invites belong on its side.

Recorded but not acted on: scoringSystems.ts vs lib/scoringSystem.ts differ by one letter, where the existing convention (scores.ts vs lib/scoring.ts) differs by word form. Deliberate and documented, but worth a naming-convention note if the pattern repeats.

209 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 8/8.
