Do NOT start implementation from this body: run the full brainstorming flow first, replace this description with the approved design (scope, decisions + alternatives ruled out, out-of-scope), then create child issues per atomic task. Sequenced after roadmap #2 (screenshot import).

title: Board import from a pasted screenshot (paid) — post-v2 roadmap #2
description:
# Post-v2 roadmap #2 — Board import from a screenshot (PAID / Pro)

**Status:** stub. Needs the full brainstorming flow before any planning or code.

## What and why

Let a player paste (or upload) a screenshot of their finished Wordle board and have the
app parse the guesses and fill the board in for them, instead of retyping five or six
five-letter words by hand.

Manual entry is the single largest piece of friction in the daily loop, and the loop is
the product. It is also the most legible "worth paying for" feature we have: the value is
immediate, obvious in a demo, repeats daily, and has a real marginal cost, which makes it
an honest thing to put behind Pro rather than an artificial gate.

## Open questions for brainstorming (not decisions)

- **Do we need letters, or only colors?** We store the actual guessed words, not just the
  green/yellow pattern. A screenshot of the NYT board *does* contain letters; the shared
  emoji grid does **not**. That difference decides everything below.
- Cheaper 80% first: paste the *share text* (emoji grid) to populate the color pattern,
  and treat screenshot-with-letters as the real feature? Worth costing as a separate,
  possibly free, stepping stone.
- Parsing approach: deterministic image processing of the tile grid (crop → grid detect →
  per-tile color + character recognition) versus a vision model call. Trade-off is
  accuracy on messy crops vs. per-parse vendor cost, latency, and offline behavior.
- Input variety we must survive: light/dark mode, iOS vs Android, NYT app vs web, partial
  crops, status bars, screenshots of screenshots, non-English keyboards, Hard Mode.
- Confirm-before-save UX: never silently write a parsed board. Show the parse, let the
  user fix a letter or a row, then save. This is also our accuracy feedback channel.
- Where does the image go? Strong preference: parse and discard, never persist. If a
  vendor call is involved, what leaves our boundary and what do we say about it publicly.
- Quota and abuse: parses per user per day, and what happens on the free tier (zero? a
  taste? a hard paywall at first attempt?).
- Failure path: always a one-tap fall back to manual entry. A failed parse must never
  cost the user their board.
- Cheat surface: does image import make it easier to enter a board you did not play, and
  do we care? (Teams are friends; the honor system already applies.)
- Unit cost: per-parse cost × expected daily parses per Pro user has to fit inside the
  Pro price with room. Model it before choosing the approach.

## Explicitly out of scope until argued otherwise

Importing other games' boards, bulk/backfill import of historical screenshots, OCR of
someone else's board to enter on their behalf.
acceptance_criteria: Brainstorming complete and this epic body replaced with an approved design; child issues created for each atomic task; parse accuracy measured on a labeled corpus of real user screenshots (light/dark, iOS/Android, app/web) with a stated pass bar; feature shipped gated to Pro with a per-parse unit cost documented against the Pro price.
notes: STUB EPIC — not ready to build. Post-v2 roadmap item 2 of 7. Do NOT start implementation from this body: run the full brainstorming flow first, replace this description with the approved design (scope, decisions + alternatives ruled out, out-of-scope), then create child issues per atomic task. Sequenced after roadmap #1 (team chat).

title: Team chat (free) — post-v2 roadmap #1
description:
# Post-v2 roadmap #1 — Team chat (FREE tier)

**Status:** stub. Needs the full brainstorming flow before any planning or code.

## What and why

An in-app chat surface inside each team. Free for everyone — this is a retention and
activation play, not a monetizable add-on.

The funnel data is the argument: 87% of prod signups have never entered a single board
(wordle-teams-456), and the only independent team that ever showed sustained multi-user
usage was a 5-player team that talked to each other in volume before churning. A team
with nothing but a scoreboard gives you one reason to open the app per day, and only if
you already played. Chat gives teammates a reason to come back that does not depend on
having entered a board yet — and gives the person who created the team a way to nudge
the four people who never started.

Convex reactivity makes realtime messaging close to free to *build*, which is why this is
first: highest engagement leverage per unit of implementation effort on the new stack.

## Open questions for brainstorming (not decisions)

- One channel per team, or threads/topics? Almost certainly one channel for v1 — confirm.
- **Cost sizing before anything else.** Convex *database bandwidth*, not function calls,
  is our binding free-tier limit (wordle-teams-dcu). Chat is the first feature with a
  genuinely chatty read pattern, on the free tier, for every team. Model reads per active
  team per day before committing to a design.
- Message retention — infinite history, or a rolling window (also a cost lever)?
- Notifications: reuse the Convex cron + web-push + Resend plumbing from Phase 6, or
  in-app unread badges only? Push-per-message is a spam and cost risk.
- Unread state and badge counts — per-user read cursors, and where they live.
- Scope of message content: plain text only, or emoji/reactions/images? Images pull in
  file storage and moderation.
- Moderation and abuse: delete own message, team owner delete any, report path.
  Small teams of friends today, but this is the first user-generated-content surface in
  the product and the first one that could require us to act on a complaint.
- Rate limiting and message size caps.
- Membership rules: members only, and what happens to messages when someone leaves or a
  team is deleted.
- Does chat show up on the scoreboard screen or as its own tab? Mobile-first — traffic is
  heavily iPhone.

## Explicitly out of scope until argued otherwise

Cross-team/global chat, DMs, voice, file sharing, chat search.
acceptance_criteria: Brainstorming complete and this epic body replaced with an approved design; child issues created for each atomic task; chat shipped to production for real teams; Convex bandwidth cost per active team measured against the free-tier ceiling before GA.
notes: STUB EPIC — not ready to build. Post-v2 roadmap item 1 of 7. Do NOT start implementation from this body: run the full brainstorming flow first, replace this description with the approved design (scope, decisions + alternatives ruled out, out-of-scope), then create child issues per atomic task. Blocked on v2 cutover (wt-ksh.9).

title: Convex free-tier risk: database bandwidth, not function calls, is the binding limit
description:
Sizing check against Convex free tier (0.5GB db storage / 1M function calls / 1GB database I/O / 1GB egress) found storage and function calls have huge headroom, but database I/O is the metric that could actually blow the free tier.

Convex bills database bandwidth on data SCANNED, even if filtered out, and counts reactive subscription re-runs as function calls. The schema comment on the teams table says there is no index for 'teams containing player X' because Convex cannot index array membership, so the intended approach is collect-and-filter over all teams.

A full teams scan is ~88KB today (171 rows). At 1GB/month that is only ~10k executions of that one query before the free tier cap. Two amplifiers make that reachable: it likely runs on every page load, and a write to ANY team invalidates the subscription for EVERY connected client. Free plan caps are hard - mutations start failing rather than generating a bill.

Mitigation to decide before Phase 3 queries land: a teamMemberships join table (playerId, teamId) with a by_player index, so a player's team lookup reads O(their teams) instead of O(all teams). Revisit the schema.ts comment that ruled this out.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded (join table vs collect-and-filter) with the database-I/O math behind it, and if collect-and-filter is kept, Convex usage dashboard is checked against the 1GB database I/O line after Phase 3 queries ship.

title: v1: boards entered in another timezone show on the wrong day for teammates
description:
Reported by the owner from lived experience: travel to another timezone, enter a board, and teammates cannot see that score on the day it belongs to.

CAUSE, confirmed in code and data. daily_scores.date is a 'timestamp with time zone' — an INSTANT — and nothing stores which puzzle day a board belongs to. src/lib/types.ts:179 decides that with isSameDay(new Date(s.date), day), which resolves the stored instant in whatever timezone the VIEWER is in. Board entry (src/components/action-buttons/board-entry/form.tsx:154) sends date.toISOString(), so the instant reflects the ENTERER's local day, and every other viewer re-derives a day from it in their own zone.

SIZE, measured across all 7468 production rows (scripts/prod-score-day-ambiguity.mjs):
  733 rows land on a different calendar day in UTC than in America/Chicago
  581 rows differ between UTC and the player's own recorded timezone
  160 rows differ between America/Chicago and the player's own timezone
  8 players have no recorded timezone at all
  57 distinct player timezones exist in production — Auckland, Tokyo, Cairo, Honolulu, most of Europe

So roughly one board in thirteen can appear on the wrong day depending on who is looking. This is not a rare edge case; the user base is genuinely global.

The stored time-of-day is a broad spread peaking at 12-13:00Z rather than a normalised midnight, which confirms v1 stores 'when you submitted' rather than 'which puzzle this is'. Only 20 rows sit at 06:00Z.

DECISION 2026-08-12: FIX IN v2 ONLY, DO NOT FIX v1. v2 stores puzzleDay ('YYYY-MM-DD') as a first-class field and groups by it, so every viewer agrees regardless of where they are; historical rows are backfilled in each player's own timezone. Fixing v1 as well would mean a Postgres migration plus changes to board entry and scoreboard rendering on the live app — the same work twice, on a system cutover retires. v1 has carried this for years.

This issue exists so the behaviour is understood rather than rediscovered, and so anyone hitting it before cutover gets a real answer.
acceptance_criteria: Closed at cutover, when v2 serves the production domain and puzzleDay is the stored fact. No v1 code change expected.
notes:
FIXED by PR #162 (branch fix/me-hydration), not yet merged. Filed 2026-08-12 from lived experience; I hit the same bug from the other end on 2026-08-17 while chasing a hydration error on /me (wordle-teams-dyp) and did not know this issue existed until afterwards.

Same cause, independently confirmed: instant-not-day, resolved in the viewer's zone. Measurements agree — this issue recorded 733/581/160 across 7468 rows on 2026-08-12, I measured 734/582/160 across 7495 rows on 2026-08-17. The deltas are just the ~27 rows entered since.

The fix attributes a board to the day it was in the SCORE OWNER'S recorded timezone (players.time_zone), read from the database rather than the runtime, so the server, the browser and every teammate agree. src/lib/score-day.ts holds the rule.

NOT fully closed by that PR: board-entry/form.tsx:154 still sends date.toISOString(), so the stored value is still an instant reflecting the enterer's local day. Display is now consistent; the underlying representation is not. Storing the puzzle day explicitly remains v2's job.

Close this together with dyp once #162 ships.

title: Production has 5 duplicate daily_scores rows for the same player and date
description:
Found while building the v2 copy script (wt-ksh.2.8). Production daily_scores holds 7468 rows across 7463 distinct (player_id, date) pairs — 5 pairs have two rows each.

CAUSE: there is no uniqueness constraint on (player_id, date), and upsertBoard (src/app/me/actions.ts:195-250) does not upsert. It UPDATEs by id when the client already has a scoreId and INSERTs otherwise. A submit that fires twice before the client learns its new id therefore creates two rows. Four of the five pairs were created 1-3 seconds apart, which is the signature of exactly that. The remaining pair is 40 seconds apart and its two rows DIFFER in content.

Dates affected: 2024-11-17, 2025-01-09, 2025-12-25, 2026-01-10, 2026-04-05.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: if the scoreboard sums a player's daily_scores, a duplicated day is counted twice, so five months of standings may be very slightly wrong. Worth confirming against the scoring code before deciding.

RELATED, ALREADY FIXED: a335ae8 (wordle-teams-5zs) hardened board submit so a failure can no longer leave the form stuck or silently lose an entry. That reduces the chance of new duplicates but does not add a constraint, so the door is still open.

OPTIONS: add a unique index on (player_id, date) and de-duplicate the five, or make upsertBoard a real upsert, or accept and clean up the five by hand. Note that v1 stores Wed Aug 12 03:12:29 PM CDT 2026 as timestamptz with an inconsistent time-of-day, so a naive unique index on the raw column would not catch two entries made for the same calendar day at different times.

THE v2 COPY DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REPAIR THIS. It keys on the Supabase primary key and copies all 7468 rows, so the Phase 7 parity check compares like with like. Collapsing them during the copy would have made Convex disagree with Supabase for a reason the check could not explain.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on whether to de-duplicate and constrain, and if so the five pairs resolved in production.
notes: Reproduce with scripts/prod-duplicate-scores.mjs (read-only, prints dates and counts, no addresses).

title: P1.T7: Parity spot-check script (Supabase vs Convex)
description:
Assert row counts per table and a couple of known aggregates — a specific month's winner is the design's example — match between Supabase and Convex for whatever scope was copied.

This is the design's 'parity spot-checks' testing pillar. It matters more than it looks: the copy runs again at Phase 7 and once more in the cutover window, and a silent undercount discovered after the DNS flip is the worst possible time to find it.

Depends on P1.T6.
acceptance_criteria: Passes against a fresh copy run and fails loudly when a count drifts.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-12. v2/scripts/verify-parity.mjs, green against beta for scope=mine: 6948 daily scores across 18 players and 6 teams, every puzzleDay histogram agreeing, exit 0.

WHAT IT COMPARES: row counts for all six tables; team name, member count and the normalised invited set; the FULL monthly-winner set as (team, year, month) -> winner rather than the design's single sample; membership statuses; and a per-player daily-score fingerprint of count, total guesses and a puzzleDay histogram. The histogram is the part that would catch a board landing on the wrong day, which is the failure the whole puzzleDay change exists to prevent.

PROVEN TO FAIL, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS. Injected one bogus score into Convex and the check caught it four independent ways — dailyScores total, that player's count, their guess total, and their puzzleDay histogram — and exited 1. Then purged, re-copied and re-verified clean. A check that has only ever returned OK is not evidence of anything.

SHARED SCOPE MODULE: scripts/lib/supabase-scope.mjs now owns connect, readScoped and puzzleDayFor, imported by both the copy and the verify scripts. They MUST agree about what is in scope and how a puzzle day is derived; if they drifted, the verifier would report mismatches that are really two scripts disagreeing, and the instinct would be to distrust the data rather than the tooling.

CONVEX-SIDE: migrate.parityProbe returns everything from the small tables in one call; migrate.playerScoreFingerprint runs one player at a time because Convex bounds reads per execution and the scoped set alone is ~7000 rows. Both internal, both needing CONVEX_MIGRATION_KEY.

FOR PHASE 7 AND CUTOVER: run with --scope=all. Expect the run to be slower and the fingerprint loop to make one call per player, so ~530 calls.
close_reason: Parity check green against beta and proven to fail on injected corruption, catching it four independent ways and exiting non-zero. Scope resolution and the puzzleDay rule now shared with the copy script so the two cannot drift.

title: P1.T4: OAuth console registrations for four providers (manual)
description:
Owner-only step. Register OAuth apps for Google, Azure, GitHub and Discord, each with the beta.wordleteams.com callback, and set client ids and secrets on the Convex deployment. Never in the repo — it is public.

PROVIDER LIST IS DATA-DRIVEN AND DIFFERS FROM THE DESIGN. Production 2026-08-11 (scripts/prod-auth-providers.mjs, 530 auth users): google 236 linked, azure 15, discord 6, github 6, twitter 2, slack 0. The design proposed dropping discord and keeping twitter, which is inverted against usage.

AMENDED 2026-08-17: slack dropped (zero users) AND X/Twitter dropped (2 users, both with confirmed emails who can use OTP; X retired its free tier and better-auth spends two metered /2/users/me calls per sign-in; the v1 app is OAuth 1.0a and unusable by v2 anyway). See wordle-teams-aw3. Final list is FOUR: google, azure, github, discord.

PROD callbacks are NOT part of this — they go in the pre-cutover week, Phase 8.
acceptance_criteria: All five app registrations exist with beta callback URLs and their credentials set on the Convex deployment.
notes: 2026-08-17: 4 of 5 registered (google, azure, github, discord). X/Twitter outstanding — existing app not locatable in the X portal. Root cause and required config in wordle-teams-aw3. Whether to carry X at all is now a live decision, not a settled one.
close_reason: All four OAuth apps registered with beta callbacks and credentials set on Convex prod. Amended from five to four: slack had zero users, X/Twitter dropped (wordle-teams-aw3). All four callbacks verified working by real sign-in.

title: v2 pages still carry the scaffold title 'TanStack Start Starter'
description:
The SSR document served by https://beta.wordleteams.com/login has <title>TanStack Start Starter</title> — the C3 scaffold default, never replaced. Visible in the browser tab, in search results, when a link is shared, and in the PWA install prompt.

Distinct from wt-ksh.7.1, which covers the PWA MANIFEST identity (name, icons, theme colour). This is the document <title>, set in the router/route head config, and it would still be wrong even after the manifest is fixed.

Not urgent while beta is private, but it is the first thing anyone sees and it is a one-line fix per route or one default in __root.tsx.
acceptance_criteria: No route serves the string 'TanStack Start Starter'; the default title identifies Wordle Teams and per-route titles override it where the v1 app has them.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-03, verified on beta:
  /login  -> 'Login / Signup - Wordle Teams'
  /about  -> 'Wordle Teams: The ultimate app for Wordle enthusiasts'  (inherits the default)
  /       -> 'Dashboard - Wordle Teams'

Ported v1's scheme rather than inventing one (src/app/layout.tsx): default 'Wordle Teams: The ultimate app for Wordle enthusiasts', per-page template '%s - Wordle Teams'. Next applies that template automatically to nested pages; TanStack has no equivalent, so src/lib/seo.ts pageTitle() interpolates explicitly and each route calls it.

Two overrides, matching the only v1 pages that set their own title: /login from src/app/login/layout.tsx, and / from src/app/me/page.tsx — the signed-in landing screen, which is /me in v1 and / in v2, so the title follows the screen rather than the path.

SCOPED TO TITLES DELIBERATELY. description, openGraph and twitter metadata are still scaffold-shaped in v2. That is real parity work but it belongs to the Phase 7 route-by-route audit (wt-ksh.8), not here.

Worth knowing for future deploys: beta served a mix of old and new titles for roughly a minute after the deploy went green. Cloudflare retires in-flight isolates lazily, so verify twice before believing a deploy did not take — this looked exactly like a failed deploy and was not.
close_reason: Titles ported from v1 and verified on beta: /login 'Login / Signup - Wordle Teams', / 'Dashboard - Wordle Teams', everything else inheriting the v1 default. No route serves the scaffold string.

title: Confirm the first real Polar checkout end-to-end when it happens
description:
The Polar migration epic (wordle-teams-qp1) closed with every planned task done and verified as far as is possible WITHOUT a subscriber. Two of its acceptance criteria can only be confirmed by a real customer, and there are no Polar subscribers yet:

  - Criterion 1: a new user completes Polar checkout and lands on /me as pro without a manual refresh. Verified against the Polar SANDBOX API by scripts/verify-polar-sandbox.mjs (checkout.url and customerPortalUrl asserted against live responses), never against production with a real payment.
  - The Polar -> webhook -> notifyBilling -> LogSnag chain. scripts/verify-logsnag-billing.mjs proves the LogSnag half with the production token, but nothing has yet confirmed a real Polar delivery invokes it. See wordle-teams-sv2.

WHAT TO CHECK when the first real subscription lands:
  1. The subscriber reaches /me as pro without refreshing.
  2. A 'Subscription Started' event appears in LogSnag's 'billing' channel, tagged env=production.
  3. A row appears in webhook_events, processed=true with an empty processing_error.
  4. player_customer.membership_status is 'pro' for that player.

If 2 fails but 1, 3 and 4 succeed, the fault is between handlePolarEvent and notifyBilling, not the LogSnag credentials — those are already proven.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a real production Polar subscription has been observed completing checkout, granting pro without a manual refresh, writing a processed webhook_events row, and producing a 'Subscription Started' event in LogSnag's billing channel.

title: Publish Polar billing events to LogSnag, replacing the Lemon Squeezy integration
description:
Lemon Squeezy webhook endpoint 18808 posts to https://integ.logsnag.com/v1/lemonsqueezy/<id>, a purpose-built receiver that parses Lemon Squeezy payload shapes. It cannot be repointed at Polar — the payloads differ entirely — and LogSnag documents no Polar integration and no generic webhook receiver, only Zapier and Bubble.

No integration is needed. The app already talks to LogSnag directly (logsnagClient in src/lib/utils.ts:16, used at :313 for signups), and already receives and signature-verifies Polar webhooks in handlePolarEvent. Publishing billing events from there is provider-agnostic, needs no third-party bridge, and gives full control over what is tracked.

EVENTS (owner chose): subscription.active -> 'Subscription Started', subscription.canceled -> 'Cancellation Scheduled', subscription.revoked -> 'Subscription Ended', subscription.past_due -> 'Payment Failed'. Channel 'billing', notify true. subscription.canceled is included deliberately: it fires when a cancellation is SCHEDULED, well before access ends, and is the only signal that arrives while the person is still a customer.

CONSTRAINTS: must never throw or fail the webhook — a notification failure would return 500 and make Polar redeliver a membership change that already succeeded. Identify by player id, not email, to avoid sending further PII to a third party.

Unblocks deleting LS webhook 18808 (see wordle-teams-k6a).
acceptance_criteria: Done when: the four events reach LogSnag's billing channel from the Polar webhook, a LogSnag failure provably cannot fail the webhook, and LS webhook 18808 is deleted.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-03. PR #155 merged at 18:55Z (merge commit e04aed3); the production deploy built from it is Ready.

Acceptance, criterion by criterion:
  1. LS webhook 18808 deleted — verified, GET /v1/webhooks returns empty.
  2. A LogSnag failure provably cannot fail the webhook — holds by construction, in two layers. notifyBilling wraps its own track() call in try/catch and only log.warn's, and handlePolarEvent additionally wraps the whole body in try/catch. There is no path by which a LogSnag outage produces a non-2xx, so Polar cannot be made to redeliver a membership change that already succeeded.
  3. Events reach LogSnag's billing channel — verified as far as is possible without a subscriber, by scripts/verify-logsnag-billing.mjs (commit 1f5ab79), 7/7 passing. It publishes a real event to the real 'billing' channel with the production LOGSNAG_TOKEN, and statically asserts the four mappings, the channel, and that identification is by player id and never email.

RESIDUAL GAP, deliberately accepted: nothing yet confirms a real Polar delivery invokes notifyBilling, because no Polar billing event has occurred — there are still no Polar subscribers. What the script does cover is the set of failure modes that were actually plausible and silent: a rotated or wrong token, a project-name mismatch, a rejected payload shape. The first real subscription will be the end-to-end confirmation; if it does not appear in the 'billing' channel, the wiring between the webhook and notifyBilling is the place to look, not the LogSnag credentials.

Note: the billing channel contains two 'LogSnag Wiring Check' entries from running the script twice. Synthetic, marked as such, identified by a placeholder id rather than any real player.
close_reason: All three acceptance criteria met: LS webhook 18808 deleted, failure isolation verified structurally in two layers, and the LogSnag billing channel verified against the real service with the production token via scripts/verify-logsnag-billing.mjs (7/7). Residual gap recorded in notes — a real Polar delivery has not yet exercised the path end to end, since there are no Polar subscribers.

title:
Polar product descriptions contain literal HTML, showing

tags on checkout
description:
Both Polar products have HTML in their description field: Pro Annual : "

Pay annually and get two months free!

" Pro Monthly: "

Pay monthly

" Polar renders product descriptions as MARKDOWN, so the tags are displayed literally to the customer on the hosted checkout page. Confirmed by reading the descriptions back from the Polar API; nothing in this codebase sends product descriptions, so this is dashboard content only. Fix: edit both descriptions to plain text or Markdown, dropping the tags — Markdown produces paragraphs on its own. Must be done in the PRODUCTION organization as well as sandbox; they are separate instances with separate products. Owner-side, dashboard only, no code change.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: neither product description contains HTML tags in sandbox or production, and a checkout page renders the copy cleanly.
close_reason: Descriptions corrected; sandbox verified clean via the API, production confirmed by owner

title: next-axiom log.error from server actions never reaches Axiom
description:
When checkout failed on dev, src/lib/polar/checkout.ts ran log.error('Failed to create Polar checkout', { error, playerId }) — and NOTHING appeared in Axiom. Querying the vercel dataset for the window around the failing POST /me (2026-08-03T13:10:28Z) returned only request-level rows and the Supabase getSession warning; no application error log at all.

next-axiom buffers and needs a flush that server actions do not perform on their own (route handlers get it from withAxiom; actions do not). The practical effect is that every log.error in a server action or in code called from one is silently discarded, so the error-handling branches written across the Polar modules currently log into a void.

This cost real debugging time: the root cause had to be found by reproducing against the sandbox API locally rather than by reading logs, because the logs did not exist.

Affects all the catch blocks in src/lib/polar/*.ts and any other server-action logging in the app.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a deliberate failure inside a server action produces a visible error entry in Axiom, and the Polar catch blocks are confirmed to emit.

title: supabase start fails locally: storage container needs pgvector >= 0.7.0, image ships 0.4.0
description:
'supabase start' pulls the whole stack, applies all migrations successfully, then tears everything down because the storage-api container fails its healthcheck:

  Migration failed. Reason: An error occurred running 'init' ... pgvector >= 0.7.0 required for halfvec storage, found 0.4.0

The storage service retries, never becomes healthy, and the CLI reports LegacyHealthCheckTimeoutError and stops every container — including postgres. Net effect: no local database, so 'npm run gen-types' and any local migration testing are blocked.

The app does not use Supabase Storage, so excluding it is harmless. Working invocation:

  supabase start -x storage-api,imgproxy,studio,edge-runtime,logflare,vector,supavisor,realtime,mailpit

Discovered while verifying the Polar migration locally (wordle-teams-j8c), where the full stack had to come up to test the auth hook rewrite.

Real fix is probably bumping the postgres image version in supabase/config.toml, or updating the CLI (2.110.0 installed, 2.111.0 available). Worth resolving because ymy needs gen-types and P3 verification wants a local DB.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a plain 'supabase start' brings the stack up healthy, or supabase/config.toml and the README document the required exclude flags so the next session does not rediscover this.

title: Unexplained ~2.2s server time on prerendered marketing pages
description:
Split out of wordle-teams-sji, whose original explanation (middleware) turned out to be wrong — middleware was never running. The measurements are still real and still unexplained.

Axiom, production, 30 days, from vercel.source == 'lambda':
  /home      168 invocations  avg 2421ms   (also served 347x as 'static')
  /privacy    59 invocations  avg 2258ms
  /terms      54 invocations  avg 2159ms
  /about      97 invocations  avg  545ms
  /me        581 requests     avg 2069ms  p95 4138ms  max 6691ms

All of /home, /privacy, /terms are marked ○ (Static) in the build output, so they should be pure CDN hits with no function involved. Something is causing a CDN miss and a cold Next server render anyway.

Contrast: / averages 142ms, because the Sentry uptime bot pings it constantly and keeps it warm. That is strong evidence the 2.2s is cold-start-dominated rather than render-dominated — at ~5 human visits a day on these routes, the function is cold essentially every time.

This is the remaining half of the original churn hypothesis: real-user p75 LCP is 3678ms and p75 FCP 3605ms, both 'poor', while p75 TTFB is only 297ms (that sample is dominated by warm repeat visits from the ~6 daily actives).
acceptance_criteria: Explain why prerendered routes invoke a function at all — check Cache-Control / CDN cache headers on /home, /privacy, /terms in production, and whether anything in the root layout or a shared component opts them into dynamic rendering. Then either get them CDN-cached or accept and document the cold-start cost. Target p75 LCP under 2500ms.
notes: Do not re-blame middleware: after the fix in wordle-teams-sji it only matches /, /login, /me, /branding, /complete-profile. Re-measure after that ships, since the numbers above were taken while middleware was not running at all — whatever causes them is still present and unrelated.

title: Axiom leftovers: forced logouts on refresh-token loss, and monthly-winners RPC failures
description:
Two production log signals from the 2026-07-30 Axiom pass that were noted in analysis but never tracked.

1. FORCED LOGOUTS. 30d production: 8x 'Error [AuthApiError]: Invalid Refresh Token: Refresh Token Not Found' (code refresh_token_not_found) on /me and /login, plus 3x 'failed to get session, trying session refresh' and 3x 'Session refresh error, logging out: Auth session missing!'. Each one is a user silently kicked back to sign-in. On a passwordless app that means an entire magic-link or OAuth round trip to get back in — and given only ~12 people completed auth in 30 days (wordle-teams-390), losing a returning user this way is expensive. Low absolute count, but the app has ~6 daily actives, so this is not rare per-user. Worth checking whether src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts:49-51 is racing concurrent refreshes: the comment there warns that logic between createServerClient and getUser() causes exactly this symptom, and the middleware runs on nearly every request (wordle-teams-sji).

2. MONTHLY WINNERS RPC. Two single errors in 30d: 'Failed to get monthly winner' (monthly-winner-celebration.tsx:43, 2026-07-12) and 'Failed to update winners table' (board-entry/form.tsx:99, 2026-07-05). The second is the more interesting one: the update_monthly_winners RPC failure is only log.error'd, and the user still sees a success toast for their board entry while the winners table silently goes stale. Whoever entered that board has a wrong winner recorded for their team that month.

Both are low-volume, so neither is urgent — but both are silent-failure shaped, which is the category that produced wordle-teams-jvt.
acceptance_criteria: For (1): determine whether the refresh-token loss is ordinary cookie expiry or a middleware refresh race, and stop logging it as an error if it is expected. For (2): surface update_monthly_winners failures to the user or retry them, so a board entry cannot report success while leaving winners stale.
notes: Reproduce the log query with: node scripts/axiom-query.mjs "['vercel'] | where ['vercel.environment'] == 'production' and level in ('error','warn') | project _time, level, message | sort by _time desc" 30d — note Axiom retention is only 30 days (wordle-teams-g8h).
close_reason: Shipped 2026-07-31 (main b796d7d, via dev 3071b29). 5zs: handleSubmit now wrapped in try/catch with setSubmitting(false) in finally, a toast telling the user their entry is preserved, and the sheet closing only on success (it previously closed on the handled failure path too, discarding what they had typed). io0: update_monthly_winners failure now surfaces a warning toast instead of a bare success while standings go stale; getUser/getSession stop calling refreshSession() when the error is literally 'Refresh Token Not Found', which cannot succeed, and log at info instead. Investigation found the forced-logout half was not a user-facing fault: zero events in 12h, and the historical ones collapse to two real session expiries amplified into 4-6 log lines by parallel checks each retrying. Typecheck and build clean; not exercised end-to-end because board entry requires an authenticated session.

title: Service worker registration fails in production — PWA install/offline broken for some users
description:
Sentry 7481850095, production, 10 events / 2 users, first 2026-05-14, last 2026-07-27:

  TypeError: Failed to register a ServiceWorker for scope ('https://wordleteams.com/')
  with script ('https://wordleteams.com/sw.js'): An unknown error occurred when fetching the script.

Seen on both / and /home. Three further singleton issues are the same code path failing at a different point, all production:

  7630550063  Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scope')    /
  7629232232  Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scope')    /
  7629232309  Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'waiting')  /

The 'scope' and 'waiting' reads are almost certainly unguarded access to a ServiceWorkerRegistration that is undefined precisely because registration failed — so the registration handler in src/components/service-worker-registration.tsx does not defend against its own failure path, the same shape of bug as wordle-teams-jvt.

This matters beyond the error count: the app is a PWA, app-bar-base.tsx flags has_pwa on standalone launch, and a failed registration means no install prompt and no offline support for the affected user. Low event count, but the population that hits it is invisible — a user who cannot install simply does not come back.
acceptance_criteria: Guard every access to the registration object so a failed register() cannot throw a second error. Determine why sw.js fetch fails ('unknown error' usually means a network blip, an aborted navigation, or a bad Content-Type/scope header) and confirm next-pwa is emitting sw.js with the right headers in production. Verify no new events on 7481850095 after the fix.
notes:
DEPLOYED 2026-07-31 (main 418069d, via dev 67ca3d4).

ROOT CAUSE was double registration, not an unguarded handler as originally filed. Verified in production by wrapping navigator.serviceWorker.register: it was called twice per page load — once by @serwist/window (chunk 6537, serwist injects registration by default) and once by our own component. Serwist's call has no rejection handler, which is why failures reached Sentry with mechanism onunhandledrejection despite our component passing an error handler.

FIX: register: false in the serwist config, plus our component rewritten to async/await with try/catch, logging failure as a warning. Verified on a local production build: register() called exactly once, worker reaches state 'activated' at scope /, manifest link intact, no page errors.

THREE OF THE FOUR SENTRY ISSUES WERE NOT BUGS:
  7481850095  REAL — 10 events, 2 Chrome/Windows users since 2026-05-14. This is the one the fix targets.
  7629232309  NOT REAL — breadcrumb 'Service Worker registration blocked by Playwright'; our own test run.
  7630550063  NOT REAL — stack frames in ext:core/01_core.js, a Deno runtime; a crawler.
  (the third singleton 7629232232 is the same shape as 7630550063)
All three noise issues originate in @serwist/window's register path and should stop now the duplicate registration is gone.

BASELINE for the watch — 7481850095: 10 events, 2 users, last 2026-07-27T03:19:18Z. Check with: node scripts/sentry-query.mjs issue 7481850095. Low frequency (10 events in 2.5 months) means silence proves little quickly; the stronger near-term signal is that the three noise issues stop accruing.
close_reason: Verified in production 2026-07-31 on build layout-f9f3b86a3944759c. register() now called exactly once (was twice: @serwist/window plus our component), the worker reaches state 'activated' at scope https://wordleteams.com/, manifest link intact, no page errors. Full regression sweep on the same build also clean: P0 login check PASSes with lemon.js allowed and blocked, /home /privacy /terms all x-vercel-cache HIT, /me still 307. Watch Sentry 7481850095 (baseline 10 events / 2 users / last 2026-07-27) plus the two noise issues 7629232309 and 7630550063, which originated in the serwist register path that no longer runs.

title: Observability gaps blocking churn analysis: Sentry unreadable, Resend unreadable, Axiom 30d retention
description:
Three blind spots hit while investigating churn on 2026-07-30. Each needs a credential or config change before the corresponding question can be answered.

1. SENTRY — RESOLVED 2026-07-30. A User Auth Token with event:read + project:read + org:read is in .env.local as SENTRY_READ_TOKEN; helper at scripts/sentry-query.mjs. This immediately surfaced wordle-teams-jvt (P0). Note the issues endpoint only accepts statsPeriod of ''/24h/14d; longer windows need explicit start/end, which the script handles.

2. SENTRY TUNNEL DROPPING ~11% OF EVENTS. 30d: 3180x 200, 306x 400, 87x 429 on /monitoring. The 429s are quota/rate-limit rejections. Whatever Sentry holds is incomplete — and users running blockers (the exact population affected by wordle-teams-jvt) are the least likely to be reporting at all.

3. RESEND — STILL BLOCKED. RESEND_API_KEY in prod env is a restricted send-only key: 401 'This API key is restricted to only send emails' on /domains and /emails. Cannot check magic-link and invite deliverability, bounce rate, or SPF/DKIM domain verification. The product depends on emailed magic links, so silent spam-foldering remains a live hypothesis. Resend is not referenced anywhere in src/ — auth email delivery is configured on the hosted Supabase side, so verify prod Supabase SMTP settings too.

4. AXIOM RETENTION IS 30 DAYS. Dataset 'vercel' holds 2026-06-30 onward only (min(_time) verified, 139392 rows). The historical churn cohorts are unreachable from logs: team 55 (5 players, 39-92 entries each) churned 2025-05-02, and two solo heavy users (93 and 78 entries) went quiet in 2024-10 and 2025-07. Extend retention before the next cohort churns or the same question will be unanswerable again.
acceptance_criteria: Create a Sentry read token and store it as SENTRY_READ_TOKEN; triage the top client-side issues by event count for the last 90d. Get a full-access Resend key (or read the dashboard) and report bounce/spam rate on auth emails plus domain verification status. Confirm prod Supabase SMTP provider. Decide whether to extend Axiom retention.
notes: Player identities deliberately referenced by team id and entry count rather than email — this repo is PUBLIC (github.com/cdub615/wordle-teams). See wordle-teams-pii for the pre-existing exposure.
close_reason: Closed

title: Board entry silently hangs if the server action rejects — no try/catch in handleSubmit
description:
src/components/action-buttons/board-entry/form.tsx:66-109. handleSubmit awaits upsertBoard(formData) with no try/catch. upsertBoard itself is well guarded (src/app/me/actions.ts:191-260 catches everything and returns {success:false}), so the server path is safe — but a rejection that happens BEFORE or AROUND the action body is not:

 - Next.js rejecting the action entirely ('Failed to find Server Action', e.g. a stale tab open across a deploy — very plausible for a daily-habit app where people leave the tab open)
 - network drop mid-submit, especially on mobile
 - platform-level 500

On rejection: setSubmitting(false) at line 106 never runs, no toast fires, and document.getElementById('close-board-entry')?.click() at line 108 never runs. The form stays stuck in the animate-pulse state with a spinning button, and the entered board is lost with no error shown.

LATENT, not yet observed for a real user. The 10 'Failed to find Server Action' errors in the 30d window were all scanner probes sending Next-Action: "x" from AWS IPs (<scanner-ip>, <scanner-ip>) hitting POST /, not genuine users. Filing because the failure mode is silent and the cost is a lost board entry on an app with ~6 daily users.
acceptance_criteria: Wrap the await in try/catch: surface toast.error with a retry hint, always setSubmitting(false) in a finally block, and preserve the user's entered guesses so they can resubmit without re-typing.
notes: Same file, line 94-100: the update_monthly_winners RPC failure is only log.error'd and never surfaced. It fired once in prod on 2026-07-05 ('Failed to update winners table'). Low severity but the user sees a success toast while the winners table is stale.
close_reason: Shipped 2026-07-31 (main b796d7d, via dev 3071b29). 5zs: handleSubmit now wrapped in try/catch with setSubmitting(false) in finally, a toast telling the user their entry is preserved, and the sheet closing only on success (it previously closed on the handled failure path too, discarding what they had typed). io0: update_monthly_winners failure now surfaces a warning toast instead of a bare success while standings go stale; getUser/getSession stop calling refreshSession() when the error is literally 'Refresh Token Not Found', which cannot succeed, and log at info instead. Investigation found the forced-logout half was not a user-facing fault: zero events in 12h, and the historical ones collapse to two real session expiries amplified into 4-6 log lines by parallel checks each retrying. Typecheck and build clean; not exercised end-to-end because board entry requires an authenticated session.

title: Auth callback ignores provider ?error= params, shows generic /login-error
description:
src/app/api/auth/callback/route.ts:15-22 reads only 'code' and 'token_hash'. When an OAuth provider returns an error instead, neither is present, so it falls through to handleEmailSignin(null, null), logs 'Token Hash or Type were missing in the auth callback', and redirects to /login-error with no explanation.

Observed in prod 2026-07-22T19:31:43Z:
 /api/auth/callback?error=access_denied&error_description=AADSTS65004%3A+User+declined+to+consent+to+access+the+app.

That user declined Microsoft consent and got a dead-end error page instead of 'you cancelled — try another sign-in method'. On a funnel where only ~12 people completed auth in 30 days (see wordle-teams-390), losing one to an unexplained error page is material.

Also seen: a paramless GET /api/auth/callback at 2026-07-17T14:51:16.93Z, followed 1.4s later by a valid one carrying a code — likely a prefetch or double-fire. The paramless hit also lands on /login-error.

Related friction on the Microsoft button specifically: src/app/login/oauth/oauth-provider.tsx:36 requests scopes 'email offline_access'. offline_access asks for persistent access and is a common consent-decline trigger; it is not needed unless the app refreshes Microsoft tokens server-side.
acceptance_criteria: Parse 'error' and 'error_description' in parseRequest and branch on them: show a specific, human-readable message (declined consent vs. expired link vs. unknown) rather than routing everything to /login-error. Ignore paramless callback hits without logging them as errors. Separately, confirm whether offline_access is actually required for azure and drop it if not.

title: Invite email matching is case-sensitive — join silently fails on casing mismatch
description: handle_invited_signup uses 'WHERE invited_email = ANY(invited)' (case-sensitive) and invitePlayer stores the email exactly as the inviter typed it. If the inviter types different casing than the invitee's auth email (e.g. 'invitee-7@redacted.invalid' vs 'invitee-7@redacted.invalid'), the join never matches and the invite silently fails — a second, independent cause of the invite-not-working symptom. Seen in prod (team 181 stored 'invitee-7@...'). Fix: normalize emails to lowercase when writing teams.invited (invitePlayer) and/or make handle_invited_signup match case-insensitively (lower(invited_email) = ANY(select lower(unnest(invited)))). Add regression test.
acceptance_criteria: Invites with mixed-casing emails still join the invitee to the team.
notes: Fix in PR #153 -> dev. Code: invitePlayer lowercases/trims email + invited list on write. Data: existing teams.invited normalized to deduped-lowercase on prod (8 teams) + dev (0) — LIVE now. Migration 20260730190000 adds case-insensitive handle_invited_signup (defense-in-depth) + idempotent data normalization; untested DDL, apply dev->prod via normal migration process after review. Verified on dev: mixed-case fails to join, lowercasing joins. Code+data fix alone resolves acceptance; RPC hardening optional.
close_reason: Released to prod (PR #154). Code lowercases emails on write; existing prod/dev data normalized; migration 20260730190000 (case-insensitive RPC + normalization) ran on dev via GHA and applies to prod on this merge. Verified on dev.

title: Optional: minimal Playwright e2e smoke for invite->join
description: dev has no test tooling; add a Playwright smoke driving invite->token_hash callback->team membership assertion, matching feat/v2-replatform direction. Not a blocker for hotfix. [Epic: wordle-teams-c0v | Plan: docs/plans/2026-07-28-fix-team-invite-join-flow.md]
close_reason: Closed

title: B1 (follow-up): Branded invite via generateLink + Novu/react-email
description: Replace inviteUserByEmail with admin.generateLink({type:'invite'}); send branded email via existing react-email+Novu infra linking to /api/auth/callback?token_hash=<hashed_token>&type=invite&next=/me. Removes dashboard-template dependency. Done when invites send branded, version-controlled emails and join works. [Epic: wordle-teams-c0v | Plan: docs/plans/2026-07-28-fix-team-invite-join-flow.md]

title: testOtps pre-prod hardening: delete-on-read + cleanup
description: Deferred from Task 7 review (pattern-guard hardening already applied): consider converting the OTP read path to delete-on-read (requires mutation reshape of the E2E poll) and/or a periodic purge of testOtps rows on the dev deployment. Also confirm E2E_TEST_MODE is absent from the prod deployment before beta deploy (Task 9) — the pattern guard limits blast radius to e2e+* accounts, but the var still should not exist there.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-03, all three parts.

DELETE-ON-READ: latestFor (a query, so it could not write) is now takeFor, a mutation that deletes the row as it returns it. The e2e poll calls it the same way, with an ??= so a second poll iteration does not ask again and get null.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: the local deployment had accumulated 13 captured codes under the old query — every e2e run since Task 7 had left one behind. After purging that backlog, a full e2e run now leaves ZERO rows.

PURGE: added purgeAll, an internalMutation, for rows abandoned by runs that crash between store and read. Internal-only so no client can reach it; run from the CLI or schedule it.

E2E_TEST_MODE CONFIRMED ABSENT FROM PROD: 'convex env get E2E_TEST_MODE' on fabulous-goldfish-949 returns 'not found', and the deployment holds only BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY and SITE_URL. Verified against the deployed worker too — POSTing testOtps:takeFor to the production Convex returns a server error rather than a code, so the path is inert there regardless of what calls it.

No effect on real login: auth.ts only calls store when E2E_TEST_MODE is 'true' AND the address matches e2e+*, so production OTP email through Resend is untouched.
close_reason: testOtps now deletes on read with an internal purge for abandoned rows, proven to leave zero rows after a full e2e run, and E2E_TEST_MODE confirmed absent from the production deployment. generate-routes removed — nothing referenced it and it corrupted the route tree the build depends on.

title: Fix pre-hydration dead login form (SSR form interactive-looking before React hydrates)
description: Found during Phase 0 Task 7: v2/src/routes/login.tsx renders a fully interactive-looking form during SSR, but pre-hydration there's no onSubmit handler and no action — a click triggers a native GET submit (navigation, nothing sent) and the controlled input wipes typed text when hydration lands. Real users on slow connections hit a dead form; the E2E suite works around it with a retry-until-hydrated pattern (see e2e/login.spec.ts comment). Fix when the real login UI is built: disable submit until hydrated, uncontrolled input + defaultValue, or progressive-enhancement action. Applies to any SSR form pattern ported in later phases.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-13, and verified on the deployed site rather than only locally.

FIX: inputs are uncontrolled so pre-hydration typing survives (React does not own the value), and submit is disabled until hydrated. Disabling the button also blocks Enter-to-submit, because the HTML spec skips implicit submission when the form's default button is disabled — so both routes to a dead native GET are closed by one change.

Extracted as src/lib/use-hydrated.ts because the issue is right that every SSR form ported in later phases needs the same guard.

THE E2E WORKAROUND IS GONE and its absence is the regression test: the OTP spec now simply waits for the button to be enabled. It also got much faster — 11.0s to 3.3s — because it no longer retries its way through hydration. A second spec asserts the guarantee directly with javaScriptEnabled: false.

VERIFIED ON BETA, not just in dev: driving beta.wordleteams.com with JavaScript disabled renders the heading and a DISABLED Send code button; with JavaScript on the same button is enabled after hydration.

WORTH KNOWING FOR FUTURE CHECKS: curl | grep on /login finds no form markup, which looks alarming and is misleading — the content arrives inside the streamed SSR payload rather than as plain HTML in the initial chunk. A browser sees it. Use a real browser to judge what a route renders; grepping the raw response will produce false conclusions.
close_reason: OTP hardened (hashed storage, shared expiry constant, subpath import, real text+html email, better-auth pinned exactly) and the login form is safe before hydration — uncontrolled inputs plus a submit disabled until hydrated, verified on beta with JavaScript off. The e2e retry workaround is deleted and replaced by a direct assertion.

title: Enforce Cache-Control no-store on SSR document responses
description: Task 6 review: dehydrated SSR stream embeds the auth JWT (official pattern, safe only while HTML is uncacheable — Cloudflare's default). Enforce the invariant explicitly: set Cache-Control: private, no-store on SSR document responses when touching server entry/headers (natural home: Task 8 Sentry server.ts work or Task 9 wrangler config). Prevents a future Cache Rule from turning cached HTML into shared bearer tokens.
close_reason: Sentry + no-store SSR headers approved (2615378); verified in wrangler dev and vite dev

title: Auth hardening follow-ups from Task 5 review
description: Deferred minors from the Phase 0 Better Auth backend code review (v2/convex/auth.ts): (1) set storeOTP: 'hashed' on the emailOTP plugin — OTPs currently stored plaintext in the component's verification table (default), hashing is free UX-wise and doesn't affect the E2E testOtps capture which hooks sendVerificationOTP pre-storage; (2) couple the email copy's 'expires in 5 minutes' to a shared OTP_EXPIRY_SEC constant passed to expiresIn; (3) import emailOTP from better-auth/plugins/email-otp subpath for tree-shaking; (4) real email template with plain-text part and 'if you didn't request this, ignore' line. Also: before starting Phase 1, check the @convex-dev/better-auth migration guide for passkey-table support at the then-current 0.12.x+ (pre-1.0 breaking-changes cadence).
notes:
DONE 2026-08-13. All four items plus the exact pin.

  storeOTP: 'hashed' — the plugin's default is 'plain'. Verified the type accepts it and that the full OTP sign-in still works end to end (e2e green). NOT independently confirmed that the stored value is a hash: that would mean reading the better-auth component's own verification table, which is internal to the component. The config is set and the flow works; the storage format is taken on the plugin's word.
  OTP_EXPIRY_SEC (300) in convex/authEmails.ts now drives BOTH expiresIn and the sentence in the email. They were independent before, so the copy could have promised five minutes while the plugin enforced something else and nothing would have caught it.
  emailOTP imported from better-auth/plugins/email-otp rather than the barrel.
  Real email with a plain-text part and an 'if you didn't request this' line. The text part is not politeness — some clients prefer it and a mail with no text alternative scores worse with spam filters, which for an AUTH email means people cannot log in at all. Rendered and checked: subject, text and html all derive the same '5 minutes' from the one constant.
  better-auth pinned EXACTLY (was ~1.6.23). The AuthClient cast in __root.tsx assumes structural compatibility with component types built for 1.6.15 and the e2e suite is the only guard; a tilde range could have moved that out from under us on any install.

Hand-written HTML rather than react-email on purpose: no branding assets exist yet and the design puts that work in Phases 4 and 6. It should move over when invites and reminders land.
close_reason: OTP hardened (hashed storage, shared expiry constant, subpath import, real text+html email, better-auth pinned exactly) and the login form is safe before hydration — uncontrolled inputs plus a submit disabled until hydrated, verified on beta with JavaScript off. The e2e retry workaround is deleted and replaced by a direct assertion.

title: Replace scaffold PWA manifest with Wordle Teams identity before beta goes live
description: Code review of the v2 scaffold found v2/public/manifest.json still carries 'Create TanStack App Sample' branding and TanStack logos. v1 is an installed PWA, so the beta must not be installable with TanStack identity. Port the real manifest (name, icons, theme colors) as part of Phase 6 PWA work (spec: manifest ports as-is from the old app).

title: Pin date/answer header above scrolling guess rows in mobile board entry
description: Mobile board-entry sheet auto-scrolls to follow the active guess row, which pushed the Wordle answer out of view. Moved the date picker and answer field out of the scroll container in src/components/action-buttons/board-entry/form.tsx into a pinned shrink-0 header row so the answer stays visible while entering guesses. Commit d4d224a on feat/mobile-ux-fixes.
close_reason: Implemented in commit d4d224a on feat/mobile-ux-fixes; typecheck passes

title: The dashboard SSR loader awaits three independent Convex queries in sequence
description:
src/routes/index.tsx's loader awaits api.teams.getMyTeams, then api.teams.amIPro, then api.scores.getMyPlayerId, one after the other. They are independent of each other, so the SSR of '/' pays the sum of three round-trips where it could pay the max of them via Promise.all.

FOUND WHILE MEASURING wordle-teams-1cd. Not the cause of that flake and not fixed there, deliberately: the flake was fixed in the e2e helper and touching product code for a test's benefit was out of scope. But this is the reason a cold full-document load of the dashboard is the slowest navigation in the app, and it is on the path every OTP sign-in and every OAuth callback takes.

MEASURED CONTEXT (local backend, 6 concurrent sign-ins driven straight through /api/auth with no browser): the SSR leg that only runs beforeLoad's needsProfile and then 307s to /complete-profile took 320-590ms. The dashboard leg adds these three on top of that.

DONE WHEN: the three ensureQueryData calls are issued together (Promise.all or equivalent) and the dashboard still renders identically, with the measured before/after SSR time recorded here.

title: e2e: the pending-invite badge above zero is uncovered
description:
Task 11 (wordle-teams-ksh) shipped the non-pro 'N Invites Pending' badge in v2/src/components/Header.tsx. e2e/billing.spec.ts asserts the ZERO case (the badge is absent, so it can never render '0 Invites Pending') but not the above-zero case.

Reaching count > 0 needs a SECOND account that owns a team: the count only rises when someone else's invite is parked - a non-pro invitee already on FREE_TEAM_LIMIT teams (teams.ts invitePlayerFor) or an address invited to more teams than completeProfileFor claims at signup. That is two OTP sign-ins and two browser contexts.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE: measured during Task 11. At 15 e2e tests the suite passed 3 runs of 3. Adding 4 tests / 3 sign-ins took it to 0 clean runs of 5, always the same shape - the first 5s-default assertion after an OTP sign-in timing out on 'waiting for navigation to finish', spread across invites.spec.ts:119, invites.spec.ts:254, teams.spec.ts:85 and teams.spec.ts:145, never in billing.spec.ts. Folded back to 17 tests / 1 sign-in it passed 4 of 5, the exception being the known flake wordle-teams-1cd. Parallel OTP sign-ins are the scarce resource, not tests.

So this is blocked on the suite having headroom - either a seed mutation on convex/e2eSeed.ts that parks an invite directly (one sign-in instead of two), or pinning workers in playwright.config.ts, or fixing wordle-teams-1cd. A seed mutation is the cheapest and needs a Convex push, which Task 11 was not permitted to make.

The arithmetic itself IS covered: pendingInviteCountFor in convex/billing.test.ts, and the pluralisation in src/lib/billing-copy.test.ts.

DONE WHEN: an e2e test observes '1 Invite Pending' in the header for a non-pro player with a parked invite, and the suite still passes at the rate it does today.

title: copy-from-supabase.mjs and verify-parity.mjs silently ignore unknown flags
description:
Found 2026-08-26 during Phase 5 Task 0 review, and the review's premise was BACKWARDS - worth recording so it is not 'fixed' the wrong way round.

A code reviewer asserted that both scripts exit 1 on an unrecognised flag and that backfill-team-owner.mjs should conform. MEASURED: they do not. copy-from-supabase.mjs:56 and verify-parity.mjs:37 validate only the VALUE of --scope=; neither has a general unknown-argument check.

So 'node scripts/copy-from-supabase.mjs --dryrun' (typo for --dry-run) SILENTLY WRITES to the deployment, because has('--dry-run') is false. That is the dangerous direction: the typo turns a dry run into a real one against production data.

backfill-team-owner.mjs now rejects unknown args and is the FIRST script in the repo to do so - deliberate asymmetry, documented in its header, not precedent.

DONE WHEN: both scripts reject unrecognised arguments with exit 1, or a decision is recorded that they should not.

NOT PHASE 5's PROBLEM. Filed so the asymmetry is a choice rather than an accident.

title: Three more sites carry the stale 533 or the false 'no membership row' claim
description:
Found by the wt-ksh.13.11 review, 2026-08-24. All three verified by direct read, not inferred. Parent: wt-ksh (set separately).

wt-ksh.13.11 corrected the Phase 4 DESIGN doc and V2-ADDENDUM row 7. It did not cover these, and two of them were cleared on a partial grep during that task.

1. v2/convex/players.ts:25 - UNDATED 533 IN SHIPPED SOURCE:
     'afterwards - leaving 151 of production's 533 players permanently nameless.'
   The only undated 533 in shipped source. Its sibling v2/convex/schema.ts:55-56 carries '(measured 2026-08-20)' on the next line, and v2/scripts/lib/copy-filters.mjs:39 dates its own. This one rots silently. NOTE: source comment, so the four gates apply (pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test:once && pnpm build from v2/).

2. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md:528 - UNDATED 533:
     '// the name in later at /complete-profile - so 151 of production's 533'
   The same file's line 243 IS dated, which is why a grep that stopped at the first hit cleared the file. Line 528 is a code block reproducing what schema.ts should say, and the SHIPPED schema.ts did get the date - so this is the plan's copy drifting from what actually shipped. Plans are historical artifacts in this repo; decide whether to correct it or annotate it as superseded rather than retro-editing silently.

3. wt-ksh.5's EPIC BODY (Phase 4) still carries the false claim verbatim, at line 49 of its description:
     'teams.creator. They can be left out of the copy without orphaning anything real.'
   preceded by 'Nameless players are referenced by nothing except teams.player_ids and...'.
   This is the LAST surviving instance of the claim wt-ksh.13.8 disproved - grep -rn 'orphaning anything' now returns only this and the design doc line that 13.11 fixed.

   THERE IS PRECEDENT REQUIRING THIS ONE. wt-ksh.5's own notes record that when divergence 8's false claim was found, it was fixed in V2-ADDENDUM 7a row 8, in the Phase 4 design spec, AND in 'this epic's decision 4'. The same three-place discipline applies here and only two of the three were done.

THE FACT TO STATE, from the production query recorded on wt-ksh.13.8 (2026-08-24): players_total 535, players_nameless 151, memberships_total 535, memberships_of_nameless 151, memberships_orphaned 0. Every nameless player DOES carry a player_customer row.

DO NOT WRITE THAT THE 1:1 HOLDS 'BY CONSTRUCTION'. The wt-ksh.13.11 review checked the schema: supabase/migrations/20240319201543_move_columns_to_playercustomer.sql:8-19 declares only an FK on player_customer.player_id and a unique index on id - there is NO uniqueness on player_id. The 1:1 is a behavioural artifact of handle_new_user inserting one row per signup, i.e. a measured property that can drift. v2/scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs's header is the canonical statement of what a future divergence would mean; point at it rather than restating it.

title: Epic wt-ksh's design names the copy script as .ts; it is copy-from-supabase.mjs
description:
The epic description's Data Model & Migration section says **Copy script** (`v2/scripts/copy-from-supabase.ts`). The file is v2/scripts/copy-from-supabase.mjs — verified by ls v2/scripts/, and the sibling helpers are .mjs too (lib/copy-tallies.mjs, lib/copy-filters.mjs).

Cosmetic, but the paragraph immediately below it (added by wt-ksh.13.6) is what a cutover reader is sent to, and a wrong filename one line above the discard decision is the kind of thing that makes a reader distrust the rest. Left unfixed by 13.6 on purpose: that task's diff was required to be an insertion only, so the surrounding text was not touched.

DONE WHEN: the epic description names the .mjs file. Same body-file round-trip discipline as 13.6 (jq out, edit, diff, bd update --body-file, export, diff again).

title: The clobber banner's headline and footer are neither wrapped nor length-asserted
description:
Found by the code-quality review of wt-ksh.13.5 (Task 2), 2026-08-24. LATENT: not reachable today.

formatClobberReport wraps its DETAIL lines to the 80-column frame and pins that with a boundary test and a mutation test. The HEADLINE (copy-tallies.mjs, 'OVERWROTE STORED VALUES: <labels>') and the FOOTER notes ('Overwrote nothing: ...' / 'Not diffed: ...') are built from the same variable-length label lists and are simply emitted, unwrapped and unasserted.

MEASURED by the reviewer, sweeping every assignment of the six tables across {absent, clean, overwritten}:
  - today, with three tables reporting clobbered:        longest framed non-detail line = 80. Safe.
  - with playerMembership also reporting (Phase 5 Polar): 80. Still safe.
  - with dailyScores ALSO reporting:                      90 - the headline escapes its own frame.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FILING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT. The trigger is not hypothetical the way 'all six diff' is. convex/migrate.ts classifies upsertDailyScores as MERELY UNWIRED - it already has the same clobber shape and is left out only pending a dual-running decision. That is wordle-teams-r9d. dailyScores is the most likely next table to start reporting, and it is exactly the one that trips this.

The failure is the same defect class Task 2 already fixed for the detail lines: a continuation line loses the '##' gutter and reads as unrelated output escaping the block, which undercuts the acceptance criterion ('visually distinct from the routine output around it').

DONE WHEN: a report whose headline and footer carry the widest label list they can produce stays inside the 80-column frame, and a test pins it.

APPROACH NOTES from the review and the implementer:
  - The fix likely belongs in the same place as detailLines' wrapping (headline could wrap through it with an empty label column).
  - ALTERNATIVE, possibly better: drop the label list from the headline entirely. The detail lines below already name every table, so the headline list is redundant.
  - The existing 'stays inside its 80-column frame' describe block in scripts/lib/copy-tallies.test.mjs is where the guard slots in. It currently only exercises detail lines: its fixture has two overwritten tables and no clean/notDiffed entries, so it never renders a wide headline or any footer at all. Widening that fixture to five overwritten tables plus a clean and a not-diffed one makes it fail, which is the point.

BLOCKS NOTHING TODAY. Whoever wires dailyScores (wordle-teams-r9d) should do this in the same change.

title: The 533-player figure in the Phase 4 design and V2-ADDENDUM is now 535
description:
Measured against production 2026-08-24 while answering wt-ksh.13.8: players_total is 535, not the 533 stated in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites-design.md and in V2-ADDENDUM.md 7a row 7. Two signups since the 2026-08-20 measurement.

NO CONCLUSION MOVES. The 151 nameless figure both documents rest on is unchanged, verified in the same query, so the copy filter's premise and divergence 7's reasoning stand exactly as written.

Filed because this project treats a stated measurement as a claim, and the Phase 7 parity audit will compare against these totals. A reader who finds 535 where the document says 533 should be able to see that it was noticed and dated rather than wonder which number is stale.

FIX: state the figure with its measurement date, or express it as '151 of the then-533' so it cannot rot again. Also worth recording that player_customer is exactly 1:1 with players (535/535, 0 orphans), which is load-bearing for wt-ksh.13.7's membership narrowing and is not written down anywhere today.
notes:
SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-24 by the wt-ksh.13.7 review. The same Phase 4 design doc carries a SECOND now-false measurement, in the same table.

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites-design.md (around line 47) states that nameless players are referenced by 'no board, no winner row, no membership row'. wt-ksh.13.8 disproved the last clause against production on 2026-08-24: all 151 nameless players carry a player_customer row, memberships_total == players_total == 535, and memberships_orphaned = 0. player_customer is exactly 1:1 with players.

This matters more than the 533/535 drift does, because that line is the cited justification for leaving memberships to the upsert's own orphan tally - and it is the claim wt-ksh.13.7 had to work around by narrowing memberships verifier-side. A reader trusting it would conclude the membership narrowing in scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs is unnecessary.

Fix both in the same pass: 533 -> 535, and correct the membership clause.
close_reason:
Shipped in 804ccbe..92c497e (two commits). Documentation only.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY STALE, which is not what the bead said. The bead claimed the 533 figure appeared in BOTH the Phase 4 design doc AND V2-ADDENDUM 7a row 7. Verified by grep against both files and their pre-images: V2-ADDENDUM contains no 533 and no 535 at all, and row 7 made no membership claim. The bead's file attribution was simply wrong. No 533 edit was invented there.

FIXED IN docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites-design.md:
  - Line 30, dated PER-ROW rather than at the table header: '151 of 533' now carries 'Re-measured 2026-08-24 (wt-ksh.13.8): still 151, now of 535 - two signups since.' Per-row because the header's 'Run against production on 2026-08-20' stays true for the four rows that were only ever measured then; rewriting it to name two dates would have implied all five were re-run.
  - Lines 44-47, the false clause. 'no board, no winner row, no membership row points at one' - the last third is false. All 151 nameless players carry a player_customer row.
  - A THIRD instance the bead did not name, found by grep: the design's own divergence-7 row restated 'nothing but player_ids/creator refers to them' 275 lines later.

FIXED IN docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md 7a row 7: not false, but SILENT on memberships - and 7a is the parity audit's reference list, read by the same person who will watch verify-parity.mjs narrow memberships by 151. One clause, in-cell so a reader who only opens the table still gets it. Table still has its 11 rows and the 'Eleven known differences' header is untouched.

THE DEFECT REVIEW CAUGHT, and it is the one worth remembering. The first draft wrote that player_customer is '1:1 with players ... BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by coincidence' - and then pointed the reader at scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs, which says the opposite, deliberately, because wt-ksh.13.7 had just fixed exactly that misdirection. There is no construction: 20240319201543_move_columns_to_playercustomer.sql declares an FK on player_id and a unique index on id, and NO uniqueness on player_id. Review swept all 20 migrations touching player_customer and confirmed no later one adds it. The 1:1 is a behavioural artifact of handle_new_user inserting one row per signup - verified as the current definition, 20240321210006 being the latest of five. So the property is measured and can drift, exactly as the 533 did. Now stated as a measurement with the migration cited, in both documents - the same rule-framing had appeared in V2-ADDENDUM row 7 too.

NO CONCLUSION MOVED, as the bead required: the copy filter's premise, the 'Not copied' decision row and divergence 7's reasoning are byte-identical.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: wordle-teams-9vq (P3) - three sites still carrying a stale or false form of these claims. Two undated 533s (v2/convex/players.ts:25, the only one in shipped source, and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md:528), plus wt-ksh.5's EPIC BODY, which still carries the false 'orphaning anything real' claim verbatim - and wt-ksh.5's own notes record the three-place precedent that requires fixing it there too.

title: Add a no-restricted-imports rule so Resend cannot be imported outside email.ts
description:
The last third of wordle-teams-sga. The choke point is in place - convex/email.ts exports only a guarded sendEmail and keeps the Resend client module-private - but nothing MECHANICALLY stops a new module doing 'import { Resend } from @convex-dev/resend' and constructing its own.

That is a convention held by a comment, and this exact guard has now had to be added after the fact twice (see wordle-teams-96l).

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINER: v2 has no ESLint config of its own. The only config in the repo is v1's root .eslintrc.json (next/core-web-vitals), which does not cover v2/. So this needs a v2 config before it needs a rule.

Shape once there is one:

  'no-restricted-imports': ['error', { paths: [{
    name: '@convex-dev/resend',
    message: 'Send mail through convex/email.ts sendEmail, which applies the e2e guard.',
  }]}]

with an override allowing it in convex/email.ts and convex/convex.config.ts only.
close_reason:
Fixed. v2 now has ESLint (flat config), a lint script with --max-warnings 0, and a CI step ahead of the unit tests in deploy-v2.yml. The substantive rule: nothing but convex/email.ts may reach the Resend client.

THREE IMPORT VECTORS BLOCKED, each verified by probe with the tree restored after: a static import from convex/ or src/; a DYNAMIC import(), which core no-restricted-imports cannot see at all because it only inspects ImportDeclaration - that needed no-restricted-syntax on ImportExpression; and .tsx under convex/, which the original file glob missed and which is exactly where Phase 6's React Email templates would land.

NOT CLOSED, and stated in the config rather than implied otherwise: createRequire, and reaching the component through the generated components.resend handle (convex/_generated/api.d.ts exposes it as a typed ComponentApi, so a convex module can call ctx.runMutation(components.resend...) without importing anything restricted). 'Structural' here means the obvious path is blocked, not that every path is.

Kept deliberately narrow - the recommended sets and nothing more, so it passes clean rather than importing a style backlog. no-console left off and filed as wordle-teams-61x. rules-of-hooks turned ON (a conditional hook call is a crash, not a preference; the tree already satisfied it). --max-warnings 0 because without it the severities pointed the wrong way: an unused disable directive is an error and would fail the deploy, while a genuine missing hook dependency was a warning and shipped green.

Three pre-existing findings fixed rather than silenced: migrate.ts's chunkNote is a live @see {@link} target (proved with tsc - noUnusedLocals does NOT fire while the tag exists, and DOES when it is removed), and two disable directives that suppressed nothing.

SEPARATE FINDING, fixed here: the pre-commit hook is not a beads stager, it is scripts/check-no-pii.mjs. Committing --no-verify - which every Phase 4 commit did - skipped the PII guard on a public repo for an entire phase. It failed on 40 addresses, all RFC 2606 reserved .test names, which is why it would keep being bypassed; ALLOWED_EMAILS now covers the .test TLD alongside example.com/org/net. Clean over 471 tracked files, and a real address is still blocked.

Filed alongside: wordle-teams-61x (no-console decision), and the CI-never-typechecks gap.

title: accessError('UNAUTHENTICATED') is dead code - getAuthUser throws before it is reached
description:
Found by the Phase 4 Task 8 review, 2026-08-22.

v2/convex/players.ts:247 and :291 both do:

  const user = await authComponent.getAuthUser(ctx)
  if (!user?.email) throw accessError('UNAUTHENTICATED')

The guard is unreachable. getAuthUser throws new ConvexError('Unauthenticated') rather than returning null (@convex-dev/better-auth/dist/client/create-client.js:74). Because that payload is a bare string, convexErrorCode (src/lib/convex-error.ts:12-32) returns null and the UI renders its GENERIC fallback ('Could not save your profile, please try again') instead of the typed 'Your session expired'.

THIS IS THE ROOT OF A REAL DEBUGGING COST. Two separate attempts to diagnose a flaky e2e spec chased this: the failure presented as a mystery precisely because the typed path was dead. Had UNAUTHENTICATED been live, the spec's failure would have been self-describing.

FIX: use safeGetAuthUser (or catch and re-throw as accessError) so the typed code is live. Check every other authed wrapper for the same pattern - the ...For helpers are unaffected, this is wrapper-only, which is the exposure wordle-teams-obw already tracks.

Note this is the SAME class as the ConvexError-vs-Error rule the phase already follows: an error a human reads must carry a code the client can map.

title: Extract PendingInvites so the creator-only query boundary is structural, not a comment
description:
Raised by the Phase 4 Task 7 quality review.

current-team-card.tsx now holds 6 useState, 3 mutations and 1 query in ~330 lines. The Pending block is cleanly separable: it needs only teamId, owns openEmail / pendingEmail / the cancel mutation / the getTeamInvites query / the dedupe, and renders its own Separator + h3 + ul. Nothing else in the card reads any of it.

THE ARGUMENT IS NOT LINE COUNT. Conditional mounting makes the 'skip' subtlety structurally unnecessary:

  {isCreator && <PendingInvites teamId={teamId} />}

A non-creator never calls the hook, so no query-cache entry is created and subscribeInner never sees an 'added' event. That replaces ~13 lines of comment explaining a library internal with a guarantee the render tree enforces - and, crucially, one that survives a future contributor 'simplifying' convexQuery(..., 'skip') back to enabled: isCreator, which is exactly the regression Task 7 had to measure at the websocket to disprove.

A comment is the weakest possible protection for a security-adjacent boundary over real email addresses. See the memory note on enabled-vs-skip.

Not done in Task 7 because the plan specifies the inline shape and the shipped code is correct; changing it there would have been uninstructed refactoring.

title: ConfirmPopover loses focus to <body> when its trigger unmounts
description:
Measured during Phase 4 Task 7 review.
