After a successful destructive confirm, Radix restores focus to the trigger on close - but the handler sets the popover closed AFTER the await, by which point the Convex subscription has already re-pushed the list without that row, so the trigger is gone and there is nothing to restore to.

Measured: focus with popover open = BUTTON 'Cancel invite'; immediately after the toast = BODY; at 300ms, 1000ms and 2500ms = still BODY, never recovers. The next Tab lands on the site logo at the top of the document, then Home, About, theme switcher.

PRE-EXISTING SHAPE, NOT INTRODUCED BY TASK 7. The untouched remove-member path does the same thing (focus after remove = BODY). Radix Dialog's Escape restore is also BODY for both the new invite dialog and the pre-existing settings dialog.

WHY IT IS WORSE ON PENDING INVITES. Removing a member or deleting a team is a one-off. The pending list exists so a creator can clear out SEVERAL bad addresses in a row - and after each one a keyboard user must Tab past the header, theme switcher, team picker, month picker, board-entry button and the whole scores table to reach the next row.

FIX BELONGS IN src/components/confirm-popover.tsx, once, covering cancel-invite, remove-member and delete-team: give PopoverContent an onCloseAutoFocus that redirects when the trigger is detached, or have callers move focus deliberately after a successful destructive action (e.g. tabIndex={-1} on the list wrapper, focused on success).

title: Extract the needsProfile route guard once a third authed route needs it
description:
index.tsx and complete-profile.tsx now run near-identical mirror-image beforeLoad logic: check context.isAuthenticated, redirect to /login if not, read needsProfile via ensureQueryData, then redirect in opposite directions.

BOTH Task 6 reviewers independently recommended LEAVING the duplication for now. It is four lines, two call sites, and a shared helper would need a direction parameter and end up longer than what it replaces.

THE RISK IS OMISSION, NOT DUPLICATION. Nothing forces a new authed route to carry the guard. A route that skips it puts a playerless account in front of queries that assume a player exists - which is exactly wt-ksh.5.1's dead end, where the dashboard rendered NO_PLAYER as 'Your session expired' and signing in again could not fix it.

Phase 4/5's invite-acceptance route is the likely third. Extract then, and at that point make the guard the default rather than something each route opts into.

title: Extract the normalise-on-read invite comparison into lib/invite.ts
description:
The trim().toLowerCase() comparison over teams.invited is now restated FIVE times across two modules: teams.ts (invitePlayerFor's filter and its some() scan, and cancelInviteFor's filter) and players.ts (completeProfileFor's some() scan and its filter). Each site carries a long comment re-deriving the same reasoning.

lib/invite.ts's own header states the principle this violates: 'the rules live here, once, rather than being restated at each call site where they could drift apart.'

Suggested shape:

  export function isSameInvite(entry: string, normalisedEmail: string): boolean
  export function withoutInvite(invited: Array<string>, normalisedEmail: string): Array<string>

THE TRAP THE EXTRACTION MUST NOT FALL INTO. The obvious simplification of these five lines is normaliseInviteEmail(entry) === email. That is WRONG: normaliseInviteEmail returns null for an entry that fails EMAIL_SHAPE, so a malformed stored entry would never match and could never be cancelled - resurrecting exactly the uncancellable-invite bug this surface exists to remove. The helper must compare entry.trim().toLowerCase(), not re-run the write-side normaliser over stored data. Write a test that pins this: a stored entry failing EMAIL_SHAPE must still be cancellable by an address that normalises to the same string.

Deferred out of Phase 4 Task 4 deliberately: the extraction touches invitePlayerFor and completeProfileFor, both already shipped, tested and reviewed, while Task 4 was scoped to a new surface. Raised by the Task 4 code-quality review.

title: isNamed and isCompleteName disagree on whitespace-only names
description:
Found by the Phase 4 Task 0c/0d joint review, 2026-08-21.

scripts/lib/copy-filters.mjs's isNamed is a plain falsy test, so a name of ' '
(a single space) is treated as NAMED and copied across.

convex/lib/invite.ts's isCompleteName trims before testing, so the same value is
treated as INCOMPLETE and rejected by the profile flow.

So v2 will refuse a name that its own copy accepts. Nobody has written that
asymmetry down, and a mutant that makes isNamed trim survives the copy-filter
suite — the rule is unpinned in the direction that would fix it.

Not a regression: the retired deleteNamelessPlayers used the same falsy test, so
the two have always disagreed. Low priority because a whitespace-only name in
Supabase is unlikely and unmeasured.

Worth doing together with wordle-teams-9lt, since both are about the copy's
selection rules being exactly right before the Phase 7 audit. If the answer is
"make isNamed trim", add the pinning test at the same time.
acceptance_criteria: A whitespace-only name is treated the same by the copy filter and the profile flow, or the divergence is documented as deliberate.

title: A profile-incomplete member is invisible and unremovable
description:
Found by the whole-phase review of Phase 3, 2026-08-19. A known constraint for Phase 4 to design around, not a bug to fix now.

getMyTeamsFor filters profile-incomplete members out of the payload, so CurrentTeamCard renders no row for them and the creator never receives their id. removeMember would happily remove them — there is simply no path in the UI to call it with that id.

So an invitee who accepts but never completes their profile is INVISIBLE AND UNREMOVABLE. They sit in the team's playerIds forever, counting against nothing visible, with no way for the creator to clear them out.

Phase 4 owns invites and onboarding and is where this becomes reachable. Worth knowing going in rather than discovering it: the fix is probably a pending-members section on the team card rather than relaxing the filter, since relaxing it would put a nameless row on the scoreboard, which is the thing the filter exists to prevent.
acceptance_criteria: A creator can see and remove a member who accepted an invite but never completed their profile.
close_reason:
Closed by Phase 4, though not in the shape this issue anticipated. The premise - a member who accepted an invite but never completed their profile - is now UNREPRESENTABLE: decision 2 of the epic made firstName/lastName required and a players row is born only on profile completion, so such a person has no player row and never enters teams.playerIds. They remain an address in teams.invited.

So the remedy is the one this issue asks for, reached differently: Task 4 (wt-ksh.5.16) added getTeamInvites and cancelInvite, creator-only, with the refusal in the QUERY rather than a hidden button; Task 7 (wt-ksh.5.19) added the Pending invites section with a per-address cancel. The creator can now SEE them - v1 showed pending invites nowhere - and remove them. Case- and whitespace-insensitive, because copied rows predate v1's own case fix. Divergence 6.

Note the query is gated with convexQuery(..., 'skip'), not enabled:, because enabled does not gate a Convex query at all - see wt-ksh.5.19 and the bd memory note. These are real email addresses.

title: Month dropdown lists oldest first; most recent should be on top
description:
Reported by the owner: the month dropdown lists the oldest month at the top and the most recent at the bottom. It should be the other way round — most recent first.

CAUSE: monthOptions in v2/src/components/month-picker.tsx returns ascending:

  return [addMonths(currentMonth, -2), addMonths(currentMonth, -1), currentMonth]

and MonthPicker renders them in array order.

FIX is small: reverse the order so the current month is first. Two other things must move with it or the change is incomplete:

 1. v2/src/components/month-picker.test.ts pins the ascending order in both its tests (monthOptions('2026-08') -> ['2026-06','2026-07','2026-08'] and the year-boundary case). Update them to the new expectation rather than deleting them — the year-boundary case is the one worth keeping.
 2. This DIVERGES FROM v1. Prod builds the same list ascending (getMonthsFromScoreDate in src/lib/utils.ts appends forward from the earliest month) and renders in array order, so prod also shows oldest-first. Record the change in docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md section 7a so Phase 7's parity audit expects it.

RELATED: wordle-teams-rzu (MonthPicker does not validate its value against the offered months) is in the same component, and the deferred pro-gate expansion — which widens this list to every month back to the team's earliest score — will touch this ordering too. Worth doing together; a long ascending list makes the wrong-end problem considerably worse than a three-item one.
acceptance_criteria: The current month is the top entry and older months descend below it, with the tests and the divergence record updated.

title: Pin the invariant that N/A weekend days never affect the month total
description:
Confirmed correct, needs a test pinning it.

A weekend day on a team with playWeekends off renders N/A and contributes NOTHING to the month total — monthTotal skips it before consulting any score. That is the intended behaviour and matches v1.

The scoring for a 0 day is also correct and is NOT changing: a past day with no board scores the team's own "0 attempts" value from its scoring system (the nA field, default 0). The owner initially asked for a 0 day to score like an X, then withdrew it on realising the default system already scores a 0 day as 0 and the scoring system was being honoured correctly. No parity divergence results.

scoring.test.ts already covers "weekends are skipped entirely when the team does not play them". Add an explicit companion asserting a weekend contributes nothing even when the team's nA value is NON-ZERO — the existing test uses nA:-2 and would catch a regression, but nothing states the invariant in terms a reader would recognise as "N/A must never score".

Small, and it stops a future change to the missed-day rule from silently sweeping weekends in with it.
acceptance_criteria: A test fails if a weekend day on a playWeekends-off team ever contributes to the total.
close_reason: Closed

title: MonthPicker does not validate its value against the offered months
description:
MonthPicker takes `value` straight from the URL search param and does not check it against monthOptions(currentMonth), which is a fixed three-month window (current month and the two before it).

A bookmarked or hand-edited URL for a month outside that window renders the trigger label for that month while no radio item in the dropdown shows as selected. Not a data or access problem — getTeamMonth serves any month to a team member by design, and the window is a UI affordance rather than access control in both v1 and v2 — just an inconsistent control.

Cheapest to fold into whatever work expands the window for pro accounts, since that phase has to reason about exactly this logic anyway and will decide whether the window becomes server-enforced.

Raised in the Phase 2 whole-phase review.
acceptance_criteria: A month outside the offered window either redirects to a valid one or is shown as selected.

title: e2e login spec asserted removed Phase 1 debug-view testids
description:
Task 6 (2df6872, 'launch url, open to dashboard') rewrote v2/src/routes/index.tsx
into the real dashboard, dropping the Phase 1 debug view that rendered
data-testid="signed-in-email" / "copied-data" / "no-player". e2e/login.spec.ts
still asserted against those testids and was silently broken (pnpm e2e failed)
from that commit onward -- nothing in the normal quality gates (test:once,
tsc, build) runs Playwright, so it went unnoticed until Task 9 ran the e2e
suite directly.

Found and fixed while extracting the sign-in helper for Task 9
(wt-ksh.3.11): updated login.spec.ts's post-verify assertions to check the
CURRENT dashboard behavior (URL is '/' and the 'You are not on a team yet'
empty state renders) instead of the removed testids. Filing this so the
regression and root cause are on record, separate from the Task 9 work
itself.
close_reason: Fixed in the same commit that files this issue: e2e/login.spec.ts's assertions updated to match the current dashboard (part of Task 9 / wt-ksh.3.11).

title: form.tsx duplicates board-input.tsx's keystroke interception
description:
board-entry/form.tsx's handleAnswerKeyDown re-implements the same keystroke interception as board-entry/board-input.tsx's handleKeyDown: the letter regex, backspace handling, Tab passthrough, preventDefault-everything-else. No shared helper.

Two costs. It is a DRY violation on logic that must stay in lockstep — both fields are contentEditable and both depend on identical guarantees about which events can reach the DOM (see the beforeinput/paste hardening added in task 8). And it means BoardEntryForm is simultaneously a data-orchestration layer and a raw keystroke interceptor, so the capture logic cannot be reasoned about or tested apart from the form.

Suggested by code review: an AnswerInput component mirroring BoardInput's shape, or a shared module exporting the key classification and the apply helpers.

Raised during Phase 2 task 8 review, deliberately deferred to avoid widening that commit further.
acceptance_criteria: One shared implementation of contentEditable key capture, testable without mounting the form.

title: Extract the dashboard search-param sync into a hook
description:
src/routes/index.tsx now holds the route definition (loader, validateSearch, beforeLoad), three independent useEffects (login-funnel arrival tracking, URL/localStorage search-param sync with a redirect, team-selection persistence) and the dashboard layout.

Phase 3 adds team management to this same screen.

The search-param sync effect is the piece worth extracting: it is the highest-risk code in the Phase 2 UI (an effect that navigates to fill in URL state while racing hydration — the classic infinite-redirect shape), it is the piece Phase 3 is most likely to touch, and pulling it into a useDashboardSearchSync hook would also make it testable independently, which wordle-teams-pow wants.

DashboardError was already extracted during Phase 2 task 8 review. This covers the remainder.
acceptance_criteria: index.tsx holds the route and layout; the search-param sync lives in its own tested hook.
close_reason: Closed by wt-ksh.4.19. index.tsx holds the route and layout (143 -> 115 lines); the decision lives in the pure resolveDashboardSearch with 7 tests including an idempotency round-trip that encodes the termination property as an assertion rather than a comment.

title: The dashboard redirect effect has no targeted test
description:
The dashboard route resolves team and month from URL search params, filling in missing ones via a useEffect that navigates with replace:true and reads localStorage for the last team. That effect is the highest-risk code in the Phase 2 UI: it is the classic shape for infinite redirect loops (an effect depending on unstable-identity values that navigates to fill in URL state, racing hydration).

It currently has no test. The Phase 2 spec ruled out a component-test suite on the grounds that Phase 2 is a 1:1 port — but this code is NOT a port. v1 used a React context backed by localStorage; search params are a deliberate v2 divergence chosen because v1's approach needed three hydration guards and still shipped a production hydration crash (wordle-teams-uc5). So the no-component-tests rationale does not cover it.

Loop-safety was verified by hand during code review and holds today. Nothing would catch a regression — for instance someone adding a dependency to the effect, or reordering the early-return guard.

The Playwright smoke test does exercise the path incidentally (it must resolve params to reach the board), so this is not uncovered end to end; what is missing is a targeted test that fails fast and points at the cause.

v2 already has jsdom and @testing-library/react installed. vitest's global environment is edge-runtime, so a component test needs a per-file `// @vitest-environment jsdom` pragma.
acceptance_criteria: A test fails when the redirect effect loops, double-fires, or stops filling in missing params.

title: INVALID_BOARD does double duty for a rejected today
description:
upsertBoardFor throws INVALID_BOARD for two distinct failure classes:
  - the board itself is malformed (boardIsValid failed)
  - the board is fine but the client-supplied today is outside +/-1 day of the server date

Inert today because nothing on the client branches on AccessCode yet. It stops being inert as soon as an error-message mapping keys off INVALID_BOARD to say something like "your board is incomplete" — a clock-skew rejection would then show a misleading message to someone whose board was perfectly good.

Wants a distinct code (INVALID_TODAY or similar) before the client starts consuming these. Note the Phase 2 plan specified INVALID_BOARD here explicitly, so this is a plan choice to revisit rather than an implementation slip.

Related: wordle-teams-3ht (AccessCode carrying non-access concerns).
acceptance_criteria: A clock-skew rejection is distinguishable from a malformed board by its error code.

title: Extract recomputeWinners from scores.ts before Phase 3 needs it
description:
recomputeWinners is an unexported function inside convex/scores.ts, reachable only through upsertBoardFor. Its five distinct behaviours (a row per team, tie-break by team order, no-winner deletes, preserve hasSeenCelebration on unchanged, reset on changed) can only be exercised by first constructing a valid board submission and passing the whole validity/upsert machinery.

Compare lib/scoring.ts, whose monthTotal and winnerOf get direct dependency-free unit tests.

The forward-looking cost is the bigger one: Phase 3 changes team membership, and a member leaving mid-month plausibly needs the same recompute triggered from a DIFFERENT mutation. Today there is no way to call it without either exporting it or duplicating ~70 lines.

Suggested by code review: extract to convex/winners.ts, typed against the same narrow WriterCtx scores.ts already uses. Decouples winner tests from board-validity setup and gives Phase 3 an entry point.

Also noted: scores.ts is now 349 lines holding reads, the write, team listing, player-id lookup and winner recomputation. Not unreadable, but the split is cheapest before Phase 3 needs it.

Not blocking Phase 2.
acceptance_criteria: Winner recomputation is callable and unit-testable independently of a board submission.
close_reason: Closed by wt-ksh.4.18. recomputeWinners now lives in convex/winners.ts as recomputeTeamMonth / recomputeTeamMonths / monthsWithWinners / recomputePlayerMonth, unit-tested directly without constructing a board submission — which was this issue's acceptance criterion. Phase 3 tasks 6/7/8 call it from removeMember, updateTeam and setScoringSystem.

title: Today's answer is visible to teammates who have not played yet
description:
PRODUCT QUESTION, not a defect. Needs an owner decision.

getTeamMonth returns every team member's scores for the month, each row carrying its own answer. Wordle has one global puzzle per day, so once any teammate submits today's board, today's correct answer is present in the wire payload sent to every other member of that team — including those who have not played yet. Opening devtools reveals the day's answer.

The showLetters team setting does not prevent this. Per the comment in wordle-board.tsx, showLetters only hides LETTERS; the client still needs the raw answer to compute tile colours, so it must cross the wire regardless.

v1 has the same architecture (client-side tileStates(answer, guess)), so this is inherited rather than introduced by the re-platform, and strict parity argues for leaving it. Worth an explicit "yes, we know" rather than silent inheritance across a re-platform.

If it is ever deemed undesirable the fix is not small: tile states would have to be computed server-side for boards other than your own, so the answer never leaves the server until you have submitted.

Raised in Phase 2 task 3 review.
acceptance_criteria: Owner decision recorded: accepted as v1 parity, or a follow-up filed to compute tile states server-side.

title: getTeamMonth collapses a missing answer into an empty string
description:
getTeamMonthFor returns answer: score.answer ?? '', collapsing a genuinely-absent answer into an empty string. dailyScores.answer is v.optional(v.string()) for a real reason — legacy Supabase rows can lack one — and "no answer on record" is distinguishable from "the answer was empty".

For SCORING the coalesce is correct and deliberately harmonised with scoring.ts, which does attemptsFor(guesses, answer ?? '') itself.

For DISPLAY it loses something. WordleBoard feeds answer straight into tileStates(answer, guess) to colour tiles. A legacy row with no answer renders every tile as absent/grey — indistinguishable from a real answer sharing no letters with the guesses — rather than letting the UI say "no answer on record". Because the query collapses the type before it reaches a component, that distinction cannot be recovered downstream.

Not biting yet: no client consumes getTeamMonth as of task 3. Decide when the board history view is built — either keep answer optional through the query and let the presentational layer choose, or keep the coalesce only on the path feeding attemptsFor/monthTotal.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on whether the absent-answer state survives to the presentational layer.

title: ReaderCtx is duplicated with a comment-only guarantee
description:
convex/access.ts and convex/scores.ts each define an identical private type:

  type ReaderCtx = { db: GenericDatabaseReader<DataModel> }

scores.ts carries a comment saying it mirrors access.ts's exactly. Nothing enforces that. If access.ts later widens its version (say it needs ctx.storage), the comment in scores.ts silently becomes false with no compiler signal.

Two options: promote it to a shared export once a third consumer appears, or make the claim self-verifying now with a type-level equality assertion. Near-zero cost either way.

Raised in Phase 2 task 3 review, deliberately deferred rather than widening that commit.
acceptance_criteria: Either one shared definition, or a type-level assertion that fails when the two drift.

title: SITE_URL guard checks presence, not scheme
description:
convex/auth.ts guards startup with:

  const siteUrl = process.env.SITE_URL
  if (!siteUrl) throw new Error('SITE_URL is not set on this deployment')

That checks PRESENCE only. The bug it exists to prevent (amendment A2, commit fe81c46) was a redirect origin built from a scheme-LESS deployment hostname, which Supabase then silently replaced with its own Site URL. A bare hostname with no https:// satisfies this guard completely, so the guard is narrower than the comment framing around it suggests.

Also: there is no regression test asserting auth.ts throws when SITE_URL is unset. Phase 2 added env.SITE_URL to vitest.config.ts so tests could import auth.ts transitively; that dummy is never dereferenced, so it hides nothing that was previously covered, but it does mean the guard itself stays untested.

Consider validating the shape (parses as a URL with an http/https protocol) rather than mere presence, and adding a test.

Found during Phase 2 task 2 review. Not blocking.
acceptance_criteria: SITE_URL is validated as a URL with an http/https scheme, with a test covering the rejection.

title: AccessCode carries INVALID_BOARD, a non-access concern
description:
AccessCode in convex/access.ts is the union UNAUTHENTICATED | NO_PLAYER | NOT_A_MEMBER | INVALID_BOARD. The first three are access concerns. INVALID_BOARD is board-shape validation, which is not, and the file's own header describes itself as "the access checks that replace Supabase's RLS policies".

The consequence: scores.ts imports access.ts partly just to borrow an error-code union and factory unrelated to membership or authentication. Every future domain wanting a typed ConvexError faces the same choice — pile onto AccessCode, or fork the pattern.

Suggested by code review: a shared errors.ts owning a generic factory (appError<T extends string>(code: T): never), with access.ts importing only the codes it actually throws and each domain declaring its own literal union.

Cheap now, more annoying after a third domain reaches for AccessCode. Not blocking Phase 2 — flagged during task 2 review and deliberately deferred to avoid widening that commit.
acceptance_criteria: Typed ConvexError codes are organised so a new domain can declare its own without touching AccessCode.

title: me.ts duplicates access.ts playerForEmail instead of calling it
description:
convex/me.ts myData looks a player up inline: same by_email index, same .toLowerCase(), same .first()-not-.unique() choice, same justifying comment. convex/access.ts playerForEmail is now the canonical version of exactly that lookup.

Two hand-synced copies of the player-resolution rule. It is the join the whole migration rests on (copied players carry a Supabase uuid with nothing tying them to a Better Auth user id, so email IS the join), which makes drift between the copies expensive rather than cosmetic.

Point me.ts at playerForEmail. Small and safe; deliberately left out of Phase 2 task 2 to keep that commit to its stated file list.
acceptance_criteria: me.ts myData resolves its player through playerForEmail; one definition of the email join remains.

title: public/sw.js is a tracked build artifact that dirties the tree on every build
description:
next.config.js:46 has serwist write the service worker to swDest: 'public/sw.js', and both public/sw.js and public/sw.js.map are tracked by git. Every 'pnpm build' rewrites them (Sentry debug IDs and the workbox precache manifest change with the chunk hashes), so the working tree comes back dirty after any build.

git log shows they are only actually committed occasionally — 543d4f0, 24732bf, e2d9ee0 — while recent app changes that certainly altered the bundle (391a065, touching src/app/login/actions.ts) left them untouched. So the committed copy is already stale relative to main, and the churn is pure noise that has to be reverted by hand before every commit. It is also an easy way to accidentally commit an unrelated 2-line binary-ish diff.

Either gitignore them and let the build produce them (they are regenerated on every deploy anyway), or regenerate and commit them deliberately as a release step. The first is almost certainly right — nothing reads the committed copy.
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout plus 'pnpm build' leaves 'git status' clean.
notes:
FIXED on fix/untrack-sw-artifact. .gitignore entries for /public/sw.js and /public/sw.js.map, plus git rm --cached on both.

VERIFIED THE ARTIFACT IS ACTUALLY REGENERATED BEFORE UNTRACKING IT, because the failure mode of getting this wrong is a production PWA with no service worker:
  deleted both files, ran pnpm build -> serwist logs 'Bundling the service worker script with the URL /sw.js' and both files reappear (49302 and 192923 bytes)
  pnpm start -> GET /sw.js returns 200, application/javascript, size 49302; GET /sw.js.map returns 200
Same build pipeline Vercel runs, so nothing depends on the checked-in copy.

ACCEPTANCE MET: with the change applied, pnpm build leaves git status showing only the intentional edits — no sw.js churn at all.

The committed copy was stale regardless: git log shows public/sw.js last updated in 543d4f0 / 24732bf / e2d9ee0, while recent app changes that certainly altered the bundle (391a065, touching login/actions.ts) left it untouched. So the tracked file had not matched the built output for some time.

Cost before fixing: it dirtied the tree on every build, got swept into unrelated commits, and blocked the #157 rebase outright ('cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes').

title: Drop the two instant-based dailyScores indexes once a key can
description:
dailyScores still carries by_player_and_date and by_date, which index the raw instant. Nothing should use them — grouping by an instant across 57 player timezones is the bug puzzleDay exists to fix — and the schema says DO NOT USE in as many words.

They survive only because REMOVING a Convex index requires deployment:data:view, which neither the CI key (deployment:deploy only) nor the local-cli key carries. Adding indexes is permitted; dropping them is not. Isolated by experiment: the identical deploy succeeds with the two indexes present and fails with them absent, and Convex's own error names CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY as the cause.

TO FIX: add deployment:data:view to the github-actions deploy key (and local-cli if local deploys are wanted), then delete the two .index() lines and the DO NOT USE comment block from v2/convex/schema.ts.

Low priority — they cost a little storage and are correctly labelled — but worth doing before Phase 2 builds scoreboard queries, so nobody reaches for the wrong index.
acceptance_criteria: Both indexes gone from schema.ts and from the deployment, with CI green.
notes: Reparented from wt-ksh.2 to the top-level epic on 2026-08-18 when Phase 1 closed. This is not Phase 1 work and must not hold a phase open: it is blocked indefinitely on a Convex key carrying deployment:data:view, which neither the CI key nor the local key has. Adding an index is permitted; removing one is not. The two indexes are harmless while unused and carry a DO NOT USE comment in the schema explaining that grouping by the raw instant is the v1 timezone bug puzzleDay exists to fix.

title: Root package.json pins pnpm 11.13.0, which pnpm has marked a broken release
description:
Root package.json has packageManager: pnpm@11.13.0, added in 16af819 to make Vercel corepack deterministic. pnpm now refuses that version outright:

  [ERR_PNPM_BROKEN_PNPM_RELEASE] pnpm v11.13.0 is a broken release and cannot be installed
  Its "@pnpm/exe" build shipped without a binary and does not run.

Observed in GitHub Actions on 2026-08-03: pnpm/action-setup read the root manifest and its self-installer failed hard. Run 30853583666.

NOT CURRENTLY BREAKING v1. Vercel production builds are green — the most recent Production deployment succeeded 2h before this was filed, and .env.production.local sets ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_COREPACK. The break is specific to the @pnpm/exe artifact that pnpm's own self-installer pulls; Vercel's corepack path evidently fetches the ordinary npm tarball and is unaffected.

So this is a latent risk, not an incident: the pin names a version its own maintainers say cannot be installed, and any change to how Vercel resolves corepack would turn a green build red with an error that looks nothing like an app problem.

v2 is already insulated — v2/package.json pins pnpm@11.20.0 independently (c8bb3ea), per the island rule.

FIX: bump the root pin to a current 11.x (latest-11 was 11.20.0 on 2026-08-03) and confirm one Vercel preview build goes green before merging. Deliberately not done as a drive-by during v2 CI work, since it touches the production build of the live app.
acceptance_criteria: Root packageManager names a pnpm version that installs cleanly, proven by a green Vercel preview build and a successful pnpm install --frozen-lockfile at the repo root.

title: Close the Lemon Squeezy store once the final payout clears
description:
Last remaining step of the Lemon Squeezy decommission (split out of wordle-teams-k6a so that issue could close).

Everything else in the decommission is done: no LEMONSQUEEZY_* env var remains in any Vercel scope, all LS webhooks are deleted, @lemonsqueezy/lemonsqueezy.js is absent from package.json and the lockfile, and README.md documents Polar.

DO NOT close the store yet. Two things must clear first:
  1. The final payout must land. Closing the store early can strand funds.
  2. Subscription 370720 (owner's annual, cancelled at period end) runs to 2027-05-17.

Subscription 1676073 (the real paying customer) was cancelled at period end and ends 2026-08-05, so it is no longer a blocker.

The LS API key is no longer in Vercel but is retained in the gitignored local .env files, which is what to use for any further GET /v1/subscriptions checks against the store.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: the final Lemon Squeezy payout has cleared, subscription 370720 has ended (2027-05-17), and the store is closed in the Lemon Squeezy dashboard.

title: custom_access_token_hook is declared IMMUTABLE but reads tables
description:
public.custom_access_token_hook is declared 'immutable' while performing a SELECT against public.players and public.player_customer. Postgres defines IMMUTABLE as 'cannot modify the database and always returns the same result for the same arguments', which permits the planner to pre-evaluate or cache calls. A function that reads mutable tables should be STABLE at most.

In practice the risk is low - Supabase's auth service invokes the hook directly per token issuance rather than inside a query the planner would fold - which is presumably why it has never visibly misbehaved. But the declaration is incorrect and could produce stale membership claims.

Pre-existing since 20240313202756_custom_claims.sql and carried through every subsequent redefinition, including the Polar migration (20260731120000). That migration deliberately preserved 'immutable' rather than changing it, to keep the riskiest migration in the project scoped to exactly one concern - see wordle-teams-j8c.

Changing it is a one-word migration but alters planner behavior for the function that gates every login, so it deserves its own change with its own verification.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: the volatility is either corrected to STABLE with login verified on dev and prod, or a comment in the migration documents why IMMUTABLE is deliberate.

title: public/sw.js churns on every build, dirtying the working tree
description:
public/sw.js and public/sw.js.map are tracked build artifacts regenerated by serwist on every 'pnpm build'. The only delta between builds is a rerolled Sentry debug ID inside the minified bundle, so every build leaves ~96KB of meaningless diff in the working tree that has to be reverted by hand before committing anything unrelated.

Discovered while building for the Polar migration (wordle-teams-9he), where the artifact churn had to be discarded to keep the commit readable.

Options: gitignore them and generate at build time on Vercel; or configure the Sentry plugin to emit a stable debug ID; or leave as-is and keep reverting. Low priority - it is a papercut, not a defect.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a clean 'pnpm build' either leaves the working tree clean, or the churn is documented as intentional so future sessions stop reverting it.

title: Triage 'Error: Rejected' on /home in production
description:
Sentry 6835069821, production, 30 events / 1 user, https://wordleteams.com/home, last seen 2026-07-23.

'Error: Rejected' with no further detail is typically an unhandled promise rejection that Sentry could not resolve to a useful message — often a fetch abort, a cancelled navigation, or a rejected dynamic import. 30 events from a single user suggests a loop or a repeated retry rather than a broad problem.

Low priority on its own, but it is the last unexplained production Sentry issue and 30 events from one person on the marketing landing page is odd enough to be worth ten minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Identify the rejecting promise (check the attached session replay and breadcrumbs) and either fix it or add a proper catch so it reports with a usable message. If it is benign, resolve or ignore it in Sentry with a note explaining why.

title: /maintenance is listed in sitemap.xml — crawlers and searchers land on a maintenance page
description:
src/app/sitemap.ts includes /maintenance. In 30d prod, 16 unique IPs hit /maintenance — mostly crawlers (AhrefsBot, SeznamBot, PetalBot with referer https://wordleteams.com/sitemap.xml, Applebot, SERankingBacklinksBot) but also 3 real browsers (<redacted-ip> Safari 18.1, <redacted-ip> Chrome 129/Windows) with no referer, consistent with arriving from search results.

Maintenance mode itself was NOT on during the window — middleware.ts:6-10 only rewrites to /maintenance when the Edge Config flag maintenance_prod is true, and total traffic was normal. The page is simply publicly indexable because the sitemap advertises it. A prospective user finding 'Wordle Teams' via search and landing on a maintenance notice is a silent, permanent loss.
acceptance_criteria: Remove /maintenance from src/app/sitemap.ts and add noindex to the page. Confirm no non-bot traffic reaches /maintenance while the maintenance flag is off.

title: Fix generate-routes script stripping Register block from routeTree.gen.ts
description: Task 8 review: pnpm generate-routes (standalone tsr generate) strips the Register block incl. the startInstance config registration; the vite plugin's generator writes it back on next dev/build. Drift predates Task 8 but now more consequential. Fix or remove the script.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-03 — removed rather than fixed.

Nothing referenced the generate-routes script: no CI workflow, no docs, no other script. The vite plugin in vite.config.ts is the only generator that produces a correct routeTree.gen.ts, and it runs on every dev and build. A hand-run 'tsr generate' had no job to do except corrupt the file.

Why it mattered more than it looked: the Register block it strips contains the startInstance registration, which is what wires the Sentry global middlewares from src/start.ts. Because the vite plugin writes the block back on the next dev/build, the damage only survives if someone commits in between — a drift that appears and disappears depending on command order. It was a live suspect while diagnosing wordle-teams-7qa and cost time to rule out (it was innocent: the registration was present).

Replaced with a '//generate-routes' comment key in package.json explaining all of the above, so the script is not helpfully restored later.
close_reason: testOtps now deletes on read with an internal purge for abandoned rows, proven to leave zero rows after a full e2e run, and E2E_TEST_MODE confirmed absent from the production deployment. generate-routes removed — nothing referenced it and it corrupted the route tree the build depends on.

title: Decide whether v2 enables no-console
description:
Deferred out of wordle-teams-9lh, which added v2's ESLint setup for one substantive rule and deliberately did not import a style policy along with it.

no-console is NOT enabled. There are four call sites in the app source, all deliberate diagnostics:
  convex/auth.ts:101   console.log  - operational logging, which is how anything reaches the Convex dashboard
  convex/auth.ts:140   console.warn
  src/components/board-entry/form.tsx:146  console.error - a submission that failed before it could be saved
  src/lib/funnel.ts:48 console.debug - DEV-only, already gated on import.meta.env.DEV

scripts/ has ~55 more, where console IS the output; any rule must exempt that directory.

EVIDENCE THE AUTHOR EXPECTED THIS RULE: funnel.ts carried an 'eslint-disable-next-line no-console' directive written before any linter existed. Enabling the ESLint config surfaced it as an unused directive, and it was removed rather than have the config lie about what it enforces. If no-console is later enabled, that directive comes back.

If enabled, the likely shape is no-console with allow: ['warn', 'error', 'debug'] plus an off-override for scripts/**, which would leave only auth.ts:101 to resolve.
close_reason:
Decided and implemented: no-console is ON, scoped to src/ only, with warn and error allowed.

THE SCOPING IS THE DECISION. src/ is the only code that ships to a user's browser, so a debugging line left behind there has a real cost. In convex/ the identical call is the LOGGING API - console.log is how anything reaches the deployment log at all, and auth.ts:101 uses it deliberately to print Microsoft id_token claim KEYS (never values, per the comment beside it). In scripts/ console IS the program's output, ~55 calls. A blanket rule would have been wrong in two of the three directories, which is why the earlier config comment said the question needed deciding rather than defaulting.

warn and error stay allowed: form.tsx:146's console.error on a board submit that died before it saved is exactly the kind of failure a user should not have to open the network tab to see. debug is NOT allowed, which is what gives funnel.ts:48 its directive back - the same 'eslint-disable-next-line no-console' its author wrote before any linter existed to honour it. It is now load-bearing rather than decorative: reportUnusedDisableDirectives is an error, so lint passing proves the directive is doing work.

Verified by probe, tree restored after each: console.log and console.debug in src/ both blocked; console.warn and console.error in src/ allowed; console.log in convex/ and in scripts/ allowed. lint, typecheck, 328 unit tests, build and e2e 15/15 all exit 0.

title: The complete-profile alert's non-stickiness is not pinned by any test
description:
Found by the Phase 4 Task 8 review, 2026-08-22.

Deleting setError(null) from v2/src/routes/complete-profile.tsx - the only thing that ever clears the inline alert - leaves all four complete-profile e2e tests green (mutation N1, exit 0). A reject-then-correct block that claimed to pin this was removed, because it did not, and its stated mechanism was impossible anyway.

WHY IT IS HARD, AND WHY IT MAY NOT BE WORTH FIXING. CompleteProfilePage unmounts on await navigate({ to: '/' }), so the error state is destroyed on success regardless of whether setError(null) ran. The ONLY window in which stickiness is observable is between the submit click and the navigation, while the button reads 'Saving...'. Pinning it means holding the mutation open - page.route or a CDP delay on the Convex socket - and asserting getByRole('alert') has count 0 during that window.

Filed at P4 because the user-visible consequence is close to nil. Recorded so the absence is deliberate rather than an oversight, and so nobody adds another comment claiming coverage that a mutation test refutes.

title: Gate UpdateTeamDialog on isCreator like InvitePlayerDialog
description:
Phase 4 Task 7 gated InvitePlayerDialog on isCreator: a member was mounting a dialog they have no trigger for, plus useVisualViewport's resize/scroll listener pair.

UpdateTeamDialog at src/routes/index.tsx:186 is equally creator-only - its only trigger is the creator-gated Settings button - and is still ungated, so every non-creator mounts it and its listeners for the same no benefit. One line.

Task 7's comment currently names this inconsistency while leaving it standing, which is why it is filed rather than just noted.

title: The setScoringSystem month filter direction is unpinned by tests
description:
Found during Task 8's review (wt-ksh.4.25).

setScoringSystemFor recomputes [effectiveFrom, ...monthsWithWinners.filter(m => m > effectiveFrom)]. The filter is strictly greater-than: the edited month plus every LATER month with a winner row. Earlier months resolve to an earlier version and must be left alone.

Nothing pins the direction. A reviewer mutation-tested >= and all 208 tests still passed, because with both halves of version resolution correct, recomputing an earlier month is harmless — it resolves to the earlier version and produces the same winner. recomputeTeamMonth is idempotent and its unchanged-winner early return preserves hasSeenCelebration.

So >= would be wasted reads, not a wrong answer, and no assertion can distinguish the two. Recording it rather than leaving a silent gap: if the resolution logic is ever changed such that recomputing an earlier month is NOT a no-op, this filter becomes load-bearing with no test behind it.

Not worth a contrived test today. Worth knowing it is unpinned.
acceptance_criteria: Either a test distinguishes > from >=, or the comment records that it cannot and why.
notes: Whole-phase review: still the right call, and lower stakes than this issue implies. effectiveFrom is always the current month and monthsWithWinners only returns months that already have rows, so 'later' is empty unless someone entered a board for a future day. The recompute-every-later-month branch is effectively unreachable in production — a stronger reason than 'idempotent' for why no test can distinguish > from >=.

value: The .beads/issues.jsonl export lags bd writes, so committing it right after 'bd create' can silently omit the new issue. Caught 2026-08-22: a commit message said it filed wordle-teams-sga, but 'git show <sha>:.beads/issues.jsonl | grep -c wordle-teams-sga' returned 0 — the issue existed only in the local dolt DB, so a fresh clone would not have had the issue the next commit was named after. A later 'bd show' flushed the export and it appeared in the working tree as an uncommitted change. ALWAYS 'grep -c <id> .beads/issues.jsonl' before committing the export, and again after, rather than assuming bd create wrote through. Note 'bd dolt push' is a no-op in this repo — no Dolt remote is configured — so the tracked JSONL is the ONLY way beads state reaches anyone else.

The local anonymous Convex backend can silently serve stale code: 'convex dev' keeps retrying and codegen keeps succeeding, but a push is REFUSED outright if any existing document violates the new schema. It froze for 4 days after the creator->owner rename over 1348 teams still carrying 'creator'. tsc/vitest/build are all green while this is happening - none of them look at what is deployed. If local behaviour disagrees with the working tree, check the convex dev log for 'Schema validation failed' BEFORE theorising about anything else.

v2 e2e failing with 'Could not find public function for X:Y' is almost always a STALE LOCAL CONVEX BACKEND, not a code fault. A 'convex dev' process can keep the backend on port 3210 alive for days with a dead file watcher, so new convex/*.ts modules never get pushed and the signed-in page dies with a server error. Fix: find the pid (ss -ltnp | grep 3210, plus the parent 'convex dev' node process), kill both, then 'npx convex dev --once' to push, then restart 'convex dev'. 'convex dev' refuses to start while another backend holds the port, and the error text ('A local backend is still running') does not hint that the running one is the problem. Also: 'npx convex codegen' regenerates convex/_generated/api.d.ts WITHOUT deploying — needed after adding a convex module, because tsc fails on the missing api property and CI verifies generated types are checked in.

To flush beads state into the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl reliably, run 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl'. Do NOT assume bd create/close writes through - it does not, and 'bd show' only sometimes triggers a flush. Verified 2026-08-22: wordle-teams-px4 was created and stayed absent from the file through several bd show calls; an explicit export added it (236 -> 237 lines). Check the fresh export is a superset first (compare sorted "id": lists) before overwriting, then grep -c each new id to confirm. This matters because 'bd dolt push' is a no-op here - no Dolt remote is configured - so the tracked JSONL is the only way beads state reaches anyone else, and an issue that never lands in it does not exist for a fresh clone.

v2 replatform credentials now exist in .env.local (gitignored): CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (active; Workers Scripts+Routes Edit, but NOT Zone:DNS:Edit — /zones/{id}/dns_records 403s), SENTRY_WRITE_TOKEN (sntryu_; can create projects and read /projects/{org}/{proj}/keys/ but 403s on /organizations/*). Sentry has THREE tokens with different reach: SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN releases-only, SENTRY_READ_TOKEN reads /organizations/* but 401s on /projects/{org}/{proj}/, SENTRY_WRITE_TOKEN the inverse. wordleteams.com zone id 977da23b3a282fc32bb7cbec147894c5, status active, all records DNS-only. A wildcard *.wordleteams.com A record points at Vercel, so every subdomain including beta already resolves and returns a Vercel 404.

vercel env pull redacts secret values as the literal string [SENSITIVE] (11 chars) rather than the real value — so a token read from a pulled .env file will always fail auth. Do not conclude a production credential is invalid from this. Also: .env.production.local in this repo is STALE and pre-dates the Polar migration (it has no POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN at all, but does still hold the working LEMONSQUEEZY_API_KEY used to query the LS store).

Convex's default runtime has NO Buffer, so @polar-sh/sdk's validateEvent cannot run there. Measured 2026-08-27 on the local backend: 'ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined', from its first line Buffer.from(secret,'utf-8'). Invisible to vitest (its edge-runtime env DOES define Buffer) and to npx convex codegen (module analysis serves no request) - only a live request finds it. convex/http.ts verifies through standardwebhooks directly instead, keyed on the secret's UTF-8 bytes via { format: 'raw' }. Consequence: a verified delivery is the snake_case WIRE json, so convex/lib/polarIdentity.ts reads external_id/customer_id/checkout_id, NOT the SDK's camelCase.

Numeric claims in code comments on this repo must come from a command you ran, not from reasoning. On wt-ksh.13.5 the implementer asserted three figures from reasoning (a column width, a second corrected column width, and 'verified against every db.patch in convex/') and ALL THREE were wrong; the three figures they actually measured were all correct. The db.patch one failed because 'convex/*.ts' does not descend into subdirectories and the output was head-truncated, so the claim was broader than the command supported. Reviews caught every one. Rule: if a comment states a number or says 'verified/every/exhaustive', run the command and paste the result, or do not make the claim.

v2 login funnel goes to LogSnag, project 'wordle-teams' (same as v1, so the funnels stay comparable), channel 'login-funnel', notify off. The token is a SECRET and must never reach the browser: the client beacons to /api/funnel and the Worker forwards. LOGSNAG_TOKEN is a wrangler secret on wordle-teams-v2; ENVIRONMENT is a wrangler VAR currently 'beta' and MUST become 'production' at cutover or every prod event is mistagged. To check a deployment without a browser: curl -sI -X POST -d '{"name":"login_view"}' https://beta.wordleteams.com/api/funnel and read the x-funnel header — sent | skipped | dropped. That header exists because a bare 204 cannot distinguish delivered from silently dropped when the token is unset.

shadcn's 'radix-nova' style is BROKEN UPSTREAM (verified 2026-08-18 against ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/radix-nova/*.json): it imports Radix primitives but styles on BASE UI data attributes. Radix emits data-state="checked" / data-orientation="horizontal"; the components style on data-checked: / data-horizontal:. ~80 dead selectors across dialog, dropdown-menu, select, separator, sheet, switch, tabs, table. Build, tsc and tests all stay GREEN because Tailwind just never emits the rules — it only shows up visually (invisible Switch track, zero-height Separator). v2 uses style:'default', which is radix-native, internally consistent, and matches v1's components.json and DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 7 metrics. Do not switch to a radix-* nova/vega/etc style without re-checking this.

The wordle-teams pre-commit hook is NOT a beads stager - it is 'node scripts/check-no-pii.mjs', which blocks third-party email addresses from a PUBLIC repo. Phase 4 operated on the belief that it staged .beads/issues.jsonl and therefore committed everything with --no-verify, which skipped the PII guard for an entire phase. Verified 2026-08-22: cat .git/hooks/pre-commit is one line, the PII check. Do NOT default to --no-verify. The reason it kept getting bypassed is that it failed on 40 legitimate RFC 2606 reserved .test addresses (ada@example.test and friends) because ALLOWED_EMAILS covered example.com/org/net but not the .test TLD; that is now fixed and the tree is clean over 471 files. Note the check scans STAGED files by default and only TRACKED files under --all, so an untracked probe file will not be seen.

wordle-teams dev deployment (dev.wordleteams.com) is behind Vercel Deployment Protection (SSO) — automated curl to it 302s to vercel.com/sso-api. To validate auth flows on dev without a bypass token, reproduce the callback steps via supabase-js against the dev Supabase (sgrxuealmksermhjqepj): see scripts/validate-invite-dev.mjs. Prod Supabase ref is dcfqzbdusxhrfgvnpwqc. App logs land in Axiom dataset 'vercel' (field vercel.environment distinguishes production/preview); read via scripts/axiom-query.mjs.

A fix can be a regression: wt-ksh.13.10 added a pre-write internal.migrate.counts call on a bare top-level await in copy-from-supabase.mjs. That query does unbounded .collect()s, so a failure that previously cost only the end-of-run summary would have killed the whole copy BEFORE any write, inside the cutover's sub-one-hour window. Caught by review, fixed by wrapping it to degrade to null with an explicit 'DID NOT RUN' line. Rule: when adding a call EARLIER in a script than an existing identical call, ask what happens if it throws there - moving a query forward moves its failure mode forward too.

CORRECTS my two earlier notes about the wordle-teams pre-commit hook - both were half right and the full picture matters. core.hooksPath is .beads/hooks, so BD'S hooks are the active ones. bd's pre-commit does TWO things: it exports and stages .beads/issues.jsonl, AND it chains to .git/hooks/pre-commit, which is scripts/check-no-pii.mjs blocking third-party emails from this PUBLIC repo. So the original session premise ('a pre-commit hook stages issues.jsonl') was true - but the advice that followed it, 'commit with --no-verify', silently disabled BOTH: no beads export and no PII check, for all of Phase 4. That is the complete explanation for wordle-teams-sga never reaching the repo: it was created and then committed with --no-verify, so the export hook never ran and the issue stayed only in the local dolt DB. DO NOT USE --no-verify HERE. Commit normally and the export is staged for you. If you ever must bypass, run 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl' and 'node scripts/check-no-pii.mjs' by hand, and grep the export for each new issue id before pushing.

In @convex-dev/react-query, TanStack's 'enabled: false' does NOT gate a Convex query - it is not a security boundary. subscribeInner opens the websocket watch from the query cache's 'added' event, which TanStack fires even for a disabled query, and it never consults enabled. Only convexQuery(..., 'skip') short-circuits it: isConvexSkipped is checked before the switch and sets enabled: false itself. Measured at the websocket during Phase 4 Task 7 - under 'enabled: isCreator' a non-creator's browser sent ModifyQuerySet for teams:getTeamInvites and got a QueryFailed Transition with NOT_TEAM_CREATOR; under 'skip' it sent zero frames. Worse, the refusal NEVER reaches the console: the adapter writes it into query state via query.setState({status:'error'}), so a reviewer grepping for a red console line sees nothing. Probe the websocket frames, not the console. Applies to every access-gated query - getTeamInvites returns real email addresses.

shadcn CLI in wordle-teams/v2: 'init' is INTERACTIVE even with --yes and its prompts require a real TTY (piped stdin, piped arrow-key escapes, and a script(1) pty all failed). Bypass it — hand-author v2/components.json against https://ui.shadcn.com/schema.json, then use 'pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <c> --yes', which is fully non-interactive. Also: components.json has NO 'base' field; the base is encoded into 'style' (we use style:'radix-nova' for the radix base). Writing base:'radix' fails with 'Invalid configuration found'. And v2's import alias is #/ (tsconfig '#/*' -> './src/*'), not shadcn's default @/.

Run the shadcn CLI from INSIDE v2/, never the wordle-teams repo root. From the root it misdetects the project as v1 (Next.js 15.4.10, Tailwind v3, rsc true) and resolves tailwindCss to docs/design-system/globals.v2.css — the handoff reference file, not a real stylesheet — so init would write config against the wrong app and the wrong CSS. v2 is TanStack Start + Vite + Tailwind v4 + React 19, pnpm@11.20.0, so: cd v2 && pnpm dlx shadcn@latest.

The Claude Design bundle's contrast numbers are unreliable — verified 2026-08-18 with a checker exact against six published WCAG reference pairs. MIGRATION.md's table disagrees with the bundle's OWN hex values on 5 of 7 pairs in light and 6 of 7 in dark. Worst case, DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 10 calls v1's success badge a '~2.1:1' AA failure: near-black #111113 on green-600 #16a34a is really 5.72:1 and PASSES, while the prescribed fix (white on #16a34a) is 3.30:1 and FAILS. Never take a contrast claim from that bundle at face value — recompute. v2's tokens now deviate from tokens.json on four values for this reason (success/accent-solid light -> #15803d, text-subtle light -> #767680, danger dark -> #dc2626), all documented in v2/src/styles.css.

Always screenshot v2 UI work before calling it done. wt-ksh.12.5 shipped a completely invisible Switch and a zero-height Separator with vite build, tsc --noEmit and the full vitest suite all passing — Tailwind silently emits nothing for a selector that never matches, so broken component styling is invisible to the toolchain. Use the project's own Playwright chromium (node script importing @playwright/test from inside v2/); the MCP browser tool fails with 'Chromium distribution chrome is not found'. Kill stray dev servers by port first (lsof -ti :3000) — a second 'pnpm dev' silently binds 3001/3002 and you end up screenshotting a stale server.

Microsoft/Entra in v2 needed two non-obvious fixes, both of which would have broken users at cutover rather than in beta. (1) better-auth's default scope list includes User.Read, a Microsoft GRAPH permission that becomes an admin-consent gate in tenants restricting consent; v1 asked only for email+offline_access. Removed via disableDefaultScope + explicit scope. Nothing needs Graph — every claim read comes from the ID TOKEN; User.Read bought only the profile photo. (2) better-auth defaults emailVerified to FALSE when Microsoft omits the claim, and a false REFUSES the sign-in with account_not_linked rather than creating a duplicate. Microsoft does not reliably emit email_verified or the verified_*_email arrays. Fixed with mapProfileToUser accepting xms_edov (Microsoft's own 'email domain owner verified' signal) and the fixed CONSUMER tenant id 9188040d-6c67-4c5b-b112-36a304b66dad. Also: AADSTS900971 'No reply address provided' means a PLATFORM mismatch (URI registered under SPA instead of Web), not a URI typo.

Never run two review subagents in parallel when either might mutation-test. Task 5's spec and quality reviewers ran concurrently; the spec reviewer's harness mutated the live working tree while the quality reviewer was reading it, and the quality reviewer observed teams.test.ts spontaneously revert to the plan's draft assertions and back mid-review. It defended itself by extracting 'git archive <sha>:v2' into the scratchpad with node_modules symlinked - that is the pattern to mandate. The commit survived (git diff vs the sha was empty), but a restore that raced a concurrent read could have silently corrupted a verdict. Either serialise the reviewers or require every mutation harness to work in an isolated extraction.

A commit can falsify a comment it writes in the SAME commit. Phase 5 Task 8 wrote billing.ts's 'the first two are claimed by completeProfileFor' and then, forty lines away in players.ts, capped completeProfileFor so it leaves a surplus parked. It also changed InviteOutcome's 'v1 reports all of them' to 'four of them' while the parenthetical two lines below said the fifth is reported as a success too - and left invite-player-dialog.tsx still saying 'all of them'.

Both survived four green gates: comments are invisible to lint, tsc, vitest and build.

So the sweep for comments a change falsifies must include the comments that change WRITES, not just the ones it finds - and it must cross module boundaries, because the falsifying edit was in a different file from the false sentence. Cheapest catch: after the last edit, re-read every prose paragraph the diff touched as if the diff were already merged. Task 8's own commit message claimed 'comments that this makes false are fixed with it' while shipping two that were not.

Allowlist lookups keyed by untrusted input must not use a plain object literal. In v2's funnel-payload.ts, EVENTS['__proto__'] resolved up the prototype chain to Object.prototype — truthy — so the allowlist check passed for a name that was never allowed and emitted an event with an undefined name. Caught by a unit test on 2026-08-18. Use a Map (or Object.create(null) / Object.hasOwn). Applies anywhere a public endpoint looks up user-supplied keys.

Convex CLI in wordle-teams/v2: v2/.env.local pins CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT=anonymous:anonymous-v2, which SILENTLY WINS over a CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY passed in the environment — 'convex env list' with a prod key still read the local anonymous deployment and looked plausible. Always pass --env-file pointing at a file containing ONLY the deploy key; the CLI then prints '(on prod deployment <name>)' so the target is unambiguous. Deployments: prod fabulous-goldfish-949, dev jovial-koala-428. Deploy keys must contain a '|' (prod:name|key) — a key without one is rejected with 'Please set CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY to a new key', per node_modules/convex/src/cli/lib/deployment.ts:189.

docs/design-system/ (the Claude Design export) targets v1, NOT v2, despite its README saying 'for the v2 replatform'. 'v1 -> v2' there means token-set version 1 -> version 2 applied in place to the Next.js app on main. globals.v2.css is Tailwind 3 and is described as a drop-in for src/app/globals.css; tailwind.tokens.ts needs a tailwind.config.ts; the Layer 3 alias block exists so v1's src/components/ui/* compiles unchanged; MIGRATION.md phases 2-4 name only v1 files. Do NOT run MIGRATION.md against v2. Use DESIGN_SYSTEM.md as the spec and tokens.json's v2 block as values, translated to Tailwind v4. The original export files stay unmodified as the diff baseline for future Claude Design revisions.

v2 OAuth callback URLs: better-auth uses https://<site>/api/auth/callback/<providerId> — NO version segment, provider id ON THE END. Supabase/v1 used https://<ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback — version segment, NO provider segment. Mixing the two shapes cost most of a day across four consoles on 2026-08-17/18 (missing /<provider>, then missing /api, then an inherited /v1). Provider ids: google, microsoft (NOT 'azure' — that is the v1/Supabase name), github, discord. Verify with 'node v2/scripts/check-oauth-callbacks.mjs [baseUrl]'. CRITICAL LIMIT: only Google validates redirect_uri BEFORE login, so only Google can be proven by that script; microsoft/github/discord validate AFTER authenticating and the script reports them UNVERIFIED. A provider reaching its login screen proves nothing about the callback.
